title: Thermodynamics Of Speed And Efficiency With Quantum Feedback
authors: Yue Liu, Ryotaro Honma, Ruicheng Bao, Tan van Vu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rapid thermodynamic operations generally entail irreversible dissipation, giving rise to trade-offs between operating speed and thermodynamic cost. Yet, how quantum feedback fundamentally reshapes these trade-offs remains elusive. Here, we derive a finite-time current--dissipation relation for continuously monitored open quantum dynamics with jump feedback. From this fundamental relation, we establish a quantum speed limit and a power-efficiency trade-off for stationary information engines, identifying how feedback affects state transformations and the performance of engines through both informational entropy and direct dynamical contributions. Our results provide a quantitative foundation for fast, low-dissipation quantum thermodynamics in the presence of feedback control, exemplified by attaining the generalized Landauer bound in finite-time information erasure and approaching unit information efficiency at finite power in the large-system limit of a collective engine.
tldr: The paper derives finite-time thermodynamic trade-offs for continuously monitored open quantum systems with jump feedback, including a quantum speed limit and a power-efficiency bound for information engines.
motivation: Fast thermodynamic operations incur dissipation, and how quantum feedback reshapes speed-cost and power-efficiency trade-offs is not well understood.
method: The authors establish a finite-time current-dissipation relation for continuously monitored open quantum dynamics with jump feedback, then use it to derive a quantum speed limit and a power-efficiency trade-off for stationary information engines.
result: The analysis separates informational-entropy and direct dynamical contributions of feedback, yields a generalized finite-time Landauer bound for information erasure, and shows unit information efficiency at finite power in the large-system limit of a collective engine.
conclusion: The work provides a quantitative foundation for fast, low-dissipation quantum thermodynamics under feedback control and clarifies how feedback affects state transformations and engine performance.

title: Optimal Asymptotic Pure-state Conversion Under Thermal Operations
authors: Naoto Shiraishi Tatsuya Yamanouchi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum thermodynamics seeks to characterize possible state transformations under thermodynamic constraints in microscopic quantum systems. In the fully quantum regime, however, quantum coherence imposes various restrictions on state conversions, and a complete characterization of state convertibility has remained open. Here we resolve this problem for asymptotic conversions between pure states. Specifically, we show that asymptotic convertibility is fully determined by the free-energy and energy-variance ratios. Our result reveals how genuinely quantum effects quantitatively constrain state conversions in quantum thermodynamics.
tldr: The paper fully characterizes asymptotic convertibility between pure quantum states under thermal operations, showing it is determined by free-energy and energy-variance ratios.
motivation: Quantum thermodynamics aims to characterize which state transformations are possible under thermodynamic constraints, but in the fully quantum regime coherence imposes restrictions that have prevented a complete characterization of state convertibility.
method: The authors analyze asymptotic conversions between pure states under thermal operations, deriving necessary and sufficient conditions expressed through ratios of free energy and energy variance.
result: Asymptotic pure-state convertibility under thermal operations is shown to be completely determined by the free-energy ratio and the energy-variance ratio, quantifying how genuinely quantum coherence effects constrain conversions.
conclusion: The work closes a key open problem in quantum thermodynamics by providing an exact asymptotic characterization of pure-state conversions, clarifying the quantitative role of quantum effects in thermodynamic state transformations.

The authors show that asymptotic convertibility is completely determined by two ratios: the free-energy ratio and the energy-variance ratio. This result provides a quantitative link between genuinely quantum effects (coherence) and the restrictions they impose on state transformations in quantum thermodynamics. The work resolves a long-standing question by demonstrating that, in the asymptotic limit, the interplay between free energy and energy variance fully captures the feasibility of converting one pure state to another. The paper is theoretical, spanning 6+23 pages with 2 figures, and likely employs resource-theoretic and information-theoretic techniques to derive the necessary and sufficient conditions for asymptotic conversions.

title: Harnessing Dimensional Leakage For Continuous-variable Randomness Certification
authors: Mois\'es Alves, Tailan S. Sarubi, Vitor L. Sena, Alexandre B. Tacla, Rafael Chaves
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semi-device-independent quantum protocols often rely on strict Hilbert-space dimension assumptions that are difficult to satisfy in realistic implementations, particularly with infinite-dimensional optical fields. The almost-qudit framework addresses this issue by quantifying the leakage of quantum states beyond a target subspace. Although such leakage can severely compromise randomness certification for fixed preparation and measurement inputs, we show that averaging over the full input ensemble can mitigate this vulnerability and extend the range of tolerable leakage. This enhanced robustness enables nonzero randomness certification using low-squeezing single-mode Gaussian states and homodyne detection, thus offering an experimentally accessible continuous-variable implementation.
tldr: The paper shows that input-ensemble averaging can make semi-device-independent continuous-variable randomness certification robust to Hilbert-space dimensional leakage.
motivation: Semi-device-independent protocols often assume strict finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, which are difficult to justify for infinite-dimensional optical fields; dimensional leakage can severely compromise randomness certification.
method: The authors use the almost-qudit framework to quantify leakage beyond a target subspace and analyze randomness certification when averaging over the full input ensemble, focusing on low-squeezing single-mode Gaussian states and homodyne detection.
result: Averaging over the input ensemble mitigates the vulnerability to leakage, extends the range of tolerable leakage, and enables nonzero randomness certification in an experimentally accessible continuous-variable setup.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to continuous-variable semi-device-independent randomness certification that is more robust to realistic dimensional imperfections.

The work bridges theory and experiment by demonstrating that SDI protocols can be made more resilient to dimension leakage through ensemble averaging, and it offers a practical path for CV quantum randomness generation.

title: Interaction-enabled Charging And Thermal Crossover Of The Spin-work Deficit In A Hubbard Double Quantum Dot
authors: Khalil Loukhssami, Cheng Shang, Morad El Baz, Khadija El Hawary
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how conservation of total spin affects the extractable work of an interacting Hubbard double quantum dot charged in the presence of unresolved quasistatic detuning fluctuations. The full fermionic Fock space is used to model preparation through electronic reservoirs, whereas the additional work deficit associated with spin conservation arises entirely from the singlet and triplet states at half filling. At zero detuning, modulation of the symmetric tunnel barrier couples two singlets of even parity. The corresponding transition matrix element vanishes when U = V . An exact formula for the additional work deficit follows from passive spectral rearrangement under two extraction constraints: conservation of particle number alone and conservation of both particle number and total spin. At low temperature, an expansion in the detuning response gives a leading estimate of the noise amplitude at which this deficit first appears. Increasing the preparation temperature changes the triplet population and produces a crossover at s2 = q, where the additional spin constraint becomes nonbinding for the averaged state, even though both ergotropies may continue to decrease. We obtain a semi-analytic expression for this crossover by separating the thermal Gibbs weights from the singlet dynamics under a fixed charging pulse. Averaging over symmetric detuning disorder also restores parity in the density matrix and allows singlet eigenvalues of different parity to exchange order, changing the branch that determines the thermal boundary. The work values are optimal over specified classes of unitary operations and do not establish the yield of a finite discharge protocol.
tldr: The paper analyzes how total-spin conservation and detuning disorder modify the extractable work, or ergotropy, of an interacting Hubbard double quantum dot during charging.
motivation: It aims to quantify an additional work deficit that arises from spin conservation beyond the usual particle-number constraint in a quantum dot charging process.
method: The authors use the full fermionic Fock space, focusing on singlet and triplet states at half filling, and derive exact and semi-analytic expressions via passive spectral rearrangement under particle-number and spin-conservation constraints.
result: They find that the relevant transition matrix element vanishes at U = V, obtain a low-temperature estimate for the noise amplitude where the spin-work deficit appears, and identify a thermal crossover at s2 = q where the spin constraint becomes nonbinding.
conclusion: The work clarifies how interactions, spin conservation, and thermal preparation control work extraction in a double quantum dot, while noting that the results do not establish the yield of a finite discharge protocol.

At zero detuning, modulation of the symmetric tunnel barrier couples two even-parity singlet states, and the transition matrix element vanishes when the on-site interaction U equals the interdot Coulomb interaction V. An exact formula for the additional work deficit is derived from passive spectral rearrangement under the two constraints. In the low-temperature limit, an expansion in the detuning response yields a leading estimate of the noise amplitude at which the deficit first appears. The authors also examine the effect of preparation temperature: increasing it changes the triplet population and produces a crossover at s2 = q, where the additional spin constraint becomes nonbinding for the averaged state, even though both ergotropies may continue to decrease. A semi-analytic expression for this crossover is obtained by separating thermal Gibbs weights from the singlet dynamics under a fixed charging pulse. Averaging over symmetric detuning disorder restores parity in the density matrix and allows singlet eigenvalues of different parity to exchange order, thereby changing the branch that determines the thermal boundary. The work values are optimal over specified classes of unitary operations and do not establish the yield of a finite discharge protocol.

title: Parametric $\mathrm{CZ}$ Gates In A Tunable Tripod Architecture With Fixed-Frequency Superconducting Qubits
authors: Chanpyo Kim, Hansol Kim, Jeongsoo Kang, Younghun Kwon
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient implementation of the operations required for quantum error correction in superconducting quantum computers requires high gate fidelity, adequate qubit connectivity, and selective control of interactions. Sharing a single coupler among multiple qubits can improve connectivity, but also requires accounting for its effects on qubits outside the target pair. In this work, we numerically investigate the feasibility of implementing parametric-resonance [MATH] gates in a tunable tripod structure consisting of three fixed-frequency transmon qubits connected to a single tunable coupler. We modulate the external flux applied to the coupler and optimize the pulse parameters for each qubit pair to construct [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH] gates. We calculate the time evolution of a Hamiltonian that includes three energy levels for each circuit element and evaluate gate fidelity and leakage after virtual Z correction. The fidelities obtained for the target-pair computational blocks, whose input and output basis states have both the coupler and spectator qubit in their ground states, are 0.9943, 0.9834, and 0.9907, respectively. We also find that population preservation at the end of the gate depends on the initial state of the spectator qubit. These results demonstrate the possibility of constructing [MATH] operations for each qubit pair through flux modulation of a shared coupler while maintaining fixed data-qubit frequencies. They also highlight the need to evaluate performance and optimize control over the full computational space, including the spectator qubit.
tldr: Numerically demonstrates parametric CZ gates in a tunable tripod architecture with three fixed-frequency transmon qubits coupled to a shared tunable coupler.
motivation: Superconducting quantum processors require high-fidelity entangling gates with sufficient connectivity and selective control; sharing a coupler among multiple qubits can improve connectivity but introduces spectator-qubit effects.
method: The authors modulate the coupler flux and optimize pulse parameters for each qubit pair, simulating a three-level Hamiltonian for each circuit element and evaluating fidelity and leakage after virtual Z correction.
result: Target-pair computational-block fidelities of 0.9943, 0.9834, and 0.9907 are obtained for the three CZ gates, while spectator-qubit population preservation is found to depend on its initial state.
conclusion: The results support the feasibility of parametric CZ operations via a shared tunable coupler while keeping data-qubit frequencies fixed, and highlight the need to optimize control over the full computational space including spectator qubits.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper numerically investigates the feasibility of implementing parametric-resonance CZ gates in a tunable tripod architecture comprising three fixed-frequency transmon qubits coupled to a single tunable coupler. The authors modulate the external flux on the coupler to activate effective qubit-qubit interactions and optimize pulse parameters for each pair, constructing CZ gates between qubits 0-1, 0-2, and 1-2. The Hamiltonian includes three energy levels per circuit element, and they simulate time evolution to evaluate gate fidelity and leakage after virtual Z corrections. For target-pair computational blocks (with coupler and spectator qubit in ground states), fidelities of 0.9943, 0.9834, and 0.9907 are obtained for CZ01, CZ02, and CZ12, respectively. The study also finds that population preservation at the end of the gate depends on the spectator qubit's initial state, highlighting the need to consider the full computational space including the spectator. Overall, the results demonstrate the possibility of constructing CZ operations for each qubit pair via flux modulation of a shared coupler while maintaining fixed data-qubit frequencies, and underscore the importance of optimizing control over the entire system to mitigate spectator effects.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ numerical simulation of a time-dependent Hamiltonian that includes three energy levels for each circuit element (three transmon qubits and one tunable coupler). They modulate the external flux applied to the coupler to induce parametric resonance conditions that enable effective CZ interactions between selected qubit pairs. For each pair, they optimize the pulse parameters (likely amplitude and duration) to maximize gate fidelity while minimizing leakage to non-computational states. Gate fidelity is evaluated after applying virtual Z corrections, which account for single-qubit phase shifts. The simulation considers the full system including the spectator qubit, allowing assessment of spectator-induced errors. The methodology is sound for a numerical feasibility study, but it relies on a simplified three-level model per element and does not include noise or decoherence effects, which are critical for experimental implementation.

The results are limited to numerical simulations without noise, so experimental fidelities would likely be lower.

title: Magic Is In The Eye Of The Measure
authors: Zhi-Heng Shen, Zhewei Yin, Hao-Lin Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magic, or nonstabilizerness, is the quantum resource behind universal quantum computation. Its applications in high-energy and nuclear physics rely almost exclusively on the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy (SRE), although magic has no unique measure. For two qubits, we compare the SRE with three measures defined through optimizations over stabilizer states: the min- and max-relative entropies of magic and the logarithmic free robustness. We determine the maximal-magic states of all four measures, with exact proofs, and find that they depend on the measure. In the determination of the weak mixing angle from minimal magic in M{\o}ller scattering, the min-relative entropy gives an energy-dependent value that differs from that of the SRE, whereas the max-relative entropy and the logarithmic free robustness give [MATH] at all energies. We trace this difference to the non-analytic structure of the optimization-based measures. Physical conclusions drawn from extremizing magic can thus depend on the measure.

method: For two qubits, the authors compare SRE with min- and max-relative entropies of magic and logarithmic free robustness, determine maximal-magic states with exact proofs, and apply the measures to the weak mixing angle from minimal magic in Møller scattering.

conclusion: Physical conclusions drawn from extremizing magic can depend on the measure, traced to the non-analytic structure of optimization-based measures.

title: Nonequilibrium Fluctuations And Intrinsic Stability Of Nanostructured Solar Cells: Microscopic Derivation And Universal Laws
authors: Rivo Herivola Manjakamanana Ravelonjato, Ravo Tokiniaina Ranaivoson, Philipe Manjakasoa Randriantsoa, Raoelina Andriambololona, Wilfrid Chrysante Solofoarisina
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study nonequilibrium fluctuations of efficiency in nanostructured solar cells. Our contribution is threefold. First, we derive a microscopic stochastic model of efficiency from a two-state master equation describing absorption, radiative recombination, and extraction. This derivation establishes an explicit link between efficiency fluctuations and entropy production, and justifies the thermodynamic affinity through local detailed balance. Second, we review universal fluctuation laws established in the recent literature and apply them for the first time to the real parameters of nanostructured solar cells. We show that the total entropy production behaves as a submartingale, and that its negative exponential is a martingale. For a biased discrete random walk, the exact infimum law is verified numerically in the near-equilibrium regime, then applied to realistic solar cell configurations. Third, our simulations show that nanostructured solar cells operate in a strongly nonequilibrium regime, where negative entropy fluctuations, and hence efficiency fluctuations, are exponentially rare. Over all simulated trajectories, most configurations show no detectable negative fluctuation, consistent with the theoretical prediction. These results explain the intrinsic statistical stability of the devices and provide a conceptual and quantitative framework for understanding efficiency fluctuations around the mean values. They do not modify the mean efficiencies obtained previously, but clarify their statistical robustness in the strongly nonequilibrium regime.

result: They show entropy production behaves as a submartingale and its negative exponential as a martingale, verify the exact infimum law near equilibrium, and find that negative entropy/efficiency fluctuations are exponentially rare in the strongly nonequilibrium operating regime.
conclusion: The framework explains the intrinsic statistical stability of nanostructured solar cells and clarifies the robustness of mean efficiency predictions without modifying them.

title: What Are Local Complementations, Really?
authors: Kenneth Goodenough
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A local complementation at a vertex [MATH] of a graph [MATH] replaces the induced neighborhood of [MATH] with its complement. Local complementations are, at face value, peculiar operations. Yet they famously show up when describing the local Clifford equivalence among graph states, and, because of this, have become a fundamental notion in the study of graph states. Following Bouchet, we show here how local complementations on graphs are more naturally thought of in terms of switchings of (matroid) bases of stabilizer states. Bases and switchings reveal structural properties of stabilizer states that are harder to glean from the graph-theoretic description alone, such as vertex-minors and statistics of local Pauli measurements. Bases also simplify prior proofs about graphs up to local complementations, of which we give several examples. Bases are foundational in the study of (multi)matroids; as such this paper serves as a gentle introduction to the applications of multimatroids to quantum information theory.
tldr: This paper reinterprets local complementations on graphs as switchings of matroid bases of stabilizer states, offering a multimatroid-based framework for understanding graph states and local Clifford equivalence.
motivation: Local complementations are central to graph-state theory and local Clifford operations but appear ad hoc from a graph-theoretic perspective. The work aims to provide a more natural structural foundation via matroid and multimatroid theory.
method: Following Bouchet, the paper formulates local complementations as basis switchings for stabilizer states and uses multimatroids to derive structural properties and simplify existing proofs.
result: The basis-switching perspective clarifies vertex-minors, local Pauli measurement statistics, and local Clifford equivalence of graph states, while yielding simpler proofs of prior graph-theoretic results.
conclusion: The paper serves as an accessible introduction to multimatroids in quantum information and demonstrates their utility for structural questions about stabilizer and graph states.

title: Kinetic Cluster Embedding For Qubit Decoherence In Dissipative Spin Baths
authors: Xiaofei Yu, Jonah Nagura, Stella Wang, Evan J. Villafranca, Peter C. Maurer, Giulia Galli
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interpreting the decoherence of a spin qubit requires knowing how the surrounding bath spins behave: whether they fluctuate independently, exchange polarization incoherently, or evolve as coherent groups. These processes can yield the same Hahn-echo coherence time yet produce different coherence signals under pulse control of the qubit. Existing theoretical approaches either capture bath correlations at a cost that grows combinatorially with spin-bath cluster size or neglect polarization transport altogether. We introduce kinetic cluster embedding (KCE), which uses a single dimensionless parameter, comparing the flip-flop coupling of a spin pair with its detuning and linewidth, to decide how each pair must be treated. Pairs that can complete an appreciable exchange oscillation are propagated with the full dissipative quantum dynamics. All other spins are treated as random-telegraph fluctuators coupled through a kinetic network of polarization-transfer rates. We show that for nitrogen-vacancy centers coupled to surface electron spins, KCE propagates about 7 four-spin clusters, compared to more than 10[MATH] propagated by fourth-order master-equation cluster-correlation (ME-CCE4); nevertheless it reproduces ME-CCE4 coherence times to within 15[MATH] for dipolar couplings of order [MATH] times the bath relaxation rate. For a three-dimensional P1 bath, the agreement is within 16[MATH]. Coherent multispin clusters emerge as the leading correction to independent fluctuators, and they leave a distinct signature in the CPMG response. Importantly, we find that whether a rate description suffices is set not by coupling strength alone but by whether a pair can exchange polarization coherently before detuning and damping suppress it.
tldr: Introduces kinetic cluster embedding to model spin-qubit decoherence by treating strongly exchanging spin pairs coherently and the remaining bath spins as kinetic fluctuators.
motivation: Interpreting decoherence of a spin qubit requires distinguishing independent bath fluctuations, incoherent polarization exchange, and coherent multispin groups, which existing methods capture either inefficiently or not at all.
method: KCE uses a dimensionless ratio of flip-flop coupling to detuning and linewidth to decide whether each spin pair is propagated with full dissipative quantum dynamics or treated as random-telegraph fluctuators coupled through a kinetic polarization-transfer network.
result: For NV centers coupled to surface electron spins and a three-dimensional P1 bath, KCE reproduces ME-CCE4 coherence times within about 15–16% while propagating far fewer four-spin clusters, and it identifies a distinct CPMG signature of coherent multispin clusters.
conclusion: Coherent multispin clusters are the leading correction to independent fluctuators, and whether a rate description suffices depends on whether a pair can exchange polarization coherently before detuning and damping suppress it, not on coupling strength alone.

This adaptive scheme avoids the combinatorial explosion of cluster-correlation expansion (CCE) while retaining the essential physics of polarization transport. The authors benchmark KCE against fourth-order master-equation CCE (ME-CCE4) for two systems: nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers coupled to surface electron spins and a three-dimensional P1 bath. For the NV-surface spin system, KCE propagates only about 7 four-spin clusters, compared to over 10^5 for ME-CCE4, yet reproduces coherence times to within 15% for dipolar couplings of order 10^2 times the bath relaxation rate. For the P1 bath, agreement is within 16%. The paper further shows that coherent multispin clusters emerge as the leading correction to independent fluctuators and leave a distinct signature in the CPMG response. Crucially, the authors find that whether a rate description suffices is determined not by coupling strength alone but by whether a pair can exchange polarization coherently before detuning and damping suppress it.

The decision between these treatments is governed by a dimensionless parameter that compares the flip-flop coupling strength to the detuning and linewidth of the pair. This parameter effectively measures whether a pair can complete an appreciable exchange oscillation before decoherence suppresses it. The method is benchmarked against ME-CCE4, a well-established but computationally expensive technique that propagates all clusters up to fourth order. The authors apply KCE to two physically relevant systems: NV centers in diamond coupled to surface electron spins (a quasi-2D bath) and a 3D bath of P1 centers. They compute Hahn-echo and CPMG coherence signals and compare them to ME-CCE4 results, analyzing both the coherence times and the shape of the decay curves. title: Random Encoders And Expurgation Improve 1,873 Entries Of The Grassl Qubit Code Tables
authors: Marin Girard
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I report 192 explicit binary stabilizer codes [MATH] with [MATH] and [MATH] whose minimum distance exceeds the lower bound listed in Grassl's code tables at the same [MATH]: 161 codes by one and 31 by two. For 190 of the codes, a random Clifford encoder is followed by expurgation: every logical operator of weight below the target distance is enumerated, and a few logical operators are promoted to stabilizers so that each low-weight one anticommutes with at least one of them. The other two are obtained by puncturing a code from the table and repairing it in the same way. All 192 distances are exact: the lower bound is certified by exhaustive meet-in-the-middle enumeration of up to [MATH] Pauli operators, and the upper bound by an explicit logical operator of weight [MATH]. A first-moment count explains the results. Expurgated random codes have about eight more logical qubits than a typical random code of the same length and distance, so they beat the table wherever its best known codes are no better than random. The largest gains, up to nine logical qubits, are at [MATH] and [MATH], where the table often gives a lower bound without an explicit code. title: A Tutorial On Practical Qkd Post-Processing Algorithms Using A GUI-Based Simulation Framework
authors: Ushnik Nath, Neha Sharma, Ramniwas Meena, Neel Kanth Kundu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent experimental demonstrations of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) have attracted significant attention for their ability to establish information-theoretically secure encryption keys for next-generation communication systems. As practical deployment accelerates, the realization of compact, scalable, and high-throughput discrete-variable (DV) QKD systems has become increasingly important. While advances in photonic integration are enabling low-size, low-weight, and low-power QKD hardware, the security and performance of these systems rely heavily on efficient post-processing techniques to generate identical, secure keys. This tutorial presents a comprehensive algorithm-level review of practical post-processing techniques for DV-QKD, with particular emphasis on information reconciliation methods based on Cascade, Winnow, low-density parity-check (LDPC), and polar codes. We also analyze the theoretical asymptotic and finite-size secret key rates (SKRs) of DV-QKD and benchmark these bounds against the practical SKRs achieved using actual post-processing algorithms. Furthermore, we present a server-client model to implement the entire QKD post-processing pipeline. The performance is evaluated in terms of QBER and SKR across various system parameters, considering the complete post-processing pipeline, including sifting, information reconciliation, privacy amplification, and authentication. This tutorial also presents a graphical user interface (GUI) for the QKD post-processing methods, enabling researchers, industry practitioners, and academic users to visualize and analyze the impact of different post-processing techniques and system parameters, such as QBER, on the SKR performance of DV-QKD systems.

result: It benchmarks theoretical secret-key-rate bounds against practical rates achieved by actual post-processing algorithms across QBER and system parameters, evaluating the complete pipeline including sifting, reconciliation, privacy amplification, and authentication.
conclusion: The tutorial provides a practical framework for understanding and simulating DV-QKD post-processing, enabling users to analyze how algorithm choices and system parameters affect secret-key-rate performance.

title: Time- And Phase-resolved Emulation Of Sign-selective Counterdiabatic Dynamics In A Superconducting Qutrit
authors: Yiwen Li, Luojia Xu, Xinsheng Tan, Yang Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In cyclic three-level systems, phase-sensitive interference can convert a coupling-sign reversal into a population contrast, providing a controllable analogue of handedness. We emulate this mechanism in a superconducting transmon qutrit using two resonant single-photon drives and a phase-controlled effective two-photon drive. Effective loop phases \(\Phi_L=+\pi/2\) and \(\Phi_R=-\pi/2\), separated by \(\pi\), reverse the auxiliary contribution to the dark--bright coupling, canceling the intrinsic nonadiabatic term for \(L\) and reinforcing it for \(R\). Time-resolved trajectories reveal dark-pathway transfer for \(L\) and bright-manifold participation for \(R\). Measured late-time averages give a target-state population contrast of 0.929. Loop-phase measurements establish phase selectivity, while pulse-area and common-mode amplitude scans characterize the operating regime and control sensitivity. These results provide direct time- and phase-domain access to sign-selective counterdiabatic interference in a programmable cyclic qutrit.
tldr: The paper experimentally emulates sign-selective counterdiabatic dynamics in a superconducting transmon qutrit using phase-controlled microwave drives.
motivation: Cyclic three-level systems can exhibit phase-sensitive interference that converts coupling-sign reversal into population contrast, offering a controllable analogue of handedness. The authors aim to realize and time-resolve this mechanism in a programmable superconducting platform.
method: Two resonant single-photon drives and a phase-controlled effective two-photon drive are applied to a transmon qutrit to engineer effective loop phases of +π/2 and -π/2, reversing the auxiliary contribution to the dark-bright coupling. Time-resolved trajectories and phase/amplitude scans characterize the dynamics.
result: The emulation yields a target-state population contrast of 0.929, with dark-pathway transfer for one loop phase and bright-manifold participation for the other. Loop-phase measurements confirm phase selectivity, and pulse-area/common-mode scans map the operating regime.
conclusion: The work provides direct time- and phase-domain access to sign-selective counterdiabatic interference in a superconducting qutrit, demonstrating a programmable platform for emulating phase-sensitive three-level dynamics.

title: Single-photon Scattering By A Nanofiber-coupled Atomic Chain: Beyond Independent Radiation
authors: \'etienne Brion Juliette Jim\'enez-Jaimes
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study single-photon scattering by a nanofiber-coupled atomic chain, comparing a full microscopic model with an independent-radiation approximation. We show that nearly equal transmission probabilities can coexist with substantially different transmitted temporal modes, even after adjusting their relative delay. For a reference chain, a decomposition into collective atomic resonances relates this discrepancy mainly to spectral-phase changes caused by the omitted interatomic couplings. Parameter scans delimit this phase-dominated regime, and controlled comparisons separate the effects of coherent exchange and collective decay.
tldr: A microscopic model of single-photon scattering by a nanofiber-coupled atomic chain shows that matching transmission probabilities can hide substantially different transmitted temporal modes due to interatomic couplings.
motivation: The independent-radiation approximation is commonly used for atom-nanofiber systems, but its validity for temporal-mode-sensitive single-photon scattering is unclear.
method: The authors compare a full microscopic model with an independent-radiation approximation, decompose the response into collective atomic resonances, and perform parameter scans and controlled comparisons to isolate coherent exchange and collective decay.
result: Nearly equal transmission probabilities can coexist with different transmitted temporal modes even after delay adjustment, with the discrepancy dominated by spectral-phase changes from omitted interatomic couplings.
conclusion: Independent-radiation treatments can be insufficient for nanofiber-coupled atomic chains when temporal mode structure matters, and collective interatomic couplings must be retained for accurate scattering predictions.

title: Local Distinguishability Of Five Five-partite Orthogonal Product States
authors: Guang-Bao Xu, Jie Zhan, Yu-Guang Yang, Dong-Huan Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The local distinguishability of five orthogonal product states (OPSs) has been studied in several multipartite settings, but the five-partite case still requires a systematic characterization. In this paper, we consider five five-partite OPSs, where any two states are orthogonal on exactly one subsystem. By analyzing the distribution of ten pairwise orthogonality relations over five subsystems, we classify the corresponding orthogonality structures by colored orthogonality graphs. After eliminating identical graphs under relabeling of states and permutation of subsystems, we obtain 443 different graphs in seven genuinely five-partite categories. We prove that the OPSs corresponding to 434 of these graphs can be perfectly distinguished by local operations and classical communication (LOCC), while the remaining 9 exceptional cases fall into two types and require separate analysis. Our results give a characterization of the local distinguishability of five OPSs in five-partite OPSs.
tldr: The paper classifies the orthogonality structures of five five-partite orthogonal product states using colored graphs and determines their LOCC distinguishability across 443 cases.
motivation: Local distinguishability of orthogonal product states is a key manifestation of nonlocality without entanglement and is relevant to multipartite quantum information protocols.
method: The authors encode the ten pairwise orthogonality relations as colored orthogonality graphs, eliminate equivalent graphs under state relabeling and subsystem permutation, classify them into seven genuinely five-partite categories, and analyze LOCC distinguishability for each graph class.
result: They find 443 distinct graphs, show that 434 corresponding OPS sets are perfectly distinguishable by LOCC, and identify 9 exceptional cases falling into two types that require separate analysis.
conclusion: This provides a systematic characterization of local distinguishability for five five-partite OPSs, extending known multipartite results and highlighting exceptional non-LOCC-distinguishable structures.

By considering all possible distributions of the ten pairwise orthogonality relations over five subsystems, they enumerate all colored graphs, then eliminate duplicates under relabeling of states and permutation of subsystems. This yields 443 distinct graphs, which are further classified into seven genuinely five-partite categories. The main result is that for 434 of these graphs, the corresponding OPSs can be perfectly distinguished by local operations and classical communication (LOCC), while the remaining 9 exceptional graphs fall into two types and require separate analysis. The paper thus provides a systematic characterization of local distinguishability for this class of five-partite OPSs, extending previous studies on fewer parties.

title: Standard Subspaces And Modular Theory -- General Theory And Applications To Qft
authors: Ricardo Correa Da Silva, Gandalf Lechner, Roberto Longo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is a preview of an upcoming monograph on standard subspaces and modular theory. At the moment, it consists of the first chapter. title: Exploring Topological Signatures Of Quantum Fisher Information Scaling In Graph States
authors: Majid Hassani, Patrick Emonts, Jordi Tura
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph states are a versatile resource for quantum metrology, and their quantum Fisher information (QFI) has a closed-form expression in terms of the underlying graph: it counts pairs of vertices with identical neighborhoods. It remains unclear, however, which global structural properties of a graph determine whether its QFI exceeds the standard quantum limit (SQL). Here we ask whether topological invariants, namely the Betti numbers of the graph's clique complex, capture this behavior, and we address the question numerically with two complementary approaches. First, we randomly add or delete edges in balanced complete multipartite graphs, which combine a QFI beyond the SQL with a single nonvanishing higher Betti number. Edge addition eventually destroys both the metrological advantage and the nontrivial topology. Under edge deletion, by contrast, higher Betti numbers persist well after the QFI has dropped to the SQL. Second, we start from Erds--R\'enyi random graphs, whose QFI does not typically exceed the SQL, and maximize a chosen Betti number with a Monte Carlo search. The search drives the graphs toward near-extremal multipartite structures whose QFI lies well beyond the SQL. Our results show that topological optimization offers a route to metrologically useful graph states, but also that Betti numbers alone do not determine the QFI.
tldr: The paper numerically investigates whether Betti numbers of graph clique complexes capture when graph-state quantum Fisher information exceeds the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Graph states are useful metrological resources, and their QFI has a simple graph-theoretic form, but it is unclear which global topological graph properties determine metrological advantage.
method: The authors perturb balanced complete multipartite graphs by edge addition/deletion and perform Monte Carlo optimization of Betti numbers starting from Erdős–Rényi random graphs.
result: Edge addition tends to destroy both QFI advantage and nontrivial topology, while under edge deletion higher Betti numbers can persist after QFI falls to the SQL; Betti-number optimization can also drive random graphs toward multipartite structures with QFI beyond the SQL.
conclusion: Topological optimization may help find metrologically useful graph states, but Betti numbers alone do not determine QFI scaling.

title: Quantum-enabled Measurement Of Gravitational Forces At The Milligram Scale
authors: Matthew Herbst, Ewa Rej, Joe Depellette, Richa Cutting, Jinhoon Jeong, Mika A. Sillanp\"a\"a
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gravity is by far the weakest among all known interactions. While it dominates the large-scale structure of the universe, gravitational interactions between small masses in the microscopic range remain underexplored because they are too weak to be experimentally accessible. The interface between gravity, described by general relativity, and quantum mechanics, which describes the microscopic world, is of particular interest. From a theory standpoint, these two major descriptions of nature have not been combined in a satisfactory manner. Technology is gradually becoming mature enough such that probing gravity at the microscopic scale, where quantum mechanics and gravity potentially meet, is becoming accessible. Explorations towards genuine quantum gravity have to be carried out under conditions where the gravitating masses possess non-classical properties, which necessitates ultimate protection against disturbances, such as ultralow temperatures and a small range of motion. Here, we present an experiment at millikelvin temperatures, where the gravity due to a micron-range coherent displacement of an 87 mg source mass imprints on the motion of an oscillating membrane loaded with a 1.3 mg test mass. Vibrations of the membrane are measured in the microwave optomechanical scheme, which is a key setup for investigating non-classical motional states of mechanical oscillators. When considering the combination of total source and test masses, our setup presents two orders of magnitude progress in sensing gravity at the small scale, as well as a 35 dB improvement of gravitational sensitivity at kHz frequencies or above. Our setup offers a plausible approach for studying gravitational interactions between masses prepared in non-classical motional states.
tldr: The paper demonstrates millikelvin microwave optomechanical sensing of gravitational forces from a micron-range displaced milligram source mass acting on a milligram test mass.
motivation: Probing gravity at microscopic scales is motivated by the unresolved interface between general relativity and quantum mechanics, requiring ultralow temperatures and small motional ranges to protect non-classical states.
method: A 87 mg source mass is coherently displaced over micron ranges, and its gravity imprints on the motion of an oscillating membrane loaded with a 1.3 mg test mass; membrane vibrations are read out via a microwave optomechanical scheme at millikelvin temperatures.
result: The setup achieves two orders of magnitude improvement in small-scale gravitational sensing when combining source and test masses, and a 35 dB improvement in gravitational sensitivity at kHz frequencies or above.
conclusion: The platform offers a plausible route toward studying gravitational interactions between masses prepared in non-classical motional states, though it primarily advances quantum-enabled gravity sensing rather than qubit hardware or transduction.

title: How Many Shots Does A Quantum Reservoir Need? Measurement Cost And Its Scaling In Buffered Quantum Reservoir Computing
authors: Raman Khurana
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) inherits from classical reservoir computing the property that only a linear readout is trained, but unlike a classical reservoir its state is never directly observable: every feature is an expectation value estimated from a finite number of measurement shots. The shot budget is therefore a first-class hyperparameter with no classical analogue. Its effect on QRC has recently begun to be studied; what remains unsettled is how a required budget should be defined, and whether competing definitions agree. This paper argues that they do not, and that the disagreement is systematic rather than incidental. This paper distinguishes a [MATH], the shots needed to estimate the reservoir features to a fixed relative accuracy, from a [MATH], the shots needed for the trained readout to approach its own noise-free ceiling. Proposition~ shows that [MATH] depends on the noise-free error floor by construction, so that a configuration with a worse floor appears cheaper, and that configurations should therefore be compared at a fixed measurement budget rather than by the budget each needs to reach its own ceiling.
tldr: The paper analyzes competing definitions of measurement-shot budgets in buffered quantum reservoir computing and shows that they disagree systematically, so configurations should be compared at fixed measurement cost.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing requires estimating features from finite measurement shots, making the shot budget a key hyperparameter with no classical analogue; existing notions of required budget are unsettled and potentially incomparable.
method: The author distinguishes two shot-budget definitions—one based on estimating reservoir features to fixed relative accuracy and one based on approaching the readout's noise-free ceiling—and proves a proposition relating the latter to the noise-free error floor.
result: The two budget definitions do not agree: the shots needed to reach a readout's own ceiling depend on its noise-free error floor, so a worse-performing configuration can appear cheaper.
conclusion: Fair comparisons of quantum reservoir computing configurations should use a fixed measurement budget rather than each configuration's own ceiling-reaching budget.

tldr: The paper reduces Toffoli-gate and logical-qubit costs in Gidney-style RSA-2048 factoring circuits via shared table lookups and retained intermediate residues.
motivation: Factoring RSA-2048 with fault-tolerant quantum computers remains resource-intensive, and discrete-log table lookups plus residue uncomputation dominate Toffoli counts in recent low-qubit constructions.
method: The authors introduce shared lookups across primes in a residue number system and lazy modular arithmetic using retained intermediate residues, with proofs of output preservation and resource estimates from an open benchmark simulator.
result: They report substantially fewer Toffoli gates than the best reference within the same logical-qubit budget, including a matched ablation isolating gains from three-prime sharing.
conclusion: The work improves quantum resource estimates for factoring, but the practical runtime benefit depends on architecture-specific timing; it is primarily a quantum-algorithm resource-optimization contribution rather than a core information-theoretic or thermodynamic result.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Classical Communications For DPMZM-based Ng-pon2 Systems
authors: Parvin Kumar, Sourav Banerjee, Neel Kanth Kundu, Umesh Sharma
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a framework for integrating quantum detection techniques into a Dual-Parallel Mach-Zehnder Modulator (DPMZM)-based Next Generation Passive Optical Network 2 (NG-PON2) communication system. We present a system model for the DPMZM-based NG-PON2 quantum communication system and characterize its signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), demonstrating its superiority over conventional MZM-based systems. We analyze the performance of various quantum modulation techniques, including binary phase-shift keying, quadrature phase-shift keying, and M-ary quadrature amplitude modulation. A comprehensive analytical framework is developed to evaluate the SNR, BER, and mutual information for both classical and quantum detection schemes within the DPMZM-based NG-PON2 quantum communication system. Our simulation results show that quantum detection significantly outperforms classical detection, and the DPMZM architecture further enhances the performance over the baseline MZM architecture by improving the effective modulation efficiency and receiver sensitivity.
tldr: The paper proposes a DPMZM-based NG-PON2 optical access system enhanced with quantum detection techniques and analyzes its SNR, BER, and mutual information.
motivation: It aims to improve classical optical communication performance by integrating quantum detection schemes into next-generation passive optical networks.
method: The authors develop an analytical and simulation framework for BPSK, QPSK, and M-ary QAM in DPMZM-based NG-PON2 systems, comparing classical and quantum detection via SNR, BER, and mutual information.
result: Quantum detection is shown to significantly outperform classical detection, and the DPMZM architecture improves modulation efficiency and receiver sensitivity relative to MZM-based systems.
conclusion: Quantum-enhanced detection offers performance gains for classical NG-PON2 access networks, but the work remains an applied optical communication study rather than a core quantum information or quantum networking contribution.

title: Neutral-atom Quantum Features As Complementary Structural Encodings For Graph Learning
authors: Mathieu Garrigues, Igor O. Sokolov, Matthias Hecker, Lorenzo Moro, Shaheen Acheche
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Structural descriptors provide graph neural networks (GNNs) with positional and topological inductive biases. However, widely used classical encodings based on random walks or Laplacian spectra emphasize specific structural statistics of a graph, leaving room for alternative descriptors. Neutral-atom quantum processing units (QPUs) can realize graph-dependent Rydberg Hamiltonians, allowing graph topology to be probed through dynamical correlation measurements. In this work, we use these measurements as quantum graph features (QGFs), providing a complementary, hardware-derived family of structural encoding that is not accurately described by classical features derived from Laplacian and adjacency matrices, even when supplemented with an extended set of random-walk, geometric descriptors and classical physical models. By appropriately selecting the quench parameters of the Hamiltonian, we access two characteristic correlation regimes with distinct structural signatures: antiferromagnetic-like and ferromagnetic-like. On an intrinsic information benchmark of 15 topological and spectral probing tasks, quantum and hybrid quantum-classical features match or surpass classical descriptors on local topological properties. When supplied to message-passing, attention, and graph-transformer backbones, hybrid quantum-classical features yield improvements that are within cross-fold noise on most cells but sign-consistent across architectures. When comparing noiseless, shot-sampled emulation-derived quantum features with a neutral-atom QPU implementation, the downstream hybrid results with compressed hardware features match their emulated counterparts within [MATH] F[MATH] on all backbones. On a synthetic family of ladder graphs, QGFs distinguish two specific classes, outperforming the strongest classical structural descriptors by a margin exceeding cross-fold variability.
tldr: The paper uses dynamical correlation measurements from neutral-atom Rydberg quantum processors as 'quantum graph features' that complement classical structural encodings in graph neural networks.
motivation: Classical structural descriptors for GNNs (random-walk, Laplacian spectral) capture only specific graph statistics, so the authors seek alternative, hardware-derived descriptors enabled by graph-dependent Rydberg Hamiltonians.
method: They quench graph-encoded Rydberg Hamiltonians on a neutral-atom QPU in antiferromagnetic-like and ferromagnetic-like regimes, extract correlation-based features, and feed them (alone or hybridized with classical features) into message-passing, attention, and graph-transformer backbones across 15 probing tasks.
result: Quantum and hybrid features match or beat classical descriptors on local topological tasks, with small but architecture-consistent downstream gains; compressed hardware features match noiseless emulation within ~1% F1, and on synthetic ladder graphs QGFs separate two classes beyond classical descriptor margins.
conclusion: Neutral-atom QPUs can supply genuinely complementary structural encodings for graph learning, though demonstrated practical advantages remain modest and within noise for most settings.

title: Quantum Interactive Proofs Of Proximity
authors: Kenan Wood
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We initiate the systematic study of quantum interactive proofs of proximity (QIPPs). These are quantum interactive proof systems with sublinear communication, where the verifier accepts inputs in a property [MATH] and rejects inputs [MATH]-far from [MATH], while only querying the input a sublinear number of times. 1. We show that all logspace-uniform [MATH] properties admit QIPPs with query, communication and time complexity all [MATH]. This improves on the best known classical total complexity of [MATH], which is optimal in the worst case for polynomial-time verifiers under the PRG assumption of Kalai and Rothblum (CRYPTO, 2015). This resolves an open question of Dall'Agnol, Gur, Roy Moulik, and Thaler (Quantum, 2022) in the affirmative. 2. Assuming the existence of a post-quantum subexponentially secure PRG computable in logspace-uniform [MATH], we prove that, for every nondecreasing, logspace-computable query bound [MATH], there exists a property [MATH] in logspace-uniform [MATH] and a constant [MATH] such that no polynomial-time [MATH]-QIPP for [MATH] can achieve query complexity [MATH] and communication complexity [MATH] satisfying [MATH]. 3. We establish a bi-directional connection between QIPPs for logspace-uniform [MATH] and query-model QIPs for parity. A QIP for [MATH]-bit parity with total complexity [MATH] yields QIPPs for every logspace-uniform [MATH] property with total complexity [MATH]. Conversely, achieving total complexity [MATH] within the standard [MATH]-based framework requires improving the known query-communication tradeoff for parity. Additionally, we show that almost every size-[MATH] property ([MATH]) requires linear total QIPP complexity at constant proximity.
tldr: The paper initiates the study of quantum interactive proofs of proximity (QIPPs), establishing near-optimal upper bounds for logspace-uniform properties, matching lower bounds under cryptographic assumptions, and a tight connection to query-model QIPs for parity.
motivation: Classical interactive proofs of proximity achieve total complexity that appears optimal for polynomial-time verifiers under PRG assumptions; the authors ask whether quantum verifiers with sublinear communication can do fundamentally better, resolving an open question of Dall'Agnol et al.
method: They define QIPPs with sublinear query, communication and time complexity, construct protocols for all logspace-uniform properties, prove impossibility results assuming post-quantum subexponentially secure logspace-computable PRGs, and establish a bi-directional reduction between QIPPs and query-model QIPs for parity.
result: All logspace-uniform properties admit QIPPs with polylogarithmic query, communication and time complexity, beating the classical bound; conversely, under the PRG assumption no polynomial-time QIPP can achieve certain sub-polylogarithmic tradeoffs, and almost every size-n property requires linear total QIPP complexity at constant proximity.
conclusion: Quantum interactive proofs of proximity offer a genuine complexity-theoretic advantage over classical ones, with the parity QIP's query-communication tradeoff identified as the key bottleneck for further improvements.

title: Empirical Assessment Of Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption Status In Tls
authors: Md Ariful Haque, Sander Vinberg, Ben Edwards, Jo\~ao Cruz
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anticipating Q-day security concerns, major CDNs and cloud providers are migrating to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). While existing literature benchmarks PQC performance, empirical research evaluating real-world adoption data remains scarce. We present an empirical assessment of PQC deployment across seven critical protocols (HTTPS, LDAPS, SMTPS, IMAP-SSL, POP3-SSL, TELNETS, and RDP) using 10,000 target IP addresses per protocol. At the origin-server level, PQC algorithm support reaches 9.1% for HTTPS and 7.39% for LDAPS, while falling below 1% for all other evaluated protocols. At the entity level, PQC support is 11% for HTTPS and 5.4% for LDAPS, while the remaining protocols have less than 5% of entities supporting PQC on the hosted servers. We further correlate these adoption trends against organizational digital and financial footprint, and industry sectors, yielding a multi-dimensional empirical assessment of PQC deployment. Finally, at the domain level, we perform a comparative analysis of PQC adoption in Cloudflare-hosted domains against baseline Cloudflare datasets. Collectively, our findings provide critical insights into the current state of PQC readiness over Transport Layer Security (TLS).
tldr: This paper empirically measures post-quantum cryptography adoption across seven TLS-based protocols using large-scale IP scanning.
motivation: Anticipating Q-day security risks, cloud providers and CDNs are migrating to PQC, but empirical data on real-world deployment remains scarce.
method: The authors scan 10,000 target IP addresses per protocol for HTTPS, LDAPS, SMTPS, IMAP-SSL, POP3-SSL, TELNETS, and RDP, assessing PQC support at origin-server and entity levels and correlating adoption with organizational and sector data.
result: PQC support reaches 9.1% at the origin-server level for HTTPS and 7.39% for LDAPS, but falls below 1% for other protocols; entity-level support is 11% for HTTPS and 5.4% for LDAPS.
conclusion: PQC deployment over TLS remains limited and uneven, providing a baseline empirical assessment of current adoption readiness.

title: Anchored Iterative Decoding Of Reed-Solomon Product Codes For High-Rate Magnetic Tape Storage
authors: Nikolay Malkovsky Alexander Chvanov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a decoding algorithm for a Reed--Solomon product code targeted at the demanding reliability requirements of modern magnetic tape storage. For a code [MATH] in a BSC we achieve post-decoding bit error rate (BER) of [MATH] at [MATH] raw BER while maintaining the common requirement to detect and correct 4 out of 32 dead tracks. We resolve two common problems of miscorrections and stall patterns that arise under such a high raw BER via simplified versions of anchor decoding and binary image analysis. The highest efficiency is achieved by performing an unlimited iterative decoder, which performs decoding iterations until no changes are made. We give an empirical analysis of the average number of iterations: below the raw BER of [MATH], four half-iterations are performed on average while improving substantially over a decoder that always performs 4 half-iterations. We provide a CPU implementation achieving 100-200 megabytes/s single-core throughput on a regular laptop and a design of a potential hybrid FPGA-CPU implementation of our decoder.
tldr: The paper presents an anchored iterative decoding algorithm for Reed-Solomon product codes aimed at high-rate magnetic tape storage, using anchor decoding and binary image analysis to combat miscorrections and stall patterns.
motivation: Magnetic tape storage demands extremely low post-decoding bit error rates at high raw BER while also detecting and correcting dead tracks, and standard product-code decoders suffer from miscorrections and stall patterns in this regime.
method: The authors combine simplified anchor decoding with binary image analysis in an unlimited iterative decoder that iterates until no further changes occur, and they analyze the average number of iterations empirically; CPU and hybrid FPGA-CPU implementations are also designed.
result: Post-decoding BER of order 1e-15 is achieved at high raw BER while meeting the 4-out-of-32 dead-track requirement, with an average of fewer than four half-iterations below a certain raw BER and 100-200 MB/s single-core throughput on a laptop.
conclusion: Anchored iterative decoding with unlimited iterations offers an efficient practical solution for classical erasure/error correction in tape storage, though the work is purely classical and has no quantum information content.

title: Hardness Of Unique Shortest Vectors And Bounded Distance Decoding
authors: Jason Luo Sergei Kudria
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove randomized NP-hardness of the unique shortest vector problem (uSVP) at every constant uniqueness factor greater than one, and of bounded distance decoding (BDD) at every fixed positive fraction less than one half of the minimum distance, in both their threshold decision and search versions. Both results hold in every fixed [MATH] norm with [MATH]. Previous Euclidean NP-hardness results for the search versions reached uniqueness factors tending to one and decoding radii greater than the minimum distance divided by [MATH]. For linear codes over every fixed finite field and each fixed [MATH], the decision version of BDD with radius strictly less than [MATH] times the minimum distance is equivalent under deterministic polynomial-time reductions to satisfiability for circuits promised to have at most one satisfying input. It is therefore NP-hard under randomized polynomial-time reductions. Earlier hardness for decoding general codes applied beyond half the minimum distance. For every fixed [MATH] and for [MATH], there is a constant [MATH] such that, under randomized polynomial-time reductions, uSVP in the [MATH] norm is NP-hard at uniqueness factor [MATH], and BDD in the [MATH] norm is NP-hard at radius [MATH], where [MATH] is the lattice rank and [MATH] is its minimum distance.
tldr: The paper proves randomized NP-hardness for the unique shortest vector problem and bounded distance decoding at essentially optimal uniqueness factors and decoding radii in every fixed L_p norm.
motivation: Lattice problems such as uSVP and BDD underpin post-quantum cryptography, and prior hardness results only reached uniqueness factors tending to one (Euclidean) or decoding radii above d/2, leaving gaps at the precise parameter regimes used in cryptographic constructions.
method: The authors give deterministic polynomial-time reductions showing that decision-BDD below half the minimum distance for linear codes over fixed finite fields is equivalent to satisfiability of circuits promised to have at most one satisfying assignment, then transfer these to lattice problems in arbitrary fixed norms.
result: uSVP is NP-hard under randomized reductions for every constant uniqueness factor greater than one, and BDD is NP-hard for every fixed radius fraction below one half of the minimum distance, in every fixed L_p norm with p >= 1.
conclusion: The hardness landscape for uSVP and BDD is essentially closed at the optimal parameter thresholds, tightening the theoretical foundations of lattice-based cryptography.

title: Empirical Study Of Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption Status In Ssh Infrastructure
authors: Md Ariful Haque, Sander Vinberg, Ben Edwards, Jo\~ao Cruz
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the anticipated arrival of Q-day, quantum computers threaten current cryptographic schemes for encryption and digital signatures. In response, major content delivery networks and cloud service providers are already adopting Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC). The current state-of-the-art focuses on benchmarking the operational performance of implementing PQC, but the real-world adoption status remains under-researched. This work utilizes large-scale SSH fingerprint data from a proprietary scanning tool to analyze PQC adoption across 1.52 million hosts and 27,012 entities. Our study shows that the PQC transition in the SSH protocol is underway but highly polarized: 45.2% of SSH hosts on port 22 support PQC, while 54.8% remain classical-only. At the entity level, 39.9% have enabled PQC on at least one host, whereas 60.1% have no PQC support. By correlating PQC adoption with industry, geography, and organizational size (digital and financial), this study provides a comprehensive empirical assessment of PQC adoption status in SSH infrastructure.
tldr: A large-scale empirical scan of SSH fingerprints across 1.52 million hosts shows that post-quantum cryptography support is partially deployed but highly polarized between early-adopting entities and classical-only infrastructure.
motivation: With the anticipated arrival of Q-day, quantum computers threaten current encryption and signature schemes, and while cloud providers and CDNs are adopting PQC, the real-world adoption status remains under-researched compared to operational benchmarking studies.
method: The authors mine large-scale SSH fingerprint data from a proprietary scanning tool covering 1.52 million hosts and 27,012 entities, then correlate PQC support with industry sector, geography, and organizational size (digital and financial).
result: 45.2% of SSH hosts on port 22 support PQC while 54.8% remain classical-only; at the entity level 39.9% have PQC enabled on at least one host and 60.1% have no PQC support at all, revealing a strongly polarized transition.
conclusion: PQC migration in SSH infrastructure is underway but far from complete, and the polarization by industry, geography, and organizational size highlights where outreach and standardization pressure are most needed.

title: Levenshtein-type Bounds For $(a,b)$-avoiding Spherical Codes
authors: Peter Boyvalenkov, Danila Cherkashin, Peter Dragnev, Peter Grabner
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a Levenshtein-type linear programming framework (for maximal [MATH]-codes and for minimal energy) for [MATH]-avoiding spherical codes, that is, codes whose inner products between distinct points avoid [MATH]. We introduce and investigate signed measures that are positive definite up to an appropriate degree and yield stationary auxiliary linear programming polynomials and exact quadrature formulas. We give explicit conditions for positivity of the quadrature weights and sufficient Krein-type conditions for nonnegative Gegenbauer coefficients (positive definiteness of the candidate optimal linear programming polynomials). Under these hypotheses and suitable node-location assumptions, the resulting cardinality bounds are optimal within the corresponding degree restriction and unique under natural nondegeneracy conditions. Under proper conditions on the quadrature nodes, we obtain universal lower energy bounds by utilizing Hermite interpolants as polynomial solutions of the respective linear program. Common test functions characterize optimality in the full polynomial linear programs under mild additional assumptions.
tldr: The paper develops Levenshtein-type linear-programming bounds for spherical codes whose inner products avoid a given interval (a,b), covering maximal code size and minimal Riesz energy.
motivation: Spherical codes with forbidden inner-product ranges generalize classical spherical designs and (a,b)-avoiding configurations, but sharp universal bounds of Levenshtein type were lacking for this setting.
method: The authors construct signed measures that are positive definite up to a suitable degree, yielding stationary auxiliary LP polynomials and exact quadrature formulas, with explicit positivity conditions for quadrature weights and Krein-type conditions for nonnegative Gegenbauer coefficients; Hermite interpolants provide energy bounds.
result: Under node-location and positivity hypotheses, the derived cardinality bounds are optimal within the given degree restriction and unique under nondegeneracy, and universal lower energy bounds follow.
conclusion: The framework extends Levenshtein's LP method to (a,b)-avoiding spherical codes, giving exactly solvable bounds and optimality criteria, but it remains a purely classical discrete-geometry/coding-theory contribution.

title: Universality In Quantum Many-Body Spin Ratchets
authors: Marko Ljubotina Andrea Azzali
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a class of quantum circuits, known as quantum many-body spin ratchets, which act on alternating spin chains with two distinct spin types on even and odd sites. This setup breaks parity symmetry and exhibits chiral transport. It has been shown that the drift velocity in the case of integrable, SU(2)-symmetric quantum spin ratchets is universal, and conjectured that the same holds in the non-integrable case. Here, we prove that this universal drift is exact at all times, requiring only translation invariance and U(1) symmetry. Furthermore, we prove that it is sufficient for the circuit to be translation-invariant on average by deriving the same result in the random case. Finally, we demonstrate that breaking translation invariance immediately results in deviations from this universal prediction.
tldr: The paper proves universal drift velocity in quantum many-body spin ratchets under translation invariance and U(1) symmetry, including random circuits with average translation invariance.
motivation: Previous work showed universal chiral transport in integrable SU(2)-symmetric spin ratchets and conjectured the same for non-integrable cases; this paper aims to establish exact universality under minimal assumptions.
method: The authors analyze quantum circuits on alternating spin chains, proving exact universal drift at all times from translation invariance and U(1) symmetry, and extend the result to random circuits with average translation invariance.
result: The universal drift is exact at all times and persists under average translation invariance, while breaking translation invariance immediately produces deviations from the universal prediction.
conclusion: The results establish a broad symmetry-based universality mechanism for chiral transport in quantum many-body spin ratchets, clarifying the role of translation invariance.

title: Sign-hedged Beam QAOA:Scaling Quantum Optimization Algorithms
authors: Arush Sharma Anupama Ray
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) encodes a combinatorial objective as an Ising Hamiltonian and alternates cost and mixer operations for p rounds. Recursive QAOA (RQAOA) scales further by using the resulting correlations, whether variables tend to agree or disagree, to eliminate variables one at a time. But each inferred sign is accepted irrevocably, so a single early mistake propagates through every later reduction and can discard the global optimum. As elimination proceeds, residuals shrink while effective edge density typically rises, so later decisions face denser Ising problems, a regime that fully connected Sherrington Kirkpatrick (SK) instances stress test directly. This paper proposes sign-hedged beam RQAOA, which retains the variable or pair selected by standard RQAOA, explores both possible sign assignments, keeps the best B residual problems according to a classical score, and completes each survivor with ordinary RQAOA. On frustrated SK instances, where standard recursion collapses to AR 0.474, beam recovers near-optimal AR 0.998 at the same p. We evaluate the workflow on 50+ instances from HamLib and QOBLIB, spanning 4 and 5 regular and Erdos Renyi MaxCut graphs, Sherrington Kirkpatrick (SK) spin glasses, and cardinality-constrained portfolio optimization, with up to 60 qubits and hardware runs on ibm kingston and ibm marrakesh. Matched simulator and device cells show consistent beam rankings: simulation and hardware agree that beam recovers near-optimal approximation ratio (AR) where standard recursion fails. These gains come from additional residual-circuit evaluations, classical pruning, and exact solution of a small core, rather than from increasing p, beam is a decision-side optimization atop fixed-p QAOA/RQAOA, not a claim that quantum circuits alone scale with qubit count.
tldr: The paper proposes a sign-hedged beam search variant of recursive QAOA to avoid early irrevocable variable-elimination errors in quantum combinatorial optimization.
motivation: Standard recursive QAOA can discard the global optimum when an early sign decision is wrong, especially as residuals become denser and more frustrated.
method: The authors retain the standard RQAOA variable or pair selection but explore both sign assignments, keep the best B residual problems by a classical score, and complete each survivor with ordinary RQAOA.
result: On frustrated Sherrington-Kirkpatrick instances, standard recursion achieves approximation ratio 0.474 while the beam method reaches 0.998 at the same p; simulator and IBM hardware runs show consistent ranking improvements across HamLib and QOBLIB instances.
conclusion: The gains come from additional residual-circuit evaluations, classical pruning, and exact core solving rather than from increasing p, so beam search is a decision-side optimization atop fixed-p QAOA/RQAOA.

title: From Spectroscopy To Quantum Dynamics: Assessing Reduced Models Of A NaCs Molecular Gate
authors: Marko Gacesa
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how spectroscopic calibration and basis selection affect predictions for a dipolar-exchange gate between two optically trapped [MATH]Na[MATH]Cs molecules. We construct a 128-state molecular Hamiltonian restricted to the [MATH] rotational manifold, fit two effective optical parameters to three bright microwave transitions, and compare the resulting spectrum with four additional lines. In the coherent pair model, changing the optical polarization angle by [MATH] reduces the calculated gate fidelity from 94.64\% to 1.09\% at fixed carrier frequencies. Retuning the carriers and restoring the target Rabi frequencies recovers 89.31\%. The remaining sensitivity reflects changes in the multilevel pair dynamics that are not removed by target-frequency and target-Rabi recalibration. Enlarging the molecular basis produces nonmonotonic changes in fidelity, although the 11-state and 25-state calculations give closely agreeing logical maps after phase alignment. Two controls with isolated transfer probabilities near 98.45\% yield complete-gate fidelities differing by more than 11 percentage points. We relate these comparisons to a sufficient bound on the error of a projected propagator. The numerical tests quantify agreement among selected bases for a specified coherent Hamiltonian.
tldr: The paper evaluates how spectroscopic calibration and basis truncation affect predicted fidelity of a dipolar-exchange gate between two optically trapped NaCs molecules.
motivation: Molecular platforms are promising for quantum gates, but reduced models and spectroscopic uncertainties can strongly affect gate predictions.
method: Constructs a 128-state rotational Hamiltonian, fits two effective optical parameters to three microwave transitions, and compares spectra and coherent pair gate fidelities across basis sizes, polarization angles, and recalibration controls.
result: Changing polarization can drop fidelity from 94.64% to 1.09%, retuning recovers 89.31%; basis-size effects are nonmonotonic, and isolated-transfer controls differ by more than 11 percentage points in full gate fidelity.
conclusion: Spectroscopic calibration and basis selection critically affect molecular gate fidelity predictions, motivating careful model validation and error bounds for projected propagators.

title: Tailoring Resonator Geometry For Astigmatism Compensation With Structured Light In Birefringent Optical Cavities
authors: J. C. de Carvalho Jr., R. F. Barros, A. Z. Khoury, C. E. R. Souza, G. B. Alves
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we experimentally investigate the astigmatism induced by a birefringent crystal inside an optical cavity and demonstrate a geometric compensation strategy for structured modes carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM). We show that the astigmatism observed in the semimonolithic configuration can be fully compensated by introducing a third mirror to fold the cavity, thereby exploiting the geometric astigmatism arising from oblique incidence on the curved mirror. By performing a study of the resonator geometry, both theoretical and experimental results confirm that this approach enables the preservation of OAM between the pump beam and the converted signal and idler modes, providing an effective design strategy for birefringent optical cavities.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates geometric compensation of astigmatism in a birefringent optical cavity to preserve orbital angular momentum modes of structured light.
motivation: Birefringent crystals inside optical cavities introduce astigmatism that can distort structured light carrying orbital angular momentum, limiting mode preservation in nonlinear optical processes.
method: The authors study a semimonolithic cavity with a birefringent crystal and introduce a third folded mirror to exploit geometric astigmatism from oblique incidence, comparing theoretical resonator geometry with experiments.
