result: The folded-cavity design fully compensates the crystal-induced astigmatism and preserves OAM between the pump and converted signal/idler modes.
conclusion: The work provides a practical geometric design strategy for birefringent optical cavities using structured light, though it is primarily an experimental optics/cavity engineering result.

title: Perfect Wave Transfer In Nonconformal Tomonaga-Luttinger Liquids
authors: Denys Dutykh Davide Batic
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Perfect wave transfer (PWT) reproduces spatial reflection at a common finite time under a fixed Hamiltonian. We classify this process for open compact bosons and inhomogeneous Tomonaga--Luttinger liquids, distinguishing transfer of oscillator and neutral observables from transfer on the charged field algebra. In the single-charge model, the first two notions coincide. Global transfer additionally requires rephasing of the compact zero mode. For regular reflection-symmetric channels, exact oscillator transfer forces an odd multiple of the optical crossing time and a strictly ordered, parity-compatible spectrum differing from the conformal ladder at only finitely many levels. This spectral condition is also sufficient when the Robin boundary data induced by the physical profile are included. Requiring Neumann conditions after the Liouville transformation instead forces conformality. We construct an explicit, regular one-defect family for every [MATH]. Its transfer parameters are precisely the reduced fractions [MATH] with odd numerator and denominator, with shortest transfer time [MATH]. At the delay [MATH], the [MATH] profile has numerical contrast [MATH], compared with [MATH] for [MATH]. Two independent conservative discretizations show second-order convergence on fixed mode bands. Occupation- and charge-constrained error estimates quantify robustness, while an exact homogeneous-chain calculation explains the [MATH] resolved-band scale also observed in the engineered channels. These results provide a spectral design method and finite-device benchmarks for quadratic quantum channels. An interacting microscopic realization remains open.
tldr: The paper classifies perfect wave transfer in nonconformal Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids and constructs spectral design methods for quadratic bosonic channels.
motivation: Perfect wave transfer reproduces spatial reflection at a finite time under a fixed Hamiltonian, and the authors aim to characterize when this occurs in compact boson and inhomogeneous Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid models.
method: The authors use spectral conditions, Liouville transformations, Robin/Neumann boundary data, and two conservative discretizations to analyze oscillator and charged-field transfer in reflection-symmetric channels.
result: Exact oscillator transfer requires an odd multiple of the optical crossing time and a parity-compatible spectrum differing from the conformal ladder at finitely many levels; explicit one-defect families achieve transfer parameters given by reduced fractions with odd numerator and denominator.
conclusion: The work provides a spectral design method and finite-device benchmarks for quadratic quantum channels, while an interacting microscopic realization remains open.

title: $\mathbb{Z}_2$ Gauge And Exact Solution Of The $\pm J$ Edwards-Anderson Model In A Transverse Field
authors: Mikhail Vasin
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the Majorana representation of spin-1/2 operators, we study the [MATH] Edwards--Anderson model in a transverse field at [MATH]. We show that, in this representation, the quantity describing the coupling between neighboring spins commutes with the Hamiltonian and, unlike in the Kitaev model, is not subject to any Gauss law. The resulting [MATH] gauge freedom allows the disorder in the signs of the exchange integrals to be eliminated by an exact gauge transformation, so that the spectrum of the system coincides with that of the model with uniform couplings. The resulting theory is quadratic in the Majorana fields. Computing the local Green's functions, we find that the Edwards--Anderson order parameter vanishes for [MATH] and equals [MATH] for [MATH], which signals a second-order transition from a paramagnetic phase to a spin-glass ground state that is degenerate over spin configurations and replica symmetric at [MATH].
tldr: The paper exactly solves a transverse-field ±J Edwards–Anderson spin glass using a Majorana representation and a Z2 gauge transformation that removes disorder in the exchange signs.
motivation: The ±J Edwards–Anderson model in a transverse field is a canonical disordered spin-glass model, and the authors aim to understand its phase structure and solvability via a gauge-based mapping.
method: Spin-1/2 operators are represented by Majorana fermions, revealing a commuting Z2 gauge structure without a Gauss-law constraint; a gauge transformation eliminates the random sign disorder, yielding a quadratic Majorana theory.
result: The spectrum coincides with that of the uniform-coupling model. Local Green's functions show the Edwards–Anderson order parameter vanishes for one regime and is nonzero for another, indicating a paramagnetic-to-spin-glass transition that is replica symmetric.
conclusion: The work provides an exact solution of a quantum spin-glass model and identifies a second-order transition to a degenerate spin-glass phase, but it lies outside the listed quantum-information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid-systems research directions.

title: Low-Rank Iteration For Efficient Calculations Of Topological Surface States
authors: Kaiqi Liu, Changsheng He, Zihan Xie, Shulin Sun, Lei Zhou, Shaojie Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface states are hallmarks of topological phases, and their efficient computation is crucial for topology characterization. Conventional supercell methods (SCM) approximate semi-infinite systems as finite periodic ones, but suffer from high computational cost, artificial inter-surface coupling, and slow convergence near band edges. Recently, boundary problems for semi-infinite systems have been recast as block-tridiagonal equations and solved by the cyclic reduction method (CRM) and the transfer matrix method (TMM). However, these approaches remain resource-intensive, as fine-mesh discretization produces very large matrices. Recognizing the intrinsic sparsity and low rank of these matrices, we develop a low-rank iterative method (LIM) with stochastic trace estimation that substantially reduces complexity and memory without sacrificing accuracy, while remaining straightforwardly parallelizable. Benchmarks on 2D and 3D topological systems show orders-of-magnitude acceleration over CRM and TMM. LIM extends readily to heterostructures, defective interfaces, and non-Hermitian systems, providing an efficient platform for topological and plasmonic surface phenomena.
tldr: A low-rank iterative numerical method with stochastic trace estimation is introduced to compute topological surface states of semi-infinite systems far more efficiently than cyclic reduction or transfer-matrix approaches.
motivation: Existing supercell, cyclic reduction, and transfer matrix methods for surface-state calculations are computationally expensive because fine-mesh discretization produces very large block-tridiagonal matrices, limiting topology characterization of realistic 3D and heterostructure systems.
method: The boundary problem for semi-infinite systems is expressed as a block-tridiagonal equation, and exploiting the sparsity and low rank of the resulting matrices, a low-rank iterative solver combined with stochastic trace estimation is developed, with straightforward parallelization.
result: Benchmarks on 2D and 3D topological systems show orders-of-magnitude speedups over cyclic reduction and transfer matrix methods without loss of accuracy, and the scheme extends to heterostructures, defective interfaces, and non-Hermitian systems.
conclusion: The method provides an efficient, scalable computational platform for studying topological surface states and plasmonic surface phenomena, though it is a numerical condensed-matter tool rather than a quantum-information or thermodynamics contribution.

title: Exploring Variational Regularization Of Krylov Subspaces
authors: Alexandre Perrin, J\'er\'emie Messud, S\'ebastien Burdin, Matthieu Sauban\`ere
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Krylov subspace methods efficiently approximate extremal eigenstates and eigenvalues of many-body Hamiltonians, but non-orthogonal bases can suffer from ill-conditioning. This challenge is amplified in quantum computing, where direct state access and thus straightforward orthogonalization are unavailable. We investigate a variational Krylov-like framework that iteratively optimizes a parametrized sequence of states to mimic Lanczos-like couplings while penalizing linear dependencies. Analyzed against exact Krylov and Lanczos on a finite Anderson impurity model, ansatz expressivity strongly influences the performance: Hamiltonian-inspired ans\"atze preserve Krylov-like convergence while improving the conditioning, whereas shallow ans\"atze remain stable but miss low-energy directions.
tldr: The paper explores a variational Krylov-like framework for approximating extremal eigenstates on quantum computers while mitigating ill-conditioning from non-orthogonal bases.
motivation: Krylov subspace methods are efficient for many-body eigenproblems, but non-orthogonal bases become ill-conditioned, and quantum computing lacks direct state access for straightforward orthogonalization.
method: The authors iteratively optimize a parametrized sequence of states to mimic Lanczos-like couplings while penalizing linear dependencies, benchmarking against exact Krylov and Lanczos on a finite Anderson impurity model.
result: Hamiltonian-inspired ansatze preserve Krylov-like convergence and improve conditioning, whereas shallow ansatze remain stable but fail to capture low-energy directions.
conclusion: Ansatz expressivity strongly affects performance, revealing a tradeoff between regularization and convergence in variational Krylov methods for quantum computing.

title: Reflections Of Nichols Algebras In Braided Monoidal Categories
authors: Bowen Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be an essentially small abelian rigid braided monoidal category. We prove a reflection theorem for Nichols algebras in [MATH] and show that tuples admitting all reflections define connected semi-Cartan graphs. As applications, we prove that a finite Nichols algebra has a generating object of length at most one in [MATH] for odd [MATH], in [MATH] for [MATH], and in the representation categories of the Virasoro minimal models [MATH] for odd [MATH]. In all three families, we prove that every finite pre-Nichols algebra is a Nichols algebra.
tldr: The paper proves a reflection theorem for Nichols algebras in abelian rigid braided monoidal categories and shows that tuples admitting all reflections yield connected semi-Cartan graphs.
motivation: Nichols algebras underlie quantized enveloping algebras and pointed Hopf algebras, and the authors aim to extend reflection/Cartan-graph techniques from the classical setting to general braided monoidal categories.
method: Abstract categorical and Hopf-algebraic arguments: reflection functors in essentially small abelian rigid braided monoidal categories, applied to determine generation in one object and to classify finite pre-Nichols algebras.
result: Finite Nichols algebras have a length-at-most-one generating object in the odd-root-of-unity and Virasoro minimal model categories (and a related family), and in all three families every finite pre-Nichols algebra is a Nichols algebra.
conclusion: The reflection theorem provides a uniform structural tool for Nichols algebras across representation categories, but the work is purely algebraic and has no direct bearing on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Reconfiguration Of Time-Bounded Descriptions
authors: Dimitrios Myrisiotis
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity measures a string by the length of its shortest program that prints it within a deadline. An adjunction-universal machine (Bauwens, Kozachinskiy, and Shen, arXiv, 2025) is a Turing machine that simulates every Turing machine [MATH] on every input [MATH] with polynomial overhead when given a code of [MATH], computable from [MATH] in polynomial time, followed by [MATH] unchanged. Any two adjunction-universal machines give the same measure up to an additive constant and a polynomial change of the deadline. However, this measure records only the shortest program for a string. We study all programs of one length that print a string within one deadline, join two of them when they differ in one bit, and ask when this graph is connected. Fix any adjunction-universal machine. For almost all [MATH]-bit strings and every deadline beyond some polynomial, the graph is disconnected at program length [MATH] and has at least [MATH] components at length [MATH]. In contrast, we build an adjunction-universal machine in which every such graph is connected or empty, at every deadline, once the program length reaches a computable threshold that is at most exponential in the length of the string. Exponential thresholds are unavoidable: for every adjunction-universal machine with such thresholds and every large [MATH], more than three quarters of the [MATH]-bit strings need a threshold exponential in [MATH]. For our machine, above the threshold, every program for the string is within three bit flips of a connected set of fastest programs for the string, along a path inside the graph, at every deadline by which that program halts. For this machine, deciding whether two given programs are connected in this graph is [MATH]-complete when the input is the string, the deadline in unary and the two programs; for each fixed string it takes polynomial time.
tldr: The paper studies the connectivity of graphs whose vertices are fixed-length programs printing a string within a deadline, in the setting of time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity with adjunction-universal machines.
motivation: Time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity only records the shortest program for a string; the authors want to understand the structure of the full space of programs of a given length that print a string within a deadline, and how universal-machine choice affects that structure.
method: Defining a graph on equal-length programs joined when they differ in one bit, the authors prove disconnection results for almost all strings under arbitrary adjunction-universal machines, and construct a special adjunction-universal machine whose graphs are connected or empty above an exponential threshold, with accompanying complexity-theoretic hardness results.
result: For generic machines the program graph is disconnected at program length n and has exponentially many components at slightly larger lengths, whereas a carefully built universal machine yields connected-or-empty graphs above a threshold at most exponential in the string length; exponential thresholds are shown to be unavoidable for most strings, and connectivity testing is complete for a high complexity class.
conclusion: The choice of universal machine strongly influences the connectivity structure of time-bounded program graphs, and exponential thresholds are intrinsic, giving a refined structural picture of time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity.

title: Modulation Induced Memory Resonances In Dynamically Driven Optical Cavities
authors: Faizan H. Lone
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temporal modulation of optical cavities provides a powerful mechanism for controlling photonic states beyond the static cavity paradigm. Here, we investigate the dynamics of periodically driven optical cavities using a time-dependent cavity-field model with modulated resonance frequencies. We demonstrate modulation-induced tuning of cavity resonances and analyze the resulting intracavity field evolution in both amplitude and phase. The interplay between periodic modulation and cavity dissipation gives rise to pronounced hysteretic behavior, revealing memory effects associated with the finite photon lifetime of the cavity. By quantifying the hysteresis area as a function of modulation frequency, we identify distinct memory resonances characterized by enhanced field-history dependence at specific driving frequencies. Furthermore, we examine the time-resolved local density of optical states (LDOS) and show that temporal modulation enables dynamic spectral redistribution of photonic states, with the degree of confinement governed by the cavity loss rate. Our results establish a simple framework for understanding and engineering memory effects in dynamically driven optical resonators and provide new opportunities for tunable photonic environments, dynamic LDOS control, and reconfigurable light-matter interactions.
tldr: The paper investigates periodically driven optical cavities, revealing modulation-induced memory resonances and dynamic control of the local density of optical states.
motivation: To understand and engineer memory effects in dynamically driven optical resonators for tunable photonic environments and reconfigurable light-matter interactions.
method: A time-dependent cavity-field model with modulated resonance frequencies is used to analyze intracavity field evolution and hysteresis area as a function of modulation frequency.
result: Distinct memory resonances are identified, and temporal modulation enables dynamic spectral redistribution of photonic states, with confinement governed by the cavity loss rate.
conclusion: The work establishes a simple framework for engineering memory effects in optical cavities, offering opportunities for dynamic LDOS control and tunable light-matter interactions.

title: Transformer-Based Characterization Of Criticality In Directed Percolation
authors: Wei Li Bozheng Dou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Directed percolation (DP) provides a canonical framework for studying nonequilibrium phase transitions into absorbing states, yet extracting critical behavior directly from high-dimensional spatiotemporal configurations remains challenging. Here, we investigate (1 + 1)- and (2 + 1)-dimensional bond DP using a supervised Transformer encoder. Supervised learning results demonstrate that the Transformer can distinguish between the active and absorbing phases of directed percolation with high accuracy. The critical point and critical exponents estimated from the model's classification probabilities align closely with reference values from existing literature, indicating that the model not only achieves phase classification but also yields outputs containing information related to critical scaling behavior. To probe the model's internal representation, we employ attention rollout and define an attention center that quantifies the temporal centroid of the cumulative attention distribution. The attention patterns and the attention center reorganize systematically near the critical region and exhibit pronounced finite-size dependence. Finally, we examined the model's transferability between configurations generated from fully occupied initial states and those from single-seed initial states. The results indicate the presence of transferable information between the two types of data, though the transfer performance exhibits directional asymmetry. Furthermore, when using an equal amount of target-domain data, fine-tuning yielded only a marginal improvement in accuracy compared to training from scratch.
tldr: A supervised Transformer encoder is used to classify phases and extract critical behavior in (1+1)- and (2+1)-dimensional directed percolation.
motivation: Directed percolation is a canonical nonequilibrium phase transition into an absorbing state, but extracting critical scaling directly from high-dimensional spatiotemporal configurations remains challenging.
method: The authors train a supervised Transformer on bond directed percolation configurations, estimate critical points and exponents from classification probabilities, and analyze internal representations via attention rollout and an attention-center metric.
result: The Transformer distinguishes active and absorbing phases with high accuracy, yields critical estimates close to literature values, and shows attention patterns reorganizing near criticality with finite-size dependence; transfer between initial-state ensembles is directionally asymmetric.
conclusion: Transformer-based classifiers can capture information about critical scaling in directed percolation, but the work is a classical statistical-physics/ML study and does not address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Conley Index Theory For Asymptotically Autonomous Systems And UV-to-IR Connections
authors: Alireza Behtash, Syo Kamata, Mauricio M. Martinez
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many non-equilibrium systems, such as expanding plasmas, evolve by equations that depend explicitly on time and interpolate between autonomous early-time (UV) and late-time (IR) limits. After time is compactified, fixed points lie on invariant boundary fibers, where the Conley index is one-sided and blind to the UV. For time dependence that admits a [MATH] compactification, we reflect the extended phase space across these fibers. Both sheets of the double run from the UV to the IR, and the UV index reappears, suspended by one degree. Extending one sheet slightly beyond both fibers gives an explicit UV-to-IR transport map between the Conley indices of the limit systems, and its non-vanishing forces connecting solutions. If one block with a fixed strict entrance/exit decomposition serves every frozen system, this map is an isomorphism at every admissible rate. If the block also has nonzero relative homology, the isolated invariant sets of the two limits are connected at every rate. In the Gubser flow of Israel-Stewart theory, the separatrix between two classes of initial data is a transversal connection at every finite relaxation scale [MATH], with splitting [MATH]. In the Bjorken flow at the lowest moment truncation, we prove existence and uniqueness of the attractor solution without regularization. For the three-dimensional Gubser system we construct the global Morse decomposition. In the one-loop flow of the [MATH]-dimensional [MATH] model with cubic anisotropy, a shift of [MATH] through [MATH] has vanishing transport map, but a driven connection and a nonzero connecting homomorphism detect it at every rate.
tldr: The paper develops a Conley index framework for asymptotically autonomous dynamical systems and applies it to UV-to-IR connections in relativistic hydrodynamic flows such as Gubser and Bjorken flows.
motivation: Many non-equilibrium systems interpolate between autonomous early-time UV and late-time IR limits, but standard compactified Conley index methods can be one-sided and blind to the UV limit.
method: The authors reflect the extended phase space across invariant boundary fibers, construct a double-sheet UV-to-IR transport map between Conley indices, and analyze its properties under common block decompositions and nonzero relative homology.
result: They show that nonvanishing transport maps force connecting solutions, prove rate-dependent isomorphism conditions, and apply the framework to Gubser-flow separatrices, Bjorken-flow attractor uniqueness, a three-dimensional Morse decomposition, and a cubic-anisotropy flow.
conclusion: The work provides a topological tool for tracking asymptotic UV-to-IR dynamics in non-equilibrium systems, but it is not directly aligned with quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Fluctuations In Noether's Theorem
authors: J. A. Crosse
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When deriving the expression for the Noether's current one obtains a term that is an integral over the Euler-Lagrange equation. This term vanishes along the classical path and so does not contribute to the current. However, quantum particles do not necessarily follow the classical path; this concept is the basis of Feynman's path integral quantization formalism. Thus, for a quantum system, the Euler-Lagrange term does not vanish and, hence, corresponds to a quantum fluctuation of the Noether's current owing to the system deviating from the classical path. Here, we compute this quantum fluctuation from Noether's theorem and the path integral formalism. We find that, for a time invariant system, the expression for the quantum fluctuations is give by minus the functional expression for the Hamiltonian, [MATH], evaluated at the distance from the classical path, [MATH]. As an example we evaluate quantum energy fluctuations of a single Harmonic oscillator. In the short time limit we recover the energy-time uncertainty relation and in the long time limit we recover the zero point energy of the quantum harmonic oscillator.
tldr: The paper derives quantum fluctuations of Noether's current using the path integral formalism, showing they correspond to the Hamiltonian evaluated at deviations from the classical path.
motivation: To understand quantum corrections to Noether's theorem arising from path integral deviations from classical trajectories.
method: Path integral quantization and functional differentiation of the action, focusing on the Euler-Lagrange term that vanishes classically.
result: For time-invariant systems, the quantum fluctuation equals minus the Hamiltonian evaluated at the distance from the classical path; for a harmonic oscillator, it recovers the energy-time uncertainty relation and zero-point energy.
conclusion: Quantum fluctuations modify Noether's current, with implications for fundamental quantum mechanics and the interpretation of conservation laws.

title: Enhanced Informed Dynamic Bp Decoding Scheduling Strategies For 5g Nr Ldpc Codes
authors: Tofar C. -Y. Chang, I-Hsiang Lee, Pin-Han Wang, Jian-Jia Weng, Yu T. Su
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an enhanced informed dynamic scheduling (IDS) strategy to avoid propagations of unreliable messages in the residual belief-propagation (RBP) algorithm for decoding low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. To reduce the resource needed for updating the degree-one variable nodes (VNs) in an RBP-based algorithm for decoding 5G New Radio (NR) LDPC codes, we further introduce a process consisting of several simple procedures for managing the resource consumption. Simulation results demonstrate that our RBP algorithm based on the Proposed IDS strategy outperforms existing RBP-based algorithms at the early decoding iterations. By using our degree-one VN resource managing approach, the performance of both the proposed and the existing decoders is significantly improved in decoding the 5G NR codes.
tldr: This paper proposes an enhanced informed dynamic scheduling strategy for residual belief-propagation decoding of 5G NR LDPC codes, including a resource-management scheme for degree-one variable nodes.
motivation: Residual belief propagation suffers from propagation of unreliable messages and from high resource cost when updating degree-one variable nodes in 5G NR LDPC codes.
method: The authors design an informed dynamic scheduling rule that suppresses unreliable message propagation, plus a set of simple procedures to manage the computational resources consumed by degree-one variable-node updates.
result: Simulations show the proposed RBP-IDS decoder outperforms existing RBP-based decoders in early decoding iterations, and the degree-one resource-management approach improves performance for both the proposed and existing decoders on 5G NR codes.
conclusion: The scheduling and resource-management enhancements yield faster convergence and better decoding performance for classical 5G LDPC codes.

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Annealing For Protein Side-Chain Optimization: A Feasibility Study
authors: Valeria B. C. Visani, Simone Reale, Alfonso Gautieri, Elisabetta Di Nitto
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical annealing solvers are moving from research laboratories toward industrial use, but their advantage over classical optimization appears to be confined to a narrow class of problems. A recent systematic benchmark of the D-Wave hybrid solver against industry-leading classical solvers, across several classes of optimization problems, found it to be most competitive on binary quadratic programs, while noting that few industrial problems take this form. Therefore, identifying real-world industrial problems that can be modeled with this structure is a key challenge. We propose protein side-chain optimization, a core step of computational protein design, as one of these problems: it is natively a binary quadratic program, and its application context requires pools of low-energy solutions, which annealers naturally return. In this feasibility study, we test whether the competitiveness of the hybrid solver against industry-leading classical solvers extends to this problem. On 40 instances derived from 20 experimentally determined protein structures with up to about 200 amino acids and 2000 binary variables, we compare the results achieved with a hybrid solver, run for 5 seconds, against those of the commercial solver Gurobi, run for 10 seconds, 1000 seconds, and 4 hours. The hybrid solver reaches the certified optimum whenever one is available, matches Gurobi's performance on smaller instances, and outperforms it on larger instances, finding lower-energy solutions. These results show that the competitiveness of the hybrid solver on binary quadratic programs, so far observed only on a synthetic benchmark, extends to a real-world problem. This motivates comparisons with classical heuristics specific to protein side-chain optimization.
tldr: A feasibility study benchmarks D-Wave's hybrid quantum-classical annealer against Gurobi on protein side-chain optimization formulated as a binary quadratic program.
motivation: Hybrid quantum-classical annealers have shown competitiveness mainly on synthetic binary quadratic programs, so the authors seek a real industrial problem with this native structure.
method: They model protein side-chain optimization as a binary quadratic program and compare a 5-second hybrid annealer run against Gurobi runs of 10, 1000, and 14400 seconds on 40 instances from 20 protein structures with up to ~2000 binary variables.
result: The hybrid solver reaches certified optima when available, matches Gurobi on smaller instances, and finds lower-energy solutions on larger instances.
conclusion: The hybrid annealer's competitiveness on binary quadratic programs extends to a real-world protein design problem, motivating comparison with domain-specific classical heuristics.

title: Symmetry Breaking Over Multiway Channels
authors: Raymond Zhang, Richard Combes, Sheng Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identical users running the same algorithm must often break their symmetry and agree on distinct roles, as in leader election, naming, and resource allocation. We study anonymous symmetry breaking over a discrete memoryless multiway channel invariant under permutations of its [MATH] users: each user observes only a private output and must choose a number in [MATH], and the symmetry is broken if the [MATH] numbers are distinct. Using a R\'enyi change of measure, we derive a finite-blocklength converse on the error probability of every symmetric causal protocol, including adaptive and randomized ones. For achievability, block coding with random names reduces the problem to all-source multicast, for which we derive a Gallager random-coding exponent for every fixed [MATH], and a cut-set bound that limits the exponent of the probability that two names coincide or are decoded wrongly. Interactive role controllers instead let the users contend for identifiers directly: we give their exact error probability, an achievable exponent given by a spectral radius when some outputs certify a role, and a floor for finite-state controllers when every output has positive probability, and we introduce generalized musical chairs. On a noisy bandit channel motivated by multiplayer multi-armed bandits, with noiseless collisions and arms of a common mean below one, interactive schemes provably exceed the limit of name decoding, and numerical estimates suggest the same with noisy collisions. For two users, noiseless collisions, one informative arm and a silent arm, the optimal error probability is determined up to a factor of two.
tldr: The paper studies anonymous symmetry breaking among users communicating over a permutation-invariant discrete memoryless multiway channel, deriving finite-blocklength converses and achievable exponents for symmetric causal protocols.
motivation: Users running identical algorithms often need to break symmetry and adopt distinct roles, as in leader election, naming, and resource allocation, but the fundamental limits of doing so over noisy multiway channels are not well understood.
method: The authors use a Rényi change of measure to prove a finite-blocklength converse for all symmetric causal protocols, including adaptive and randomized ones; for achievability they analyze block coding with random names via all-source multicast, Gallager random-coding exponents, cut-set bounds, and interactive role controllers.
result: They obtain converse and achievability bounds, exact error probabilities for interactive controllers, spectral-radius achievable exponents, finite-state controller floors, and show interactive schemes can outperform name decoding on a noisy bandit channel; for a two-user case the optimal error probability is determined up to a factor of two.
conclusion: The work provides an information-theoretic characterization of symmetry breaking over multiway channels, highlighting the power of interactive protocols and leaving gaps such as closing the two-user constant-factor gap and understanding noisy collisions.

title: Capacity Of Generic Symmetric Distributed Linear Computation: The Geometry Of Relations
authors: Hua Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In distributed linear computation, [MATH] users observe linear functions of common finite-field data and send separate messages to a server that wants another linear function. We characterize the generic capacity [MATH], the minimum total number of field symbols sent per computed instance, when all observations and the demand have dimension [MATH], the data have dimension [MATH], and the coefficients of these linear functions are drawn independently and uniformly from the field and stay fixed during coding, with the field size growing through arbitrary prime powers. For fixed [MATH], [MATH] depends only on [MATH]: the curve has finitely many linear pieces for at most three users, infinitely many pieces approaching one value of [MATH] for four users, and a rational part between two sequences of linear pieces for five or more users. The geometry of the relation space, formed by the linear relations among the observations and the demand, determines three things: the shape of the curve, which relations the coding scheme aligns, and the entropy inequalities used in the converse. Generically, the user subspaces of this space are either balanced, where the capacity lies on a single rational curve, or split into two balanced components, a sparse and a dense one, which produces the linear pieces. Achievability uses asymptotic set alignment, in which monomial precoders confine the combined observation differences to a small set. The converse uses the same geometry to lower-bound the sum of the users' remaining observation entropies in terms of the remaining data entropy.
tldr: The paper characterizes the generic capacity of symmetric distributed linear computation over finite fields using the geometry of linear relations among observations and demand.
motivation: Distributed linear computation involves users sending messages to a server that wants a linear function of common data, and its fundamental communication limits are not fully understood in the generic symmetric setting.
method: The authors analyze the relation space formed by linear relations among observations and the demand, classify user subspaces as balanced or split, and combine asymptotic set alignment for achievability with entropy inequalities for the converse.
result: For fixed observation/demand dimension, the generic capacity depends only on the data dimension, yielding finitely many linear pieces for up to three users, infinitely many pieces approaching one value for four users, and a rational part between two sequences of linear pieces for five or more users.
conclusion: The geometry of the relation space determines the capacity curve shape, which relations a coding scheme aligns, and the entropy inequalities needed for the converse.

title: Constructing Casimirs For The Quantum Reflection Equation
authors: Erik Brodsky, Leonid O Chekhov, Quanyu Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore the quantum reflection equation in the case of a full-dimensional [MATH] matrix [MATH]. Using the technique of [MATH]-determinants, we find closed expressions for the quantum Pfaffian (in the case of even [MATH]) and for new quantum Casimirs that are ratios of special quantum (Sklyanin) minors of [MATH]. Special attention is paid to the self-adjointness property of the newly constructed Casimirs. We put forward a conjecture that, adopting a natural ansatz for a quantum deformation of a Casimir of a classical algebra, self-adjointness implies commutativity. We also explore the relationship to networks of quantum cluster variables.
tldr: This paper constructs quantum Casimirs and quantum Pfaffians for the quantum reflection equation using q-determinant techniques and studies their self-adjointness and relation to quantum cluster variables.
motivation: The work aims to extend algebraic structures of quantum integrable systems by finding closed expressions for Casimir-like invariants associated with the quantum reflection equation for full-dimensional matrices.
method: The authors use q-determinants and Sklyanin minors to derive closed formulas for quantum Pfaffians and new quantum Casimirs, and analyze self-adjointness properties; they also conjecture a link between self-adjointness and commutativity.
result: Closed expressions are obtained for the quantum Pfaffian for even M and for quantum Casimirs expressed as ratios of special quantum minors, with a conjectured self-adjointness-commutativity relationship and connections to quantum cluster variable networks.
conclusion: The paper provides new algebraic constructions in quantum integrable systems, but its focus is mathematical and not directly aligned with quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Differential Chiral Sensing At Exceptional Points In Intrinsically Chiral Metastructures
authors: Suzit Hasan Nayem, Zhanni Wu, Mariusz Drong, Kamyar Behrouzi, Boubacar Kant\'e
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discriminating opposite enantiomers through their weak chiroptical responses remains a fundamental challenge in optical sensing. Exceptional points (EPs), non-Hermitian singularities at which eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, offer a route to enhanced spectral responses through their characteristic square-root eigenvalue splitting. However, their potential for chiral discrimination remains largely unexplored. We demonstrate exceptional points in an intrinsically chiral hybrid metamaterial and reveal strongly asymmetric responses to enantiomeric perturbations. The interplay between intrinsic chirality and non-Hermitian degeneracy is realized through the coupling of a chiral plasmonic nanoantenna array to a photonic crystal slab. We observe characteristic complex-square-root scaling, with both resonance frequencies and loss-rates exhibiting pronounced handedness dependence. Remarkably, opposite enantiomers produce complex mode splittings that differ by more than an order of magnitude. Our findings establish intrinsic chirality as a new degree of freedom in non-Hermitian physics and reveal a fundamental route toward topological singularities enhanced discrimination of chiral matter.
tldr: The authors demonstrate exceptional points in an intrinsically chiral plasmonic-photonic metamaterial and exploit the square-root mode splitting to achieve strong enantioselective discrimination of opposite chiral molecules.
motivation: Chiral discrimination is difficult because chiroptical responses of enantiomers are extremely weak; exceptional points in non-Hermitian systems can amplify small perturbations via square-root eigenvalue splitting, but this enhancement mechanism had not been applied to intrinsic chirality.
method: A chiral plasmonic nanoantenna array is coupled to a photonic crystal slab to realize a non-Hermitian degeneracy, and the complex eigenfrequency response to enantiomeric perturbations is measured and analyzed for both handednesses.
result: The system exhibits characteristic complex square-root scaling of resonance frequencies and loss rates, with opposite enantiomers producing complex mode splittings differing by more than an order of magnitude.
conclusion: Intrinsic chirality is established as a degree of freedom in non-Hermitian photonics, offering a route to topologically enhanced chiral sensing and discrimination of chiral matter.

title: Resolvent-Diagonal Energy Of Isospectral Jacobi Matrices
authors: Martin Tak\'a\v{c} Dmitry Pasechnyuk-Vilensky
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the minimum squared resolvent diagonal among Jacobi matrices with prescribed eigenvalues. For the zeros of [MATH], we construct a canonical realization and bound its asymptotic cost against the optimum. Its rescaled inverse converges to the Green operator of a reflection-symmetric singular Schr\"odinger operator with Bessel-zero spectrum. A Green-coordinate identity places this construction and all finite realizations in the same density framework. Mass-constrained spectral problems then give computable lower bounds. The bounds meet at [MATH], with optimal energy [MATH], and have first-order contact with derivative [MATH]. We classify the constrained extremal profiles and the three endpoint geometries of the canonical density. Two polynomial families with the same limiting edge spectrum have different limiting optimal energies. For Nesterov momentum [MATH], the optimal leading endpoint Hessian-drift gain among nonnegative-link Jacobi realizations is [MATH] times the original gain. An explicit isospectral flow strictly improves the standard one-sided realization for [MATH], [MATH].
tldr: The paper studies the minimum squared resolvent diagonal (energy) over isospectral Jacobi matrices with prescribed eigenvalues, constructing canonical realizations and asymptotically tight bounds.
motivation: Motivated by spectral optimization problems for Jacobi matrices, including connections to Nesterov momentum acceleration, the authors seek optimal realizations (densities) among isospectral matrices.
method: They build a canonical realization for zeros of a special function, show its rescaled inverse converges to the Green operator of a reflection-symmetric singular Schrödinger operator, and use a Green-coordinate identity plus mass-constrained spectral problems to derive computable lower bounds.
result: Lower and upper bounds coincide at a specific optimal energy with matching first derivative; they classify extremal profiles and three endpoint geometries, exhibit two polynomial families with identical limiting edge spectrum but different limiting optimal energies, and bound the endpoint Hessian-drift gain for Nesterov momentum.
conclusion: The work provides a density-framework characterization of optimal isospectral Jacobi realizations and explicit isospectral flows that improve on standard one-sided realizations, with applications to momentum optimization.

title: Composition Theorem For Randomized Query Complexity
authors: Supartha Podder Samruddhi Pednekar
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For bounded-error randomized query complexity, we resolve the composition conjecture up to logarithmic factors. The general upper bound [MATH] was already known. Although Meiburg recently disproved constant-factor multiplicative composition for total Boolean functions, the conjecture allowing polylogarithmic losses remained open. We settle this question by proving that, for all (possibly partial) Boolean functions [MATH] and [MATH], \[ R(f\circ g) = \Omega\!\left({\log(n+1)}\right), \] where [MATH] is the input size for [MATH].
tldr: The paper resolves the randomized query complexity composition conjecture up to polylogarithmic factors for all Boolean functions, including partial functions.
motivation: Composition of query complexity is a fundamental question in theoretical computer science, and the multiplicative composition conjecture for randomized query complexity had remained open with polylogarithmic losses allowed.
method: The authors prove a lower bound showing that the randomized query complexity of a composed function f∘g is at least logarithmic in the input size of g, up to constant factors, for all Boolean functions f and g.
result: They establish R(f∘g) = Ω(log(n+1)) where n is the input size for g, settling the composition question up to logarithmic factors.
conclusion: This work advances classical randomized query complexity theory, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Efficient Spintronic Stochastic In-Sensor Computing Modules
authors: Abdolah Amirany, Hamidreza Imani, Samuel Farid, Tarek El-Ghazawi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In-sensor processing (ISP) is used in various fields, including autonomous driving automotive systems, wearable healthcare devices, environmental monitoring, wireless sensor networks, smart cities, and industrial control systems. One of the main features of most of these applications is energy and hardware restriction. This restriction amplifies the importance of using high-performance and low-energy consumption computing systems and methods. This paper proposes efficient spintronic stochastic computing modules for in-sensor computing systems to address this challenge. The proposed design utilized the stochastic behavior of the magnetic tunnel junction in the subcritical switching regime to generate a probability-adjustable random stream. Probability-adjustable random stream generation is the most important step in any stochastic system because it determines the quality of the final output. The simulation results indicate that the proposed design offers almost the same peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity while occupying at least 62\% lower area and consuming 60\% lower energy. These advantages made the proposed design a good choice for ISP applications with limited energy.
tldr: The paper proposes spintronic stochastic computing modules that exploit subcritical magnetic tunnel junction switching to generate probability-tunable random bitstreams for energy-constrained in-sensor processing.
motivation: In-sensor processing for autonomous driving, wearables, and sensor networks is limited by area and energy budgets, motivating low-power hardware random number generation for stochastic computing.
method: Magnetic tunnel junctions biased in the subcritical switching regime are used as tunable random-stream generators, which are then integrated into stochastic in-sensor computing modules and evaluated via simulation.
result: The design achieves comparable PSNR and SSIM to baselines while reducing area by at least 62% and energy consumption by about 60%.
conclusion: Spintronic stochastic generators offer a compact, low-energy alternative for stochastic in-sensor computing, though the work is a classical hardware/device engineering contribution.

title: Gain-Dependent Entropy Characterization Of A Zener Avalanche Noise Trng Via Dual Nist Standards: Toward Low-Cost Hardware Entropy For Ics Deployments
authors: Rishabh Das
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: True random number generators based on Zener avalanche noise offer a low-cost entropy source for industrial control system and IoT edge devices, yet the relationship between amplifier gain, coupling capacitance, and entropy quality remains uncharacterized under current NIST standards. This paper presents a comprehensive entropy assessment of an op-amp-based Zener avalanche noise generator across five gain configurations and two coupling capacitor values, evaluated against the NIST SP 800-22 statistical test suite and the SP~800-90B entropy source assessment using 1.44 billion raw bits per configuration. We identify a three-phase autocorrelation structure, attributed to comparator saturation-recovery dynamics, consistent across all gain settings. A direct-current substitution experiment, replacing the Zener diode with a stable voltage source at the same bias point, reduces switching activity by approximately 97%, confirming that Zener avalanche noise, rather than amplifier self-excitation, is the necessary entropy source. The coupling capacitor is further shown to govern comparator overdrive and entropy quality independent of this source mechanism, with the smaller capacitance improving entropy, throughput, and bias. The combined results identify an optimal gain configuration achieving a perfect statistical test score, NIST-compliant min-entropy, and peak entropy throughput at a bill-of-materials cost under five dollars, offering practical design guidance for low-cost entropy sources in industrial and embedded deployments.
tldr: This paper characterizes a low-cost Zener avalanche-noise true random number generator across gain and coupling-capacitance settings using NIST SP 800-22 and SP 800-90B.
motivation: Zener avalanche noise is attractive as a cheap entropy source for embedded and industrial systems, but the dependence of entropy quality on amplifier gain and coupling capacitance is not well characterized under current NIST standards.
method: The author tests an op-amp-based Zener avalanche noise generator over five gain configurations and two coupling capacitor values, analyzing 1.44 billion raw bits per configuration with NIST SP 800-22 and SP 800-90B; a DC substitution experiment isolates the contribution of Zener avalanche noise.
result: A three-phase autocorrelation structure is observed across gain settings, DC substitution reduces switching activity by about 97%, and a smaller coupling capacitor improves entropy, throughput, and bias; an optimal gain configuration achieves a perfect statistical test score and NIST-compliant min-entropy.
conclusion: The work provides practical design guidance for sub-$5 hardware entropy sources in industrial and embedded deployments, but it is an applied classical hardware-randomness study rather than a quantum information or quantum thermodynamics contribution.

title: Deterministic Factorization Of Constant Depth Circuits From Whitebox Pit
authors: Somnath Bhattacharjee, Mrinal Kumar, Shanthanu S. Rai, Varun Ramanathan, Ramprasad Saptharishi, Shubhangi Saraf
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that over the field of rational numbers, there is a deterministic algorithm for factorization of constant depth circuits that makes calls to a (whitebox or blackbox) PIT algorithm for such circuits. The time complexity of the algorithm (and hence the number of calls to the PIT oracle) is polynomially bounded in the size and degree of the input circuit. Our reduction to PIT is fairly simple and general and applies as it is to other natural classes of algebraic circuits like formulas and algebraic branching programs. Prior to this work, the known deterministic factorization algorithms for constant depth circuits crucially relied on PIT [Bhattacharjee et al.]. Our main technical ingredient is an efficient, deterministic algorithm that, when given access to sufficiently high degree truncations of the power series roots of a constant depth circuit, uses oracle calls to any (whitebox or blackbox) PIT algorithm for these circuits, and partitions the roots into the sets of conjugates; thereby identifying the irreducible factors. For our proof, we rely on a root recombination criterion using logarithmic derivatives [Sasaki et al., Bostan et al., Lecerf] and show that this criterion can be efficiently and deterministically implemented for power series roots of constant depth circuits using access to any PIT oracle. On the way, we discuss an algorithm that may be of independent interest: it takes as input a matrix whose entries are multivariate constant depth circuits over a field [MATH], requires oracle access to any PIT algorithm for these circuits and outputs a basis for the [MATH]-kernel of this matrix in polynomial time.
tldr: A deterministic polynomial-time algorithm is given for factoring constant-depth algebraic circuits over the rationals, assuming oracle access to a polynomial identity testing (PIT) algorithm for such circuits.
motivation: Prior deterministic factorization algorithms for constant-depth circuits relied crucially on PIT, so the authors aim to give a clean, general reduction from factorization to PIT that also covers formulas and algebraic branching programs.
method: The core technical ingredient is a deterministic algorithm that, given sufficiently high-degree truncations of the power series roots of a constant-depth circuit and oracle access to PIT, partitions roots into conjugate sets using a root-recombination criterion based on logarithmic derivatives; a PIT-oracle algorithm for computing a basis of the kernel of a matrix of circuits is also developed.
result: Factorization of constant-depth circuits reduces deterministically to polynomially many PIT oracle calls, with time polynomial in circuit size and degree, and the reduction extends directly to formulas and algebraic branching programs.
conclusion: The work yields a simple and general PIT-based reduction for algebraic factorization, clarifying the relationship between factoring and identity testing in algebraic complexity.

title: Permutation Order Governs Basin Entropy In Critical One-input Boolean Networks
authors: Ruodan Liu, Ahana Ghosh, Sean Campbell, Venkata Sai Narayana Bavisetty, Matthew Wheeler, Claus Kadelka
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Basin entropy measures uncertainty about a network's long-term behavior. For every critical one-input synchronous Boolean network with [MATH] relevant nodes, we show that the permutation structure induced by its feedback loops determines basin entropy, up to a universal error. Although the loops oscillate independently, their relative phases can be offset, producing a deviation from additivity that can grow linearly in [MATH]. Yet at the ensemble level, a previously derived additive prediction is preserved through the first subleading term, with the discrepancy appearing at order [MATH].
tldr: The paper shows that permutation structure from feedback loops determines basin entropy in critical one-input synchronous Boolean networks up to a universal error, with ensemble-level additive behavior preserved to subleading order.
motivation: Basin entropy quantifies uncertainty in the long-term behavior of Boolean networks, and understanding how network structure controls it is relevant for complex dynamical systems.
method: The authors analyze critical one-input synchronous Boolean networks with M relevant nodes and relate basin entropy to the permutation structure induced by feedback loops, including phase-offset effects and ensemble averaging.
result: Loop phases can create non-additive deviations that grow linearly in M, but the previously derived additive prediction remains valid at the ensemble level through the first subleading term, with discrepancies appearing at higher order.
conclusion: Permutation order is a governing structural determinant of basin entropy in this class of Boolean networks, refining additive predictions with a controlled error and higher-order ensemble corrections.

title: Interacting Particles Crossing Barriers: Spatial Statistics, Choice Of Route Taken And Role Of Interactions
authors: Gulzar Ahmad, Andrew J Archer, Sergey Savel'ev, Marco G Mazza
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the statistics of pairs of particles moving in a potential energy landscape exhibiting a choice of different pathways from a local minimum start point to the global energy minimum destination. We examine the impact of both attractive and repulsive interactions between the particles, treating these via either a soft Gaussian or a Lennard-Jones potential. We investigate the statistics of which particle arrives at the destination first, arrival-time distributions and where in the system the second particle is located when the first arrives. We find that the typical arrival time of the first particle can be significantly different to that of a single particle, sometimes being much longer and in other cases being shorter, depending on the nature of the particle interactions. In the case of soft Gaussian attractive interactions, which effectively bind the pair of particles together to form a single larger particle, the arrival time can be much longer, since bigger particles cross barriers more slowly. In contrast, the arrival time is shorter when there is a repulsive core interaction between the particles, due to excluded-area and particle-ordering effects. We investigate the probability distribution of particles' positions through the Jensen--Shannon divergence which unveils the dependence of the spatial distribution of the particles within the confining potential on the parameters of the particle interaction potentials.
tldr: The paper studies classical interacting particle pairs crossing a potential landscape with multiple pathways, analyzing arrival-order statistics, arrival-time distributions, and spatial distributions via Jensen-Shannon divergence.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how attractive versus repulsive interactions affect which particle reaches a target first, how long it takes, and where the other particle is located when arrival occurs.
method: They model particle pairs moving in a potential energy landscape with competing pathways, using soft Gaussian and Lennard-Jones interaction potentials, and quantify spatial statistics with the Jensen-Shannon divergence.
result: Attractive soft Gaussian interactions can bind particles and slow barrier crossing, while repulsive-core interactions can speed up arrival due to excluded-area and ordering effects; arrival-time and spatial distributions depend strongly on interaction parameters.
conclusion: Interparticle interactions qualitatively and quantitatively alter route-choice statistics and arrival behavior in barrier-crossing landscapes, with implications for classical stochastic transport and spatial distribution analysis.

title: Talanov Dynamics And Chirp-controlled Rogue-wave Formation For The Vector Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equation
authors: G. Ortenzi, G. Roberti, M. Sommacal
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the focusing vector nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, or Manakov system, for a pair of coupled initial conditions with compactly supported, concave parabolic density profiles and phases depending quadratically on the spatial coordinate. We focus on the natural class of self-similar solutions generated by such profiles, whose dispersionless evolution we refer to as Talanov dynamics. We extend the criterion for blow-up in finite time, first established for a single field, to the Manakov case. For arbitrary initial chirps in the two fields, we provide closed-form expressions for their evolution, and an explicit expression for the time of the gradient catastrophe, if it occurs, and we classify the effect of the coupling on the catastrophe. Depending on the initial chirps, the two fields may catastrophise, or relax, as each would if decoupled. However, coupling can also force the catastrophe in fields that would otherwise relax if decoupled. For identical initial supports, and in the presence of dispersion, we numerically show that the same dispersionless criterion determines, in the semiclassical regime, whether the fully dispersive solution relaxes or develops a rogue wave in each field, whose onset time is accurately predicted by the corresponding dispersionless catastrophe time, in direct analogy with the scalar case. As chirp and amplitude are relatively easy to control experimentally, we expect these results to be relevant to experiments in nonlinear optics and Bose-Einstein condensates, extending to coupled systems observations made for the scalar equation.
tldr: The paper analyzes self-similar Talanov dynamics and chirp-controlled gradient catastrophes in the focusing vector nonlinear Schrödinger/Manakov system, linking dispersionless blow-up criteria to rogue-wave formation in the semiclassical regime.
motivation: The authors aim to extend scalar Talanov-type blow-up and rogue-wave criteria to coupled Manakov systems, where the effect of inter-field coupling on finite-time catastrophe is not fully understood.
method: They consider coupled initial conditions with compactly supported concave parabolic densities and quadratic phases, derive closed-form self-similar evolution and gradient-catastrophe times for arbitrary chirps, and numerically compare dispersionless predictions with fully dispersive dynamics.
result: They classify when coupling forces, prevents, or preserves catastrophe depending on initial chirps, and show that in the semiclassical regime the dispersionless criterion predicts whether each field relaxes or forms a rogue wave, with accurate onset times.
conclusion: The results extend scalar Talanov dynamics to vector NLS/Manakov systems and suggest experimental relevance for nonlinear optics and Bose-Einstein condensates where chirp and amplitude are controllable.

title: Stability Of Large Dynamical Systems Using Gershgorin Disc Theorem
authors: Chandrakala Meena Yuvrajsingh Pravinsingh Patil
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the stability of large nonlinear dynamical systems is a fundamental problem in many fields, including biological, technological, and social networks. Traditional stability methods often rely on explicit eigenvalue calculations or the construction of Lyapunov functions, which become computationally difficult for large interconnected systems. In this work, we introduce a stability classifier that provides a computationally efficient way to determine the stability of complex systems without performing full spectral analysis. Our approach combines the Dynamical Jacobian Ensemble framework, which uses the network structure and the underlying dynamics to construct a Jacobian, with the Gershgorin disc theorem, which provides bounds on the eigenvalues of the system's Jacobian matrix. Using this combination, we derive an analytical classifier that predicts whether a dynamical system is asymptotically stable, unstable, or sensitively stable based on a small set of dynamical and network parameters. The analysis reveals that the stability of large dynamical systems is strongly influenced by highly connected hub nodes. This observation allows the stability condition to be simplified by focusing on the contribution of the hub-associated Gershgorin disc. Extensive numerical simulations on large ensembles of Jacobian matrices confirm that the proposed classifier accurately separates stable, unstable, and sensitively stable regimes across a wide range of dynamical parameters and network structures. The resulting framework provides a simple and scalable tool for predicting the stability of large dynamical networks while capturing the interplay between network topology and interaction dynamics.
tldr: The paper introduces an analytical stability classifier for large nonlinear dynamical networks by combining the Dynamical Jacobian Ensemble framework with the Gershgorin disc theorem, avoiding full spectral analysis.
motivation: Determining stability of large interconnected nonlinear systems via explicit eigenvalue computation or Lyapunov function construction is computationally prohibitive, motivating a scalable spectral-bound approach.
method: The authors build a Jacobian from network structure and local dynamics (Dynamical Jacobian Ensemble), then apply Gershgorin disc bounds on eigenvalues to derive a classifier separating asymptotically stable, unstable, and sensitively stable regimes from a few dynamical and topological parameters.
result: Hub nodes with high connectivity dominate the stability condition, allowing the criterion to be reduced to a single hub-associated Gershgorin disc; extensive numerical simulations confirm accurate regime classification across varied parameters and network topologies.
conclusion: The framework offers a simple, scalable tool for predicting stability of large dynamical networks while linking topology and interaction dynamics, though it remains a classical network-dynamics result.

title: Sensing-Based Communication: A Non-Orthogonal Passive Reflection Framework For Isac
authors: Xin Xiong, Mathew Salas, Sihua Shao, Chen Chen, Mostafa Hassanalian, Rafael Fierro
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While integrating uplink without disrupting the primary downlink remains a critical challenge for existing reflective communication systems, this paper proposes a non-orthogonal passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) mechanism termed Sensing-based Communication. Originating from and validated within an optical retro-reflective system, this mechanism possesses an underlying wave-agnostic architecture with the potential to be generalized across other physical modalities. It leverages incident downlink signals for parasitic modulation via passive tags. By relying solely on fundamental on-off keying (OOK) reflection, the tag unifies the reflective sensing channel and the uplink communication channel, and simultaneously achieves both sensing and duplex communication. Consequently, our approach introduces uplink capability without sacrificing the downlink data rate or consuming additional spectrum resources. At the receiver, we design a joint decoding architecture combining cross-correlation computation and successive interference cancelation (SIC) to fully exploit the degrees of freedom in broadband signals for multi-user interference suppression. We derive closed-form expressions for the interference and bit error rate (BER) assuming zero-mean Gaussian signals. Using an experimental testbed, we validate the pivotal theoretical finding, the scaling relationship of SINR with signal bandwidth and cross-correlation time--where linear regression yields a strong goodness-of-fit with [MATH]. Furthermore, evaluations under noise-like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms exhibit high consistency between theoretical derivations and simulation data ([MATH], mean absolute percentage error, [MATH]), confirming the model's accuracy and waveform generalizability.
tldr: The paper proposes a non-orthogonal passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) scheme in which a retro-reflective tag parasitically modulates an incident downlink signal with on-off keying to add an uplink without extra spectrum.
motivation: Existing reflective communication systems struggle to add an uplink without disrupting the primary downlink or consuming additional spectral resources.
method: A wave-agnostic, optically validated architecture uses passive OOK retro-reflection to unify the sensing and uplink channels, together with a joint receiver combining cross-correlation and successive interference cancellation; closed-form interference and BER expressions are derived and validated on an experimental testbed.
result: Experiments confirm the predicted SINR scaling with signal bandwidth and cross-correlation time (strong linear-regression fit), and OFDM waveform simulations agree closely with theory (low mean absolute percentage error).
conclusion: Sensing-based communication enables simultaneous sensing and duplex communication without sacrificing downlink rate or spectrum, with a model claimed to generalize across physical modalities.

title: Kam Theory For Quasi-periodic Equilibrium Of Generalized Frenkel-Kontorova Model In $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$
authors: Zuhong You Xiaolong He
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the KAM theory for one dimensional Frenkel-Kontorova model to multidimensional case in quasi-periodic media. By using the quasi-Newton method, we reduce the linearized operator with quasi-periodic coefficient in the Nash-Moser iteration to the composition of two diagonal operators and a near-identity operator, such that the small divisor problem can be overcome by imposing the simultaneous Diophantine condition. In contrast, we also discuss the application of Craig-Wayne-Bourgain method to the quasi-periodic equilibrium problem.
tldr: The paper extends KAM theory for the Frenkel-Kontorova model to multidimensional quasi-periodic media using a quasi-Newton Nash-Moser scheme.
motivation: The authors aim to overcome small-divisor problems in quasi-periodic equilibrium problems beyond the one-dimensional Frenkel-Kontorova setting.
method: They reduce the linearized operator with quasi-periodic coefficients to two diagonal operators plus a near-identity operator and impose a simultaneous Diophantine condition; they also compare the Craig-Wayne-Bourgain approach.
result: The construction provides a KAM-type proof of quasi-periodic equilibria for the generalized multidimensional Frenkel-Kontorova model under Diophantine conditions.
conclusion: The work advances mathematical KAM theory for quasi-periodic media but has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Schur Products Of Some Nonbinary Narrow-sense Antiprimitive Bch Codes
authors: Haojie Xu, Xia Wu, Wei Lu, Xiwang Cao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, the Schur products of linear codes have been extensively studied due to their favorable applications in cryptography. In this paper, we aim to study the parameters of the Schur products of some nonbinary narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes. Let [MATH] and [MATH] be two narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes with designed distances [MATH] and [MATH], respectively, where [MATH]. Let [MATH] be the Schur product of [MATH] and [MATH]. We present some necessary and sufficient conditions for [MATH] by applying some constraints to [MATH] and [MATH]. Furthermore, we determine the dimensions of these products and lower bounds on their minimum distance. Several linear codes with best known parameters are found.
tldr: This paper studies the Schur products of nonbinary narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes, determining conditions, dimensions, and minimum-distance lower bounds.
motivation: Schur products of linear codes are motivated by applications in cryptography, and the authors aim to characterize their parameters for nonbinary antiprimitive BCH codes.
method: The authors apply constraints to pairs of narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes with specified designed distances to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for their Schur product, then compute dimensions and lower bounds on minimum distance.
result: They identify conditions under which the Schur product has certain parameters and obtain several linear codes with best-known parameters.
conclusion: The work contributes classical coding-theoretic results on Schur products of BCH codes, with potential relevance to code-based cryptography but no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Stabilizing Vector Approximate Message Passing With Circuit-Designed Lag-Lead Damping
authors: Mohamed Akrout
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vector approximate message passing (VAMP) often fails to converge on ill-conditioned matrices, and its damping factor is tuned either manually or adaptively. Using the fact that VAMP iterations are the discretization of an electric circuit, we show that the denoiser and the likelihood act as nonlinear resistors, the Onsager correction is a mirror resistor and damping is a lag filter. This circuit gives a closed-form loop gain whose spectrum can predict when VAMP fails. Because a lag filter cannot isolate the oscillating modes, we add a lead capacitor whose design often results in a negative capacitance. Across a wide range of condition numbers, our proposed damping strategy achieves a higher convergence rate than adaptive damping and Anderson acceleration at a lower mean iteration cost. On ill-conditioned multipath channels, across ranks and sparsity levels, it also converges more reliably than existing damping baselines.
tldr: The paper reinterprets vector approximate message passing (VAMP) iterations as a discretized electrical circuit, using the resulting loop-gain spectrum to design a lead-lag damping scheme that improves convergence on ill-conditioned matrices.
motivation: VAMP frequently diverges on ill-conditioned matrices, and existing fixes—manual tuning, adaptive damping, Anderson acceleration—are heuristic and unreliable, so a principled, predictive criterion for convergence is needed.
method: VAMP is mapped onto an equivalent circuit where denoisers and likelihoods are nonlinear resistors, the Onsager correction is a mirror resistor, and damping is a lag filter; a closed-form loop gain predicts failure, and an added lead capacitor with negative capacitance isolates oscillating modes.
result: Across a wide range of condition numbers the proposed damping strategy achieves higher convergence rates than adaptive damping and Anderson acceleration at lower mean iteration cost, and converges more reliably on ill-conditioned multipath channels across ranks and sparsity levels.
conclusion: Circuit-inspired lead-lag damping provides a principled, closed-form design tool for stabilizing VAMP, outperforming existing damping baselines in both reliability and cost.

title: Twisted Verlinde Formula For Finite Cyclic Orbifolds Of Vertex Operator Algebras
authors: Jiancai Sun Wenbin Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a simple, rational, [MATH]-cofinite and self-dual vertex operator algebra of CFT type, and let [MATH] be a finite cyclic automorphism group of [MATH]. We establish a twisted Verlinde formula for cyclic groups of arbitrary finite order, expressing fusion coefficients among twisted [MATH]-modules in terms of the [MATH]-matrix in the orbifold theory. As an application, we compute fusion rules among twisted modules for the permutation orbifold [MATH] associated with a [MATH]-cycle [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves a twisted Verlinde formula for finite cyclic orbifolds of rational vertex operator algebras and applies it to permutation orbifolds.
motivation: Twisted modules and orbifold fusion rules are central in conformal field theory and vertex operator algebra theory, but a general Verlinde formula for arbitrary finite cyclic twisting had not been established.
method: The authors use the representation theory of vertex operator algebras and orbifold theory to express fusion coefficients among twisted modules via the S-matrix of the orbifold theory.
result: They obtain a twisted Verlinde formula valid for cyclic groups of arbitrary finite order and compute fusion rules among twisted modules for a permutation orbifold associated with a cycle.
conclusion: The work extends Verlinde-type formulas to broader orbifold settings, with explicit applications to permutation orbifolds, but it is a pure mathematics/CFT result with no direct quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems focus.

title: Group Invariance Of Statistical Models And Associated Statistical Manifolds
authors: Zhuohao Cheng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the group invariance of a parameterized statistical model that is closed under push-forward sample transformations given by a group action. We prove that the group action on the sample space induces an isometric action on the associated statistical manifold. Furthermore, it preserves the Fisher-Rao metric as well as the Amari-Chentsov tensor. Moreover, we establish that this isometric action is compatible with equivariant and sufficient statistics in the spirit of the Hall-Wijsman-Ghosh generalized Stein's theorem. This compatibility leads to a novel reduction of the original group-invariant model, where its Fisher information loss is explicitly quantified via conditional expectation. As an application, we apply this framework to a generalized cardioid distribution in circular data analysis, illustrating how the reduced model facilitates estimation and hypothesis testing for relative parameters.
tldr: The paper proves that a group action on a sample space induces an isometric, Fisher-Rao- and Amari-Chentsov-tensor-preserving action on the associated statistical manifold, enabling a symmetry-based reduction of group-invariant parametric models.
motivation: Symmetry in parametric statistical models is known to constrain estimation, but a systematic geometric account of how group actions propagate to statistical manifolds and interact with sufficiency and equivariance is lacking.
method: The authors use information geometry: they lift a group action to the statistical manifold, show preservation of the Fisher-Rao metric and Amari-Chentsov tensor, connect this to a Hall-Wijsman-Ghosh-type generalized Stein theorem for equivariant/sufficient statistics, and quantify Fisher information loss via conditional expectation.
result: The induced action is isometric on the statistical manifold and compatible with equivariant and sufficient statistics, yielding a reduced model with explicitly quantified Fisher information loss; the framework is illustrated on a generalized cardioid distribution for circular data.
conclusion: Group invariance yields a principled geometric model reduction with computable information loss, useful for estimation and hypothesis testing of relative parameters in symmetric models.

title: Seu Hardened Multi-Context Spintronic Fpga
authors: Abdolah Amirany, Hamidreza Imani, Samuel Farid, Tarek El-Ghazawi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Due to susceptibility to radiation-induced soft errors and resource constraints implementing large and complex designs on field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) in harsh environments is challenging.
