Therefore, to mitigate these issues, this paper proposes an innovative approach through the introduction of a single event upset (SEU)-hardened spintronic FPGA architecture that incorporates multi-context capabilities. Leveraging the non-volatile properties of magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ), the proposed design can store two/four distinct configurations internally, eliminating the dependence on external non-volatile memory which significantly boosts the system performance. Additionally, through post-layout simulation, we demonstrate our design immunity to SEU, which enhances its reliability and operational stability in environments susceptible to radiation-induced soft errors. The efficiency of the proposed design was also evaluated using the ROSSETA benchmark, which serves as a representative model for real-world FPGA applications.
tldr: The paper proposes a radiation-hardened (SEU-tolerant) spintronic FPGA architecture using magnetic tunnel junctions that stores two or four configurations internally without external non-volatile memory.
motivation: FPGAs deployed in harsh radiation environments suffer from soft errors and limited resources, so a non-volatile, SEU-immune reconfigurable fabric is needed for reliable operation.
method: The authors design a multi-context spintronic FPGA built on MTJ-based non-volatile storage and evaluate it via post-layout simulation, including SEU immunity analysis and the ROSSETA benchmark for real-world FPGA workloads.
result: Post-layout simulations indicate the design is immune to single-event upsets and achieves improved system performance by eliminating dependence on external non-volatile memory, with efficiency validated on the ROSSETA benchmark.
conclusion: MTJ-based multi-context spintronic FPGAs offer a promising radiation-tolerant, higher-performance reconfiguration platform for harsh-environment electronics.

title: Hardness Of Approximation For Polynomial Optimization Over Sphere For Linear Programming Relaxation Hierarchy
authors: Mrinalkanti Ghosh
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semidefinite programming (SDP), particularly the sum-of-squares (SoS) hierarchy, provides [MATH]-time approximation and certification algorithms for optimizing degree-[MATH] homogeneous polynomials on the unit sphere. For arbitrary inputs, degree-[MATH] SoS gives a powered-objective approximation factor [MATH] [BGGLT17]. For random order-[MATH] tensors, degree-[MATH] SoS has an integrality-gap lower bound of [MATH] relative to the true spherical maximum; lower bounds also extend to growing SoS degree in tensor PCA [BGL17,HKP17]. We establish lower bounds for weaker linear-programming relaxation hierarchies. Our degree-[MATH] moment LPs impose the sphere identities and any prescribed, instance-independent family [MATH] of valid polynomial inequalities of degree at most [MATH]. They include Sherali--Adams-type product hierarchies. For every even [MATH], constant [MATH], and [MATH] satisfying [MATH] and [MATH], every such relaxation with at most [MATH] tests has instances [MATH] satisfying \[ _{q,}(P)}{\|P\|_\infty}\ge }{}\left(\frac nq\right)^{d/2-1/2}.\] Here [MATH] is the maximum absolute value of the polynomial over the sphere and [MATH] is the relaxed objective. The exponent [MATH] improves the leading dependence on [MATH] relative to the [MATH]-type exponents in prior random-tensor SoS lower bounds. Our LP hierarchies impose weaker positivity conditions than semidefinite moment relaxations. It leaves open whether analogous degree dependence can be achieved in lower bounds for SDP hierarchies.
tldr: The paper proves hardness-of-approximation lower bounds for linear-programming relaxation hierarchies applied to polynomial optimization over the sphere.
motivation: Semidefinite sum-of-squares hierarchies achieve strong approximation guarantees for spherical polynomial optimization, but much less is known about weaker linear-programming moment relaxations.
method: The author studies degree-d moment LP hierarchies imposing sphere identities and prescribed valid polynomial inequalities, including Sherali-Adams-type product hierarchies, and constructs instances establishing integrality-gap lower bounds.
result: For a wide range of parameters, the paper shows that any such LP relaxation with a bounded number of tests has instances where the relaxed objective exceeds the true spherical maximum by a factor scaling as (n/q)^{d/2-1/2}.
conclusion: The results demonstrate limitations of LP relaxation hierarchies for spherical polynomial optimization and improve the exponent dependence relative to prior random-tensor SoS lower bounds, while leaving analogous SDP lower bounds open.

title: Attaining Optimal Values Under Sure Constraints
authors: Takuto Yamauchi (waseda University, Institute Of Science Tokyo), Kenji Tei
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A game may have, for each target below its value, a finite controller meeting that target, yet no finite controller attaining the value itself. We study finite stochastic games with a hard specification that must hold on every supported execution, including paths of probability zero. Max uses a pure finite controller; Min may use any pure public-history strategy. We distinguish three numerical questions: can a supplied target be met, can the unspecified optimum be attained, and what is one exact value? For explicit hard and Boolean soft Streett conditions, the strict and non-strict supplied-threshold problems are coNP-complete, attainment of the unsupplied supremum is [MATH]-complete, and one exact reduced fraction is [MATH]-complete under polynomial metric reductions. The proofs preserve both the value and its finite attainability when fixing a single opponent, and encode adaptive queries without computing unknown subgame values. The same construction yields matching value-comparison and exact-output lower bounds for ordinary stochastic Streett games with unrestricted randomized history strategies. We also bound the memory needed for optimal finite implementations for arbitrary Muller hard conditions and rational rewards in [MATH] determined by infinitely recurring states. One controller is sure from the entire original sure region and attains at every finitely attained start, with no attainment premise on the other states. For [MATH] states in that region it uses [MATH] modes, where [MATH] is the product of the least common denominators of full original chance rows sourced in that sure region and [MATH] clears all reward values. Its joint dependence on [MATH] and [MATH] is worst-case sharp at each fixed [MATH] when [MATH]. Optimal dependence on arena size and efficient general synthesis are not resolved here.
tldr: The paper studies finite stochastic games with hard sure constraints, analyzing the complexity of threshold satisfaction, attainment of optimal values, and exact-value computation for Streett and Muller conditions.
motivation: A game may admit finite controllers meeting every target below its value but no finite controller attaining the value itself, motivating a precise complexity-theoretic treatment of sure specifications and optimal controller synthesis.
method: The authors analyze explicit hard and Boolean soft Streett conditions under pure finite Max controllers and arbitrary pure public-history Min strategies, proving complexity results via reductions that preserve value and finite attainability.
result: For Streett conditions, supplied-threshold problems are coNP-complete, unsupplied supremum attainment is complete for a higher complexity class, and exact reduced-fraction output is likewise hard; memory bounds are also derived for optimal finite implementations under Muller hard conditions.
conclusion: The work establishes matching lower bounds for exact-value and comparison problems in stochastic Streett games and provides memory bounds for optimal finite controllers, while leaving optimal dependence on arena size and efficient general synthesis unresolved.

title: Verification Of Security Properties Of Cryptographic Protocols
authors: Joaqu\'in Ezpeleta Simona Bernardi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Developing cryptographic protocols that are free from vulnerabilities is very challenging, as evidenced by numerous design flaws and implementation bugs in widely used protocols. Recent work has leveraged model checking to generate negative test cases, that is test cases that include the behavior of Dolev-Yao attacker. In this paper, we address the problem of analyzing execution traces produced by testing protocol implementations with such negative test cases. We propose a method for detecting violations of security properties by model-checking execution traces. Our approach employs a model checker based on DLTL, a Linear Temporal Logic with freeze operators, and supports automation of the testing process through pre- and post-processing steps. These steps, respectively, bridge the gap between different levels of abstraction and synthesize the results produced by the model checker.We present experimental results as a proof of concept for the feasibility of the proposed method.
tldr: The paper proposes a model-checking method for verifying security properties by analyzing execution traces from testing cryptographic protocol implementations against Dolev-Yao attacker behaviors.
motivation: Cryptographic protocols are difficult to design and implement securely, and negative test cases can reveal vulnerabilities, but analyzing the resulting execution traces requires automated support.
method: The authors use a model checker based on DLTL, a linear temporal logic with freeze operators, together with pre- and post-processing steps to bridge abstraction levels and synthesize model-checker output.
result: Experimental results are presented as a proof of concept demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed trace-analysis and security-property verification method.
conclusion: The approach supports automated detection of security-property violations in protocol implementations, but it is a classical cryptographic verification contribution rather than a quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems result.

title: Performance Bottlenecks In Computing Zk Proofs On A Gpu
authors: Victor Carolino, Caleb Geren, Michael Kaufman, Maximilian Nussbaum, William Scott, Henry F. Korth
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zero-knowledge proofs allow one party to prove the correctness of a statement or execution of a computation while revealing no more than the statement of correctness itself. Recent use cases, such as AI datasets, suggest the need for faster proof generation over increasingly large constraint sets. This paper explores efforts in optimizing zero-knowledge proof generation, specifically PlonK, using GPUs, for applications that are not amenable to solution via incrementally verifiable computing (IVC). Our intention with this work is to improve ZK performance by introducing fundamental changes in the low-level architectural structure of proof generation. These changes affect performance curves for most current proof generation algorithms. In particular, this paper explores the trade-offs between increased parallelization on GPUs and the resultant memory management problems that occur due to this parallelization. We implement a parallelized PlonK in order to analyze these trade-offs and make arguments concerning the nature of data flows within the proving protocol. Our results lead us to consider multi-GPU environments to maximize performance for large circuit sizes. Such environments introduce issues of communication, efficient hardware management, data partition, and data transfers. This paper further discusses the use cases that motivate multi-GPU implementations, their cost models, and the use of remote direct memory access (RDMA) for data transfer among GPUs.
tldr: This paper profiles and optimizes GPU-based PlonK zero-knowledge proof generation, focusing on parallelism/memory trade-offs and multi-GPU designs for large constraint sets.
motivation: Growing applications such as AI dataset verification demand faster zero-knowledge proof generation over very large constraint systems where incrementally verifiable computation is not applicable.
method: The authors implement a parallelized PlonK prover on GPUs, restructure low-level architectural data flows, and analyze the trade-off between increased parallelization and resulting memory management overheads, including multi-GPU partitioning with RDMA transfer.
result: The parallelization gains are increasingly limited by memory management and inter-GPU communication costs, motivating multi-GPU environments with careful data partitioning and RDMA-based transfer for large circuits.
conclusion: Efficient ZK proving at scale requires fundamental restructuring of proving-protocol data flows and multi-GPU architectures, with cost models guiding hardware deployment choices.

title: On Positive Computation
authors: Eduardo Skapinakis
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce new notions of reducibility for monotone classes and show that a monotone version of Circuit Satisfiability and the Hamiltonian Cycle Problem are complete for [MATH], even under positive reductions (which are not the same as monotone reductions). If this holds for all (monotone) [MATH]-complete problems - that they are also so complete for [MATH] -, then [MATH]. We introduce positive models of relativized computation and show that the separation [MATH] does not relativize, even when oracles are restricted to monotone sets. Yet, there is a (weak) diagonalization proof that [MATH].
tldr: The paper introduces positive reductions and positive models of relativized computation to study monotone complexity classes and non-relativizing separations.
motivation: It aims to refine reducibility notions for monotone classes and understand whether completeness and separation results relativize under monotone or positive restrictions.
method: The author defines positive reductions and positive relativized computation models, then analyzes monotone versions of Circuit Satisfiability and Hamiltonian Cycle as complete problems and constructs diagonalization and oracle arguments.
result: Monotone Circuit Satisfiability and Hamiltonian Cycle are shown complete under positive reductions, a conditional implication about all monotone complete problems is given, and a separation is shown not to relativize even with monotone oracles, while a weak diagonalization proof is provided.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical computational complexity and monotone complexity theory, with no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Tensor Value And The 9/4 Bound For Matrix Multiplication
authors: Mahmut Levent Do\u{g}an, Vladimir Lysikov, Keiya Sakabe, Michael Walter
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an exposition of OpenAI's recent result that the exponent of matrix multiplication is at most 9/4 valid over every field. Our main tool is a fractional symmetrized variant of the tensor value introduced by Coppersmith and Winograd, used in place of spectral points (tensor characters) in the original proof. We prove a superadditivity inequality for a power of this value on partially direct sums, whose summands share one tensor factor and occupy independent subspaces in the other two. Together with the degenerations of polynomial multiplication tensors from the OpenAI proof, this inequality yields the bound.
tldr: An exposition of OpenAI's result that the matrix multiplication exponent is at most 9/4 over every field, proved via a fractional symmetrized tensor value.
motivation: The asymptotic exponent of matrix multiplication (ω) is a central open problem in algebraic complexity; recent work lowered the bound to 9/4, and this paper aims to make the proof accessible and self-contained.
method: Introduces a fractional symmetrized variant of the Coppersmith–Winograd tensor value in place of spectral points (tensor characters), and proves a superadditivity inequality for a power of this value on partially direct sums sharing one tensor factor.
result: Combining the superadditivity inequality with degenerations of polynomial multiplication tensors from the OpenAI proof yields the bound ω ≤ 9/4 valid over every field.
conclusion: The tensor-value approach provides a cleaner, field-independent route to the 9/4 bound and may serve as a foundation for further improvements to matrix multiplication exponents.

title: Self-injection-locked Dark-soliton Kerr Optical Frequency Combs With High Even-order Normal Dispersion
authors: Lei Shi, Rujiang Li, Shilong Liu, Dumitru Mihalache, Boris A. Malomed, Pengfei Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We numerically investigate dissipative dark-soliton (DDS) microcombs under the action of pure high even-order normal (HEON) dispersion in a microresonator with the self-injection locking (SIL). Pure 4th, 6th, 10th, and 14th-order normal dispersion can support DDSs formed by interlocked switching waves, directly excited through a SIL-based turnkey scheme without detuning sweeps. Compared to the pure 4th-order case, the switching-wave tail oscillation period increases and its decay rate decreases with the increase of the dispersion order. Although the overall comb bandwidth narrows, the number of non-pump comb lines above a common absolute power threshold increases. Furthermore, the feedback phase controls the DDS duty cycle and intracavity comb-line power distribution, while the increase of the pump power improves the estimated pump-to-comb output conversion efficiency.
tldr: This paper numerically studies self-injection-locked dissipative dark-soliton Kerr microcombs engineered with pure high even-order normal dispersion.
motivation: Turnkey soliton microcombs are attractive for practical frequency-comb generation, and understanding how higher-order normal dispersion affects dark-soliton formation could enable simplified excitation schemes without detuning sweeps.
method: The authors numerically model dissipative dark solitons in a microresonator under pure 4th, 6th, 10th, and 14th-order normal dispersion with self-injection locking, analyzing switching-wave dynamics, comb spectra, feedback phase, and pump power.
result: Dark solitons formed by interlocked switching waves are directly excited without detuning sweeps; increasing dispersion order lengthens switching-wave tail oscillation periods and slows decay, narrows overall comb bandwidth, but increases the number of non-pump comb lines above a common power threshold. Feedback phase controls duty cycle and intracavity power distribution, while higher pump power improves estimated pump-to-comb conversion efficiency.
conclusion: High even-order normal dispersion supports turnkey self-injection-locked dark-soliton microcombs, with dispersion order and feedback phase providing knobs for tailoring comb bandwidth, line distribution, and conversion efficiency.

title: Domain-uniform Integration Lower Bounds And Local Information
authors: Yutong Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study deterministic numerical integration on open subsets of [MATH] of volume one. Let [MATH] be the minimal worst-case error using at most [MATH] function values. For twice continuously differentiable functions with the normalized Lipschitz bounds proposed by Novak, we prove [MATH], where [MATH] is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball. This resolves Novak's conjecture: the lower-bound constant is independent of the dimension and the shape of the domain. A midpoint rule on the cube has the same rate, up to an absolute constant. The proof uses smooth functions that vanish near the sample points and are large elsewhere. The bound therefore remains valid when each sample supplies all local information about the function. For scalar linear targets continuous in the uniform norm, we prove a second result on the global smooth class with prescribed function, gradient, and Hessian bounds: adaptive local information has the same minimal error as values and gradients at points chosen in advance. We give extensions to function recovery, finite integration measures, and anisotropic derivative bounds.
tldr: The paper resolves Novak's conjecture on dimension-independent lower bounds for deterministic numerical integration and studies limits of adaptive local information in function recovery.
motivation: It aims to establish domain-shape- and dimension-uniform lower bounds for numerical integration under normalized Lipschitz and smoothness assumptions.
method: The proof constructs smooth functions vanishing near sample points and large elsewhere, yielding worst-case error bounds that persist even when each sample gives full local information.
result: The lower-bound constant is independent of dimension and domain shape, matching the midpoint rule on the cube up to a constant; adaptive local information is also shown not to improve minimal error for scalar linear targets.
conclusion: The work settles a numerical-analysis conjecture and gives extensions to function recovery and anisotropic derivative bounds, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fejer-Riesz Factorization For Free Products
authors: Abhay Jindal, Igor Klep, Jacob Levenson, Scott Mccullough
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an operator-valued Fejer-Riesz factorization theorem for the algebraic free product A of C[F], the group algebra on the free group F on finitely many generators, with finitely many finite dimensional C-star algebras. With respect to a natural reduced-word length, called extent, we show that every linear combination F of elements of A with coefficients from the algebra of operators on a Hilbert space of extent at most 2d that is positive under all finite-dimensional unital *-representations of A admits a factorization F=B^*B with B of extent at most d. This sharp half-extent bound holds without strict positivity. The proof combines a new finite-dimensional realization theorem for positive truncated kernels with operator-system methods. We also establish factorization results for tensor products with group algebras of arbitrary discrete groups under strict positivity in the maximal C-star-tensor product; for amenable groups, strict positivity in the minimal tensor product suffices.
tldr: The paper proves an operator-valued Fejér-Riesz factorization theorem for algebraic free products involving group algebras and finite-dimensional C*-algebras.
motivation: Fejér-Riesz factorization is a classical tool for representing positive trigonometric polynomials as squares, and the authors aim to extend it to free-product operator algebras.
method: The proof introduces a finite-dimensional realization theorem for positive truncated kernels and combines it with operator-system techniques to control factorization extent.
result: Every positive linear combination of extent at most 2d admits a factorization F = B*B with B of extent at most d, and related tensor-product factorization results are obtained under strict positivity.
conclusion: The work establishes sharp half-extent factorization bounds in a free-product operator-algebra setting, with applications to group algebras and maximal/minimal C*-tensor products.

title: Minimax Designs And Estimators For Causal Inference Under Network Interference
authors: Edoardo M. Airoldi Vishesh Karwa
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a design-based minimax theory for linear causal estimands under interference. We study the minimax risks of three problems: optimizing an estimator under a fixed design, optimizing an estimator and a design from a restricted class, or optimizing both over all designs. In each problem, we study the minimax risk over all estimators and over design-unbiased estimators separately. We allow any correctly specified exposure mapping, including the identity. Our theory represents causal inference under interference as a constrained sampling design on an expanded finite population of [MATH] potential outcomes, where [MATH] is the number of exposure levels attainable by unit [MATH]. We describe the constrained sampling design by a weighted sampling hypergraph: its vertices are the potential outcomes, its hyperedges are the maximal sets of potential outcomes that can be jointly sampled under feasible treatment assignments, and its weights are induced by the randomization design. We show that the minimax risks of the fixed-design, restricted-design, and all-design problems depend, respectively, on the weighted hypergraph induced by the design, the collection of weighted hypergraphs attainable within the restricted class, and the unweighted hypergraph. Our Bayes lower bounds compare potential-outcome tables that differ on jointly missing sets of potential outcomes: joint-missingness probabilities govern the lower bounds over all estimators, whereas the corresponding odds govern the lower bounds over unbiased estimators. We illustrate the theory for average treatment effects without interference, saturation designs under partial interference, total, direct, and contagion effects under neighborhood interference, and bipartite dose-response contrasts. The upper and lower bounds match in several settings.
tldr: A design-based minimax theory for linear causal estimands under network interference, formulated via weighted sampling hypergraphs over potential outcomes.
motivation: Causal inference under interference lacks a general minimax framework covering arbitrary exposure mappings and design classes, which is needed to characterize fundamental limits of estimation.
method: The authors recast interference-affected causal inference as a constrained sampling design on an expanded finite population of potential outcomes, encoded by a weighted sampling hypergraph, and derive Bayes-type lower bounds and matching upper bounds for fixed, restricted, and fully optimized designs.
result: Minimax risks depend on the design-induced weighted hypergraph, the collection of attainable weighted hypergraphs, or the unweighted hypergraph respectively; joint-missingness probabilities govern bounds over all estimators while the corresponding odds govern unbiased-estimator bounds, with matching bounds in several settings.
conclusion: The framework unifies treatment-effect estimation problems (ATE, saturation designs, direct/total/contagion effects, bipartite dose-response) and clarifies how randomization design and exposure mapping determine achievable accuracy.

title: Power Mean, Karcher Mean, And Log-Euclidean Mean On Positive Constant Upper Triangular Matrices
authors: Huajun Huang, Sejong Kim, Vatsalkumar N. Mer
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study weighted power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means on the Lie group CP_n of real upper triangular matrices with a constant positive diagonal. Building on the general triangular-group theory, we use the central decomposition CP_n \cong \mathbb R_+ -by-UP_n to separate the scalar power mean from a unipotent mean with reweighted coefficients. We prove that the power mean extends real-analytically through order zero, where it equals the Karcher mean. We establish exterior-power covariance for the Karcher and log-Euclidean means, and tensor-product identities for all three means, distinguishing product weights from paired inputs. Finite nilpotent functional calculus yields concise formulas on CP_2 and CP_3, where the Karcher and log-Euclidean means coincide. In dimension four, their difference is exactly a central cubic commutator, giving a necessary and sufficient equality criterion and an explicit counterexample. In every dimension, the same commutator is the leading term of their small-dispersion difference.
tldr: The paper studies weighted power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means on the Lie group of positive constant-diagonal upper triangular matrices.
motivation: The authors aim to understand and compare matrix means within a specific solvable Lie group structure, extending triangular-group theory and providing explicit low-dimensional formulas.
method: They use the central decomposition CP_n ≅ R_+ ⋉ UP_n to separate scalar and unipotent contributions, prove real-analytic extension of the power mean, and derive covariance and tensor-product identities.
result: The power mean extends through order zero to the Karcher mean; Karcher and log-Euclidean means coincide in dimensions two and three, while in dimension four their difference is a central cubic commutator, yielding an equality criterion and counterexample.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed Lie-group-theoretic analysis of matrix means on CP_n, with explicit formulas and a commutator characterization of the Karcher–log-Euclidean difference in low dimensions.

title: Spectral Characterizations, Harmonic Analysis, And Phase Transitions In 2-Nice And $k$-Nice Recurrence
authors: Dibyendu de
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09143v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the structural mechanisms governing [MATH]-nice and [MATH]-nice recurrence in measure-preserving dynamical systems. For weakly mixing systems, we establish a complete spectral characterization of two-sided [MATH]-nice recurrence via quadratic spectral functionals and Herglotz--Bochner duality, extending the theory to arbitrary integer polynomial configurations [MATH] with zero constant term and to actions of countable abelian groups. Using stationary Gaussian processes and Hermite mode decoupling, we construct explicit weakly mixing counterexamples separating one-sided and two-sided [MATH]-nice recurrence. Furthermore, we uncover a fundamental structural phase transition at [MATH]: while [MATH] recurrence is rigidly controlled by a quadratic spectral functional whose two-sided symmetrization eliminates all higher-degree cumulants, at [MATH] fourth-order centered correlations survive symmetrization and can drive a strict recurrence deficit even when the quadratic spectral functional remains strictly positive. Using lacunary and multi-frequency Riesz products alongside uniform Wiener lemmas, we analyze the upper Banach density obstructions of negative spectral sets, establish partial partition regularity on the spectral cone, resolve an inverse Furstenberg correspondence problem of Rodr\'iguez Mart\'in for countable groups via Bernoulli product extensions, and characterize spectral [MATH]-nice ultrafilters in the Stone--ech compactification [MATH].
tldr: The paper studies spectral and harmonic-analytic characterizations of k-nice recurrence in measure-preserving dynamical systems, including a structural phase transition between 2-nice and 4-nice recurrence.
motivation: The work aims to understand the structural mechanisms behind nice recurrence in ergodic theory and to resolve spectral, combinatorial, and inverse-correspondence questions for weakly mixing systems and countable abelian group actions.
method: It uses quadratic spectral functionals, Herglotz-Bochner duality, stationary Gaussian processes, Hermite mode decoupling, Riesz products, Wiener lemmas, and Stone-Cech compactification techniques.
result: The author gives a complete spectral characterization for two-sided 2-nice recurrence in weakly mixing systems, constructs counterexamples separating one-sided and two-sided k-nice recurrence, and identifies a phase transition at k=4 where fourth-order correlations can drive recurrence deficits.
conclusion: The paper advances pure ergodic theory and harmonic analysis of recurrence but has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Circuit Theory-Informed Ai For Condition Monitoring In Power Electronics
authors: Yubo Song, Pascal A. Schirmer, Subham Sahoo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence for power electronics is evolving toward a deeper comprehension of system intrinsic behaviors and dynamics. As a novel integration of neural computation and electric circuits, spike-based neuromorphic computing offers promising potential in high energy efficiency and adaptability for data-driven applications. Building on the latency-coding principles, this article proposes a framework for data-light condition monitoring that relies solely on three-phase AC current measurements. The AC current signals are encoded as membrane potentials of RC-based spiking neurons, which are inherently compatible with spiking neural networks that can effectively facilitate the estimation of device parameters. Case studies are presented to validate the performances, while constraints and further optimizations are also evaluated and discussed, and future extensions of the methodology are provided.
tldr: The paper proposes a neuromorphic, spike-based framework for data-light condition monitoring in power electronics using three-phase AC current measurements.
motivation: AI for power electronics is moving toward understanding intrinsic system dynamics, and spike-based neuromorphic computing may offer energy-efficient, adaptable data-driven monitoring.
method: AC current signals are encoded as membrane potentials of RC-based spiking neurons compatible with spiking neural networks, which are then used to estimate device parameters for condition monitoring.
result: Case studies validate the performance of the proposed framework, and constraints plus further optimizations are evaluated and discussed.
conclusion: The methodology shows promise for data-light condition monitoring in power electronics, with future extensions outlined.

title: On Derandomizing The Line-point Low-degree Test
authors: Prahladh Harsha, Swastik Kopparty, Mrinal Kumar, Ramprasad Saptharishi, Madhu Sudan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the derandomized version of the classical line-point low-degree test in the high-error regime in the bivariate setting and reveal some unexpected behavior. The classical line-point low-degree test takes an [MATH]-variate function [MATH] over a finite field [MATH], queries it along a random line and accepts if the restriction of the function to this line is a low-degree polynomial. The high-error version of (the analysis of) this test asserts that if [MATH] has at least [MATH] expected local agreement with a degree-[MATH] univariate polynomial on a random line, then in fact [MATH] is non-trivially close to some degree-[MATH] [MATH]-variate polynomial even as [MATH] approaches [MATH] (provided [MATH] is sufficiently large compared to [MATH] and [MATH]). The derandomized version of the problem asks if the same holds when the line is not chosen uniformly over all possible lines but rather from a small set.In this paper we explore the bivariate case ([MATH]). We show, somewhat surprisingly, that there exists a function [MATH] and a set of lines [MATH] in [MATH] of size nearly [MATH] such that on every line in [MATH], [MATH] has agreement [MATH] on average with some univariate polynomial of degree [MATH] and yet [MATH] is [MATH] far from every polynomial of degree [MATH]. On the positive side, we show that once the field size [MATH] is at least [MATH] such examples disappear and we can get sets of lines of size [MATH] on which the low-degree test has a high-error analysis. On the way to our positive result, we show a new high-degree version of the classical two-direction Polishchuk--Spielman divisibility lemma.
tldr: The paper studies derandomization of the line-point low-degree test in the bivariate high-error regime, showing unexpected counterexamples for small fields and positive results for sufficiently large fields.
motivation: The line-point low-degree test is a classical tool in property testing and probabilistic proof systems, and the derandomized version asks whether a small set of lines suffices for the same agreement-to-proximity implication.
method: The authors analyze the bivariate case over finite fields, construct functions and small line sets violating the derandomized test for small fields, and prove a positive result for large fields using a new high-degree two-direction Polishchuk--Spielman divisibility lemma.
result: They show that for fields of size below a threshold there exists a function with nearly maximal agreement on each line in a small set yet far from every low-degree polynomial, while for sufficiently large fields such examples disappear and small line sets suffice for the high-error analysis.
conclusion: The work reveals a sharp field-size threshold in the derandomized line-point low-degree test and introduces a divisibility lemma that may be useful more broadly in algebraic property testing.

title: Robust & Scalable Website Fingerprinting Via Minimal Dram Traffic
authors: Shubham Roy, Samar Parwez, Biswabandan Panda
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Website fingerprinting attacks infer websites visited by users and threaten their privacy. These attacks are classified as on-path, which monitor network traffic, and co-located, which exploit shared system resources. Existing co-located attacks, such as sweep-counting and loop-counting, achieve over 90% accuracy but suffer significant performance degradation on many-core systems. Loop-counting accuracy drops from 93% on 8 cores to 50% on 24 cores, while sweep-counting accuracy decreases from 84% to 45% across multiple Core Complex Dies (CCDs). To address these limitations, we propose memory-chasing, a scalable website fingerprinting attack that exploits DRAM traffic interference through pointer-chasing traversals with minimal interference. By counting DRAM accesses over fixed intervals, the attack generates distinctive traces for website classification. Evaluated on the top 50 websites, memory-chasing achieves 96% accuracy on a 24-core system, 86% across multiple CCDs, 80% across multiple sockets, and 97% in an open-world setting. Extensive evaluation across hardware configurations, browsers, operating systems, isolation mechanisms, system noise, and countermeasures demonstrates its robustness and scalability.
tldr: The paper proposes memory-chasing, a co-located website fingerprinting attack that counts DRAM accesses during pointer-chasing traversals to classify visited websites with high accuracy on many-core, multi-socket systems.
motivation: Existing co-located website fingerprinting attacks such as sweep-counting and loop-counting degrade sharply on many-core systems and across multiple CCDs, so a more scalable side channel is needed.
method: The attack induces pointer-chasing traversals that generate detectable DRAM traffic interference, then counts DRAM accesses over fixed intervals to build distinctive per-website traces used for classification.
result: Memory-chasing reaches 96% accuracy on a 24-core system, 86% across multiple CCDs, 80% across multiple sockets, and 97% in an open-world setting over the top 50 websites, remaining robust across browsers, OSes, isolation mechanisms, noise, and countermeasures.
conclusion: DRAM-traffic-based side channels provide a robust and scalable alternative for website fingerprinting on modern many-core hardware, raising new privacy concerns for shared-resource systems.

title: Differentially Private GraphRAG: Protecting Relation Connectivity And Semantics
authors: Jie Fu, Yuan Hong, Yue Ning, Wendy Hui Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) connects information across documents through entity relationships to support relational reasoning. However, black-box access to GraphRAG systems can enable adversaries to reconstruct knowledge graphs and recover both structural connectivity between entities and the semantics of their relationships. Existing defenses lack formal privacy guarantees and provide limited protection against such reconstruction attacks. We propose RelGuard, the first differentially private framework for GraphRAG, which provides formal privacy guarantees by mitigating connectivity leakage and protecting relations and their semantic meaning through relation removal. We formalize relation differential privacy (relation-DP), which bounds the distinguishability of mechanism outputs according to the semantic distance between alternative relations while accounting for relation removal. Building on this definition, we develop a four-step defense mechanism that sanitizes source documents before GraphRAG indexing by perturbing relation predicates or removing their associated connectivity using the exponential mechanism. Experiments across three GraphRAG systems and two targeted reconstruction attacks demonstrate that RelGuard provides stronger protection against reconstruction attacks than four existing defense mechanisms while better preserving downstream utility.
tldr: RelGuard is the first differentially private framework for GraphRAG that protects entity-relation connectivity and relational semantics against reconstruction attacks.
motivation: Black-box access to GraphRAG systems lets adversaries reconstruct knowledge graphs, recovering both structural connectivity and the semantics of relations, while existing defenses offer no formal privacy guarantees.
method: The authors formalize relation differential privacy (relation-DP), bounding output distinguishability via semantic distance between alternative relations while accounting for relation removal, and implement a four-step sanitization mechanism that perturbs relation predicates or removes connectivity using the exponential mechanism before indexing.
result: Experiments on three GraphRAG systems and two targeted reconstruction attacks show stronger protection than four existing defenses while better preserving downstream utility.
conclusion: RelGuard demonstrates that formal differential privacy can be integrated into GraphRAG pipelines to mitigate relation-level leakage with acceptable utility trade-offs.

title: Deep-UV All-dielectric qBIC Metasurface For Refractive Index Sensing
authors: Be\'ata Idesov\'a, Alexander A. Antonov, Lina Rohrer, Leonardo de Souza Menezes, Andreas Tittl, Tom\'a\v{s} \v{s}ikola, Filip Ligmajer
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: All-dielectric metasurfaces supporting quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs) have emerged as powerful platforms for biosensing, yet their operation remains largely concentrated in the visible and near-infrared regimes. Extending these resonances into the deep-ultraviolet (DUV) to probe the intrinsic electronic absorption of biomolecules presents substantial material and nanofabrication challenges. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a hafnium dioxide (HfO[MATH]) metasurface supporting DUV qBICs in the wavelength range from 225 nm to 340 nm with quality factors reaching 500. We further demonstrate its refractive index sensing capabilities through integration with a microfluidic cell and optical characterization in reflection mode. We show that the introduction of an aqueous buffer leads to a further quality factor enhancement. Achieving a sensitivity of up to approximately 60 nm/RIU and an operational figure of merit of 40 [MATH], this low-loss HfO[MATH] metasurface provides a robust foundation for label-free DUV biosensing.
tldr: The authors experimentally demonstrate a hafnium dioxide all-dielectric metasurface supporting quasi-bound states in the continuum in the deep-ultraviolet (225–340 nm) and use it for refractive index sensing of aqueous analytes.
motivation: qBIC metasurfaces are powerful biosensing platforms but have been limited to visible and near-infrared wavelengths; extending them to the deep UV would allow probing intrinsic electronic absorption of biomolecules, which requires solving substantial material and nanofabrication challenges.
method: A HfO2 metasurface is fabricated and characterized in reflection mode inside a microfluidic cell, with quality factors, sensitivity (nm/RIU), and figure of merit measured for varying refractive index environments including aqueous buffer.
result: Quality factors up to 500 are achieved, with further enhancement upon introduction of aqueous buffer, yielding a sensitivity of about 60 nm/RIU and an operational figure of merit of 40.
conclusion: The low-loss HfO2 DUV metasurface provides a robust foundation for label-free deep-UV biosensing, though the work is purely classical nanophotonics remote from quantum information science.

title: Laser-Direct-Written Polymer Wgm Microring Laser Integrated On A Fiber Tip For Refractive Index Sensing
authors: Mobin Yaghoobi, Seyedeh Mahshad Hosseini, Leila Hajshahvaladi, Gholam-Mohammad Parsanasab, Mohammad Ismail Zibaii
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) microlasers are promising for refractometric sensing, but their practical implementation can be limited by the need for stable resonator-coupler alignment. Here, we demonstrate a Rhodamine B-doped polymer WGM microring laser directly fabricated on an optical-fiber tip, eliminating the external resonator-fiber coupling interface at the sensing head. Micro-droplet coating and UV laser direct writing are combined for fabrication, while finite-difference time-domain simulations guide the microring laser design. The microlasers operate in air and water with thresholds of 0.224 uJ and 0.458 uJ, respectively. Refractometric measurements in aqueous glucose solutions yield a bulk refractive index sensitivity of 364.95 nm/RIU and a detection limit of 2.47 x 10^(-4) RIU. Water-induced polymer changes and photobleaching are also investigated. This fiber-tip architecture provides a basis for probe-based refractometric sensing in environmental and biochemical applications.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a Rhodamine B-doped polymer whispering-gallery-mode microring laser fabricated directly on an optical fiber tip for refractive-index sensing.
motivation: WGM microlasers are attractive for refractometric sensing, but external resonator-coupler alignment complicates practical implementation; the authors aim to eliminate this interface by integrating the microring laser on a fiber tip.
method: Micro-droplet coating and UV laser direct writing are combined to fabricate the polymer microring laser on a fiber tip, with finite-difference time-domain simulations guiding the design.
result: The microlasers operate in air and water with lasing thresholds of 0.224 uJ and 0.458 uJ, respectively, and refractometric measurements in aqueous glucose solutions show a bulk sensitivity of 364.95 nm/RIU and a detection limit of 2.47 x 10^-4 RIU.
conclusion: The fiber-tip WGM microring laser provides a probe-based refractometric sensing platform for environmental and biochemical applications, with water-induced polymer changes and photobleaching also investigated.

title: The Dynamics Through The First Two Lagrange Necks In The Small-mass Restricted Three-body Problem
authors: Pedro A. S. Salom\~ao Lei Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder. Slightly above the second Lagrange value, the dynamics is transverse to families of disks bounded by the retrograde orbits, and cylinders connecting the retrograde orbits to the Lyapunov orbits, forming a [MATH] foliation. The proof uses the rotating Kepler problem and Hill's lunar problem to control the singular limit as the mass ratio [MATH]. As a consequence of the foliation, both Lyapunov orbits have infinitely many homoclinic orbits.
tldr: The paper studies the planar circular restricted three-body problem for small mass ratios using pseudoholomorphic curve methods to construct finite energy foliations through the first two Lagrange necks.
motivation: The work aims to describe the dynamics near and above the second Lagrange value in the small-mass PCR3BP and to establish a finite energy foliation connecting retrograde orbits and Lyapunov orbits.
method: It uses Hofer-Wysocki-Zehnder theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations, together with singular limits controlled by the rotating Kepler problem and Hill's lunar problem.
result: The authors construct foliations whose binding consists of retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks, and show that slightly above the second Lagrange value the dynamics is transverse to families of disks and cylinders.
conclusion: As a consequence of the foliation, both Lyapunov orbits are shown to admit infinitely many homoclinic orbits.

title: Optical Microscopy For Pathological Imaging: Past, Present, And Future
authors: Runchen Zhang, Xiaoyi Shang, Liangyu Deng, Jingyu Wang, Xiaoyu Zheng, Lanyu Cui, Yao Du, Jiaxin Zhuang, Yifei Ma, Wanying Liu, Limei Guo, Lin Luo, Zhiyi Liu, Stephen M. Morris, Honghui He, Chao He
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Histopathology, the microscopic examination of stained tissue sections, remains the gold standard for pathology imaging, but its bright-field imaging is largely morphological. Advanced optical microscopy techniques move beyond this by exploiting diverse light-matter interactions, and are increasingly applied to pathological imaging. By capturing signals such as refractive index, polarisation, harmonic generation, Brillouin shift, and molecular vibrations, these microscopy techniques can provide quantitative or semi-quantitative information on tissue structure, mechanics, and chemical or molecular composition. In this review, we summarise the physical principles, key quantitative parameters, and representative pathological applications of seven modalities--optical diffraction tomography, polarisation microscopy, second-harmonic generation microscopy, third-harmonic generation microscopy, Brillouin microscopy, Raman microscopy, and fluorescence microscopy. We also discuss progress in artificial intelligence that supports reconstruction, analysis, and interpretation across these modalities, together with emerging trends in multimodal integration. Overall, this review shows how different optical contrasts can complement routine histopathology, while outlining the challenges and opportunities that will shape their clinical translation.
tldr: A review of seven advanced optical microscopy modalities (ODT, polarisation, SHG, THG, Brillouin, Raman, fluorescence) and their use in quantitative histopathological imaging, plus AI-assisted reconstruction and multimodal integration.
motivation: Bright-field histopathology is largely morphological, so label-free contrast mechanisms that reveal refractive index, polarisation, mechanics, and molecular composition could complement standard H&E-based diagnosis.
method: Literature review covering physical principles, key quantitative parameters, and representative pathological applications of seven optical microscopy techniques, together with AI-based reconstruction/analysis and multimodal integration trends.
result: Each modality supplies distinct quantitative or semi-quantitative contrast (structure, mechanics, chemistry) that complements routine histopathology; AI supports reconstruction, analysis, and interpretation across modalities.
conclusion: Optical contrasts beyond bright-field offer complementary diagnostic value, with clinical translation depending on addressing outstanding technical and regulatory challenges.

title: An Acousto-optic Colorimeter For Color Psychophysics
authors: Sergey Korchagin, Georgiy Lobarev, Pavel Aksentsev, Pavel Maximov, Maria Gracheva, Olga Polschikova, Egor Ershov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A complete model of human color perception requires the ability to present any color as a stimulus.Most existing measurements were collected with physical color samples, and current laboratory generators, such as displays and multi-primary LED systems, work with a small number of fixed primaries. Published color-difference data therefore cover about 40\% of the CIE~[MATH] chromaticity diagram, while commercial wide-gamut displays already reach two thirds of it and need difference metrics there. We describe an acousto-optic colorimeter that lets the experimenter choose the primaries. The device selects up to four narrow bands from a supercontinuum (white-light) laser, each with electronically set wavelength and intensity, and covers 95\% of the CIE~[MATH] chromaticity diagram. Threshold-scale color differences, presented in alternation as in a discrimination experiment, are reproduced with a mean error of 0.08--0.12 CIEDE2000 units ([MATH]) at five CIE-recommended color centers. Because one color can be built from many combinations of narrow bands, the bands are chosen for the task: the finest adjustment for color matching, the least disagreement between observers for color-difference measurement. In simulations with 151~individual observers from a published dataset, with these bands observers see colors 0.6--1.9~[MATH] from the intended one on average, against 1.2--2.5~[MATH] on a calibrated wide-gamut LCD, lower at every center. The approach applies to any narrowband source and lets experimenters use saturated colors while limiting the effect of individual differences in color vision.
tldr: The paper presents an acousto-optic colorimeter that selects narrow spectral bands from a supercontinuum laser to generate customizable color stimuli for human color psychophysics experiments.
motivation: Existing color-difference measurements cover only a limited portion of the CIE chromaticity diagram because standard displays and LED systems use a small number of fixed primaries, limiting research on saturated colors and individual differences in color perception.
method: The device selects up to four narrow bands from a supercontinuum laser, each with electronically controlled wavelength and intensity, and uses task-specific band selection to reproduce threshold-scale color differences across CIE-recommended color centers.
result: The colorimeter covers 95% of the CIE chromaticity diagram and reproduces threshold-scale color differences with mean errors of 0.08–0.12 CIEDE2000 units; simulations with 151 observers show reduced color deviation compared to a calibrated wide-gamut LCD.
conclusion: The approach enables flexible, saturated color stimulus generation with reduced observer-dependent variation and is applicable to any narrowband source for color psychophysics.

title: When Is An Optical Design Problem A Mass Transfer Problem?
authors: Albert A. Mingazov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates whether optical design problems can be represented as Monge--Kantorovich mass transfer problems with some cost function. An optical problem is specified by a function defining a particular family of supporting surfaces for the optical element. We introduce the notion of geometric equivalence between optical and transport problems, which is directly related to the possibility of formulating an optical design problem as a mass transfer problem. A necessary condition for such equivalence is derived in the semi-discrete setting. It allows a transport representation to be ruled out without choosing a cost function in advance. The condition is applied to the near-field refractor problem and to the design of two refracting surfaces transforming a spherical beam into a spherical or collimated beam. For these problems, the necessary condition is shown to fail in physically admissible configurations. We also study an optical element with a single working surface and an arbitrary regular incident wavefront. In the far field, geometric equivalence to a mass transfer problem requires a planar or spherical wavefront, whereas in the near field with a planar target, the necessary condition fails for an arbitrary smooth wavefront.
tldr: The paper studies when optical design problems admit a representation as Monge-Kantorovich mass transfer problems.
motivation: Optical design and optimal transport share a mathematical structure, so it is natural to ask when an optical problem can be exactly reformulated as a mass transfer problem.
method: The author introduces geometric equivalence between optical design and transport problems and derives a necessary condition in the semi-discrete setting, applying it to refractor and two-surface design problems.
result: The necessary condition fails in physically admissible configurations for several near-field refractor problems, and far-field equivalence requires planar or spherical wavefronts.
conclusion: Many optical design problems cannot be represented as mass transfer problems, so a transport formulation must be justified rather than assumed.

title: Singularities And Collision Criteria In The Gravitational Straight-Segment Problem With Arbitrary Positive Density
authors: F. Crespo, E. Mart\'{\i}nez, J. Vidarte, J. L. Zapata, A. Abdrabou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study singularities and collision criteria for a massless particle around a fixed finite straight segment with an arbitrary positive continuous density. We first show that every singularity forces the trajectory to approach the material segment. Using the axial symmetry of the potential, we prove that any trajectory approaching the segment is confined to an invariant plane containing it. Moreover, we show that every singularity is either a collision singularity or an ejection singularity. Finally, in the invariant plane, we introduce an angular-cone condition for positions and momenta directed toward the segment. We prove that if the initial position-momentum pair belongs to the angular cone, then the trajectory collides with the segment in finite time, and we derive an upper bound for the collision time. We further prove that the final arc of any collision satisfies the angular-cone condition.
tldr: A classical celestial-mechanics study of singularities and collision criteria for a massless particle orbiting a fixed finite straight segment with arbitrary positive density.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize the possible singularities of trajectories around an extended one-dimensional massive segment and to establish sufficient conditions guaranteeing collision in finite time.
method: Using axial symmetry of the potential, they prove trajectories approaching the segment lie in an invariant plane, classify singularities as collision or ejection type, and introduce an angular-cone condition on initial positions and momenta.
result: Initial position-momentum pairs inside the angular cone lead to finite-time collision, with an explicit upper bound on collision time; conversely, the final arc of any collision satisfies the angular-cone condition.
conclusion: The work provides geometric collision criteria for the straight-segment gravitational problem, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Extensions Of Operators Between Ordered Vector Spaces
authors: Eugene Bilokopytov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove analogues of several classical theorems about operators between vector lattices in the context of directed Archimedean ordered vector spaces. In particular, we show that every order continuous operator between pervasive Archimedean ordered vector spaces can be extended to an order continuous operator between their Dedekind completions. Additionally, we introduce the universal completion of a directed Archimedean ordered vector space, and show that every supremum-preserving operator between directed Archimedean ordered vector spaces can be extended to an order continuous homomorphism between their universal completions. We also establish some universal properties for the relative uniform completion.
tldr: The paper proves extension theorems for order continuous and supremum-preserving operators between directed Archimedean ordered vector spaces via Dedekind and universal completions.
motivation: Classical extension and lifting theorems for operators on vector lattices are well developed, but their analogues for the more general setting of directed Archimedean ordered vector spaces lacking a lattice structure remain largely unexplored.
method: Abstract order-theoretic and functional-analytic arguments are used: the author constructs the universal completion of a directed Archimedean ordered vector space, establishes universal properties for the relative uniform completion, and extends operators through these completions.
result: Every order continuous operator between pervasive Archimedean ordered vector spaces extends to an order continuous operator between Dedekind completions, and every supremum-preserving operator extends to an order continuous homomorphism between universal completions.
conclusion: The results generalize several classical vector-lattice extension theorems to the broader ordered-vector-space setting and provide new universal completion constructions with associated universal properties.

title: Proof Of The Cordero-Torregrosa Conjecture And An Improved Order Bound For Paired Jacobian Evaluations
authors: Rodrigo Alberto Castro Mar\'in
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08801v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In solving systems of nonlinear equations, one of the main objectives is to construct iterative methods that attain high orders of convergence using as few evaluations as possible. However, the information a method obtains during each iteration imposes limitations on the order it can guarantee. The Cordero--Torregrosa conjecture proposes a bound on this order in terms of the number of evaluations of the function and its Jacobian. In this work, we prove this bound for the universal local order of one iteration, without requiring the number of Jacobian evaluations to be less than or equal to the number of function evaluations. In particular, our result also covers the case in which more evaluations of the Jacobian than of the function are performed. The proof encompasses deterministic, causal, memoryless methods whose rules may be arbitrary, without imposing rationality, continuity, or computability conditions. Moreover, we prove that when each Jacobian evaluation is performed at a point where the value of the function is already known, a more restrictive bound on the order of convergence can be obtained. Finally, we propose a new conjecture that establishes a refined bound through a product of factors determined by the distribution of evaluations, under additional dimensional conditions. These results provide a better understanding of the limitations imposed by the available information and raise new possibilities for studying high-order iterative methods.
tldr: The paper proves the Cordero–Torregrosa conjecture on order bounds for iterative nonlinear-equation solvers and derives refined bounds based on Jacobian evaluation placement.
motivation: Iterative methods for nonlinear systems face fundamental limits on convergence order due to the information obtained per iteration, but the conjectured Cordero–Torregrosa bound had not been proved in full generality.
method: The author gives a general proof for deterministic, causal, memoryless methods with arbitrary rules, covering cases with more Jacobian evaluations than function evaluations, and analyzes improved bounds when Jacobian evaluations reuse known function values.
result: The conjectured universal local order bound is proved without restrictions on the relative number of Jacobian and function evaluations, and a stricter bound is obtained under additional information-reuse conditions; a refined conjecture is proposed.
conclusion: The work clarifies information-theoretic limitations on high-order iterative methods in numerical analysis, but it is not connected to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Empirical Approximation Of $L_p$ Norms For $p\in (2, \infty)$
authors: Feng Dai, Egor Kosov, Noel Murasko
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For [MATH] and an [MATH]-dimensional subspace [MATH] satisfying \[ \|f\|_\infty\le (KN)^{1/p}\|f\|_{L_p(\mu)} \quad\forall f\in X, \] we show that [MATH] independent samples [MATH] with distribution [MATH] satisfy \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(\mu)}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(\xi^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(\mu)}^p \quad\forall f\in X \] with probability at least [MATH]. This gives the optimal sample-size order [MATH] for independent random sampling with fixed [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]. This result follows from a more general empirical moment estimate over unit balls of [MATH]-convex norms.
tldr: The paper proves optimal sample-size bounds for empirically approximating L_p norms on finite-dimensional subspaces using independent random samples.
motivation: Empirical approximations of norms are fundamental in high-dimensional probability and functional analysis, with applications to sampling-based numerical methods.
method: The authors establish a general empirical moment estimate over unit balls of q-convex norms and apply it to subspaces satisfying an L_infty-to-L_p comparison condition.
result: They show that m independent samples suffice to uniformly approximate the L_p norm of all functions in the subspace within relative error epsilon with high probability, achieving the optimal sample-size order.
conclusion: The work provides sharp sample-complexity guarantees for empirical L_p norm approximation in finite-dimensional subspaces.

title: Task-Contribution Dynamics Of Adam In Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Slow-Manifold Analysis And Gradient Modulation
authors: Xiaoliang Song Enzhan Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often suffer from imbalanced optimization of competing loss components, particularly when approximating solutions with high-frequency or multiscale features. Although existing balancing strategies have proven effective in alleviating this difficulty, the mechanisms governing the evolution of individual task contributions to Adam's parameter updates remain insufficiently understood. We introduce task-wise indicators to characterize this evolution and identify three distinct training regimes: smooth variation, intermittent spikes, and persistent oscillations. Focusing on the early smooth regime, we combine discrete-time analysis with a continuous-time singular perturbation framework under the full-batch setting and the parameter regime [MATH]. A first-order approximation of the locally attracting slow manifold reveals two factors governing the step-to-step redistribution of task contributions: curvature-related alignment disparities and differences in the coordinatewise distributions of preconditioned task gradients. Both factors involve Adam's shared second-moment estimate. Inspired by AdaTask, we propose Gradient-Modulated Adam (GMAdam), which modulates incoming task gradients using task-specific second-moment estimates. Numerical experiments on high-frequency Poisson and wave equations, the Allen-Cahn equation, and two-dimensional lid-driven cavity flow ([MATH]) demonstrate consistent improvements in predictive accuracy over AdaTask at comparable computational cost.
tldr: The paper analyzes task-contribution dynamics of Adam in physics-informed neural networks and proposes Gradient-Modulated Adam (GMAdam) to improve training balance.
motivation: PINNs often suffer from imbalanced optimization among competing loss terms, especially for high-frequency or multiscale solutions, and the mechanisms by which individual task contributions evolve under Adam are not well understood.
method: The authors introduce task-wise indicators to identify three training regimes and analyze the early smooth regime using discrete-time analysis plus a continuous-time singular perturbation framework. They then propose GMAdam, which modulates task gradients using task-specific second-moment estimates inspired by AdaTask.
result: Numerical experiments on high-frequency Poisson and wave equations, the Allen-Cahn equation, and 2D lid-driven cavity flow show consistent predictive-accuracy improvements over AdaTask at comparable computational cost.
conclusion: The work provides insight into Adam's task-contribution redistribution in PINNs and demonstrates that gradient modulation with task-specific second-moment estimates can improve PINN training.

title: Polynomial Complexity, Random Graphs, And Strict Ergodicity
authors: Be'eri Greenfeld, Paul-Henry Leemann, Carlos Gustavo Moreira, Efim Zelmanov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct infinite words [MATH] whose complexity functions are quadratically bounded, but whose discrete derivatives are not linearly bounded, resolving a question of Cassaigne. Moreover, we construct infinite words of polynomially bounded complexity, and subshifts of quasi-linear complexity, whose discrete derivatives do not decay compared to their complexity functions, thus exhibiting a typical exponentially-growing behavior. As an application, we give the first examples of subshifts of polynomial complexity whose Rauzy graphs do not have Benjamini-Schramm limits. Finally, we realize (up to an inevitable linear error factor) every function satisfying the necessary conditions, as the complexity function of a minimal, uniquely ergodic, cube-free subshift, strengthening previous realization results in this direction, and derive consequences for the growth of simple algebras and just-infinite semigroups satisfying nontrivial laws.
tldr: The paper resolves a question of Cassaigne by constructing infinite words with quadratically bounded complexity functions whose discrete derivatives are not linearly bounded, and constructs polynomial-complexity subshifts with atypical derivative behavior and no Benjamini-Schramm limits for Rauzy graphs.
motivation: Complexity functions of infinite words and subshifts are central objects in combinatorics on words and symbolic dynamics, and the growth of their discrete derivatives (a measure of factor complexity regularity) was poorly understood beyond the linear-bounded cases.
method: Explicit combinatorial constructions of infinite words and minimal subshifts, together with realization theorems for prescribed complexity functions under necessary growth conditions, yielding minimal uniquely ergodic cube-free subshifts.
result: Quadratic-complexity words with non-linearly-bounded derivatives are constructed, typical exponentially growing derivative behavior is exhibited for quasi-linear-complexity subshifts, and the first examples of polynomial-complexity subshifts whose Rauzy graphs lack Benjamini-Schramm limits are given.
conclusion: The constructions sharpen realization results for complexity functions and yield applications to the growth of simple algebras and just-infinite semigroups satisfying nontrivial laws.

title: Equidistribution Of Solution Gradients In Physics-Informed Neural Networks Via Coordinate Transformations
authors: Ivan Oseledets Tianchi Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often struggle to approximate solutions with sharp gradients due to optimization difficulties and spectral bias. Motivated by the principle of gradient equidistribution from the stretching approach in grid generation, which redistributes solution gradients to reduce functional complexity, we propose Coordinate Transformation PINNs (CTPINNs), which incorporate learnable coordinate transformations to map the physical domain into a computational domain where the physical solutions become approximately affine, making them easier for neural networks to learn. We propose two constructions of the transformation: an explicit construction based on Majorants and an implicit construction based on invertable neural networks. Experimentally, the explicit construction can improve accuracy for PDEs with available explicit coordinate transformations, and the implicit construction can be combined with other advanced PINN models as an efficient plug-in module to improve performance across a range of challenging PDE benchmarks.
tldr: The paper proposes Coordinate Transformation PINNs (CTPINNs), which learn coordinate transformations to equidistribute solution gradients and ease optimization for PDEs with sharp gradients.
motivation: Physics-Informed Neural Networks often fail on solutions with sharp gradients due to spectral bias and optimization difficulties.
method: Motivated by gradient equidistribution in grid generation, the authors introduce learnable coordinate transformations, using either explicit Majorant-based constructions or implicit invertible neural networks, to map physical solutions into approximately affine computational-domain solutions.
result: Experiments show the explicit construction improves accuracy when explicit transformations are available, while the implicit construction can be used as a plug-in module to improve performance on challenging PDE benchmarks.
conclusion: Coordinate transformations provide a practical way to mitigate sharp-gradient learning difficulties in PINNs and can complement existing advanced PINN architectures.

title: Characterization Of Attenuated V-Line Transform And Direct Reconstruction From Samples
authors: Lvchang Li Youfa Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The V-line transform (V-LT), a generalized Radon transform (RT), is widely used in Compton scattering imaging (CSI). The central mathematical problem of CSI is to reconstruct a function from its V-LT. Unlike V-LT, the attenuated V-line transform (AV-LT) accounts for the medium-induced loss of intensity, and has been demonstrated to improve image quality. The present paper makes two main contributions. (1) We establish the fundamental characterizations for AV-LT including operator properties ([MATH]-boundedness, operator norm etc.), a necessary and sufficient condition for the preservation of compact support, and sharp estimation of Sobolev smoothness. These characterizations remain unexplored, and they reveal essential differences among AV-LT, RT and V-LT. (2) We develop a direct reconstruction method based on AV-LT samples that does not require solving any equation. Our sampling formula gives exact reconstruction for band-limited functions. We also provide approximate reconstruction for functions in [MATH] with [MATH].
tldr: The paper characterizes the attenuated V-line transform and develops direct reconstruction methods from samples for Compton scattering imaging.
motivation: The attenuated V-line transform improves image quality in Compton scattering imaging, but its mathematical properties and direct reconstruction formulas remain underexplored.
method: The authors establish operator properties such as boundedness and norm estimates, compact-support preservation conditions, and Sobolev smoothness bounds, then derive a sampling-based direct reconstruction formula.
result: They provide sharp characterizations distinguishing the attenuated V-line transform from the Radon and V-line transforms, exact reconstruction for band-limited functions, and approximate reconstruction for more general functions.
conclusion: These results advance the mathematical theory and practical reconstruction algorithms for Compton scattering imaging, but they are unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Byzantine-Robust Distributed Sparse Softmax Regression
authors: Yuxuan Wang, Yu Sun, Bowen Li, Kangqiang Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Byzantine-robust distributed sparse softmax regression in high-dimensional settings. We propose a communication-efficient distributed algorithm that employs robust aggregation methods---coordinate-wise trimmed mean and coordinate-wise median---to defend against Byzantine attacks. Under sub-Gaussian design assumptions with sparsity constraints, we establish that the distributed estimator achieves the convergence rate of [MATH] when the Byzantine fraction [MATH], matching the centralized oracle rate. Numerical experiments on synthetic data demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method.
tldr: The paper proposes a communication-efficient distributed algorithm for Byzantine-robust sparse softmax regression using coordinate-wise trimmed mean and median aggregation, with convergence rates matching the centralized oracle.
motivation: Distributed learning in high dimensions is vulnerable to adversarial (Byzantine) workers, and existing robust aggregation schemes lack theoretical guarantees under sparsity constraints.
method: A distributed sparse softmax regression estimator is developed that combines coordinate-wise trimmed mean and coordinate-wise median aggregation, analyzed under sub-Gaussian design assumptions with sparsity.
result: The distributed estimator attains the centralized oracle convergence rate provided the Byzantine fraction stays below a stated threshold, and synthetic experiments show improved robustness over baselines.
conclusion: Robust coordinate-wise aggregation suffices to achieve near-optimal statistical accuracy in distributed sparse softmax regression despite Byzantine corruption.

title: Strong Convergence Rates For Numerical Approximations Of The Stochastic Burgers Equation With Additive Rough Noise
authors: Houqi Su Ziyi Lei
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish strong convergence rates for a fully discrete method of the one-dimensional stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive rough noise. Using the Cole-Hopf transformation, the equation is converted into a linear stochastic heat equation, which is discretized by a spectral Galerkin method in space and an accelerated exponential Euler method in time. A numerical approximation of the original solution is then reconstructed through a regularized inverse Cole-Hopf transformation. The analysis combines strong Sobolev error estimates with the positivity and inverse-moment bounds for the transformed solution. For additive space-time white noise, the numerical method achieves mean-square convergence rates arbitrarily close to 1/2 in space and 1/4 in time. The rates are slower when the noises are rougher.
tldr: The paper derives strong (mean-square) convergence rates for a fully discrete spectral Galerkin / accelerated exponential Euler scheme for the 1D stochastic Burgers equation with additive rough noise, using the Cole-Hopf transformation.
motivation: Numerical schemes for nonlinear stochastic PDEs driven by rough noise lack sharp strong convergence guarantees; the authors aim to establish optimal-type rates for Burgers-type equations.
method: The Cole-Hopf transformation maps the equation to a linear stochastic heat equation, discretized by spectral Galerkin in space and an accelerated exponential Euler method in time, with the solution reconstructed via a regularized inverse Cole-Hopf transform; the analysis combines Sobolev error estimates with positivity and inverse-moment bounds.
