Retrospective rainfall provides no clear AP improvement; the primary validation comparisons for vegetation, land cover and their combination are inconclusive. Positive secondary or exploratory intervals do not change those decisions. Evaluation requires complete target and recent-history observations and measures satellite detections, not individual fires, causes or burned area. Prospective evaluation should archive inputs at each weekly issue and measure ranking, calibration and the usefulness of selected cells for monitoring decisions.
tldr: A reproducible benchmark forecasting next-week VIIRS fire detections across Bolivia's 0.05-degree grid cells using calibrated gradient-boosted trees, with temporal and geographic validation.
motivation: Weekly fire-detection forecasts could help prioritize fire monitoring and resource allocation across Bolivia.
method: Calibrated LightGBM models are trained on VIIRS Suomi-NPP detections and evaluated on held-out 2023-2025 temporal blocks and geographically excluded regions, with block-bootstrap confidence intervals and comparisons against climatology and persistence baselines.
result: The temporal model achieves average precision 0.323 versus 0.167 (climatology) and 0.143 (persistence); the geographic model reaches AP 0.384, and reviewing the top 5% / 10% of ranked area would cover 38.4% / 55.8% of detection cell-weeks, though high-probability bins remain miscalibrated.
conclusion: The benchmark shows meaningful predictive skill over baselines but requires prospective validation and measures satellite detections rather than individual fires or burned area.

title: A Jump-Diffusion Model Of Home Price Dynamics And Neighborhood Change
authors: Ashley Peake, Adam Gilbert-Diamond, Anette E. Hosoi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a dynamical model that links the fluctuations of individual home prices to changes in the full distribution of home prices in an urban area. We model the price of an individual home as a jump-diffusion stochastic differential equation. To capture the dynamic and hyper-local economic conditions that drive the residential real estate market, we allow all parameters to depend on both time and neighborhood. In the mean-field limit, we derive the associated Fokker-Planck partial integro-differential equation (PIDE) governing the evolution of the home price distribution in a neighborhood. We quantify spatial heterogeneity within a city by using the Wasserstein-2 distance to compare home price distributions across the city's neighborhoods. We validate our model using data from Boston, Massachusetts as a case study.
tldr: A jump-diffusion stochastic model links individual home price fluctuations to neighborhood-level price distributions via a mean-field Fokker-Planck PIDE, validated on Boston data.
motivation: The authors aim to connect micro-scale individual housing price dynamics to macro-scale distributional changes across urban neighborhoods, capturing hyper-local and time-varying economic conditions.
method: Individual home prices are modeled as jump-diffusion SDEs with time- and neighborhood-dependent parameters; a mean-field limit yields a Fokker-Planck partial integro-differential equation, and Wasserstein-2 distance quantifies spatial heterogeneity between neighborhoods.
result: The derived PIDE governs the evolution of neighborhood price distributions, and the model is validated empirically using Boston, Massachusetts housing data.
conclusion: The framework offers a tractable dynamical description of urban real estate price distributions and neighborhood change, though it lies entirely outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems.

title: An Asymptotic Framework For Closed-Form Estimators From Surrogate Estimating Equations
authors: Robert Zimmerman Yigal Teplitsky
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many statistical estimators, including maximum likelihood and method of moments estimators, are defined as roots of estimating equations. In complex models, these equations often cannot be solved explicitly; although numerical methods can provide approximate solutions, closed-form approximations can reduce computation and facilitate theoretical analysis by making an estimator's dependence on the data more transparent. In this paper, we develop a general approach to constructing such approximations and a framework for quantifying their accuracy. Our theory accommodates sequences of parameters that approach the boundary of the parameter space or diverge to infinity, and provides conditions under which a closed-form approximate estimator has the same first-order asymptotic distribution as its exact counterpart. We focus on approximations to maximum likelihood estimators, although the theory applies to general estimating equations. We apply the framework to iid models from the gamma, zeta, von Mises, and generalized Pareto families, as well as to gamma regression. Together, these examples cover scalar and vector parameters, iid and non-iid settings, and normal and nonnormal asymptotic regimes. Each example is accompanied by a simulation study, and the gamma regression example also includes a real-world data application.
tldr: The paper develops a general asymptotic framework for constructing and validating closed-form approximations to estimators defined as roots of estimating equations, with applications to maximum likelihood in several parametric families.
motivation: Estimators such as MLE and method-of-moments estimators are implicit roots of estimating equations that often lack closed forms, and numerical solutions obscure how estimators depend on data and complicate theoretical analysis.
method: The authors build a general theory of closed-form approximate estimators, including parameter sequences approaching the boundary or diverging to infinity, and give conditions under which the approximation shares the exact estimator's first-order asymptotic distribution.
result: The framework is applied to iid models from the gamma, zeta, von Mises, and generalized Pareto families and to gamma regression, covering scalar and vector parameters, iid and non-iid settings, and normal and nonnormal asymptotics, each supported by simulation studies and a real-data application.
conclusion: Closed-form surrogate estimators can match the asymptotic behavior of exact estimators under explicit conditions, offering computational savings and greater transparency in complex statistical models.

title: Exact Optimality Of Augmented Order-of-addition Designs
authors: Stelios D. Georgiou, Haralambos Evangelaras, Stella Stylianou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for the pairwise-ordering model with at least three components, adding any run to an order-of-addition orthogonal array gives a [MATH]-optimal design among all exact designs of the enlarged size, allowing replication. We also establish the corresponding result for foldover designs: adding any reversal pair to a foldover order-of-addition orthogonal array gives a [MATH]-optimal design within the foldover class at the enlarged size. Both augmentations also minimise the average prediction variance and a covariance-scaled information discrepancy, and maximise the minimum relative efficiency. The key step represents the scaled discrepancy through signed comparisons of triples and derives a sharp integer lower bound; classical spectral inequalities then give the exact-size optima, and signed four-component relative-order counts characterise equality. Complete reversal pairs additionally protect the estimation of pairwise-ordering effects against arbitrary reversal-invariant nuisance means. At the smallest estimable five-component foldover size, exact enumeration identifies five determinant-optimal classes with different prediction and balance properties, and a seven-component example shows that deleting a reversal pair need not be optimal even when it minimises the discrepancy. Constructions through ten components illustrate the attained run sizes.
tldr: This paper proves that augmenting order-of-addition orthogonal arrays with extra runs (or a reversal pair for foldovers) yields exactly optimal designs under a pairwise-ordering model.
motivation: Order-of-addition experiments require efficient designs, but optimality of simple augmentations of orthogonal arrays at enlarged run sizes was not established exactly.
method: The authors express the scaled information discrepancy via signed comparisons of triples, derive a sharp integer lower bound, and apply classical spectral inequalities to obtain exact-size optima, with equality characterized by signed four-component relative-order counts.
result: Adding any run to an order-of-addition orthogonal array (at least three components) gives an optimal design of the enlarged size; adding a reversal pair gives optimality within the foldover class, also minimizing average prediction variance and maximizing minimum relative efficiency.
conclusion: Augmented order-of-addition and foldover orthogonal arrays are exactly optimal, with enumeration at five components revealing five determinant-optimal classes and a seven-component example showing reversal-pair deletion need not be optimal.

title: Multilevel Kernel Approximation Of log-Euclidean Manifold-valued Functions
authors: Holger Wendland Nir Sharon
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study kernel approximation and multilevel residual correction for functions with values in a manifold that admits a global logarithm onto a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, such as positive definite matrices, exponential Lie groups, and Hadamard manifolds. Approximating in logarithmic coordinates keeps the approximant on the manifold and transfers Hilbert-space error estimates verbatim. To express these errors in the natural geometry of the target, we prove metric comparisons. In particular, we obtain a sharp, scale-invariant bound between the log-Euclidean and affine-invariant distances on positive definite matrices, with a constant that depends only on condition numbers. For multilevel approximation, compactly supported kernels scaled to the fill distance give algebraic convergence with sparse, uniformly well-conditioned systems. These guarantees require appropriate sample locations and approximation scales. Compact groups are treated through a principal logarithm, where a bi-invariant metric gives error bounds with constant one. Finally, the log-Euclidean and Karcher means differ by [MATH] near the identity and by [MATH] around a general point, where [MATH] is the logarithmic data radius and the second bound is sharp.
tldr: The paper develops kernel and multilevel approximation methods for functions taking values in manifolds that admit a global logarithm, with applications to positive definite matrices, Lie groups, and Hadamard manifolds.
motivation: Approximating manifold-valued functions while preserving the manifold structure is challenging; working in logarithmic coordinates can transfer Hilbert-space error estimates back to the manifold geometry.
method: The authors approximate in logarithmic coordinates, prove metric comparisons between log-Euclidean and affine-invariant distances, and analyze multilevel residual correction using compactly supported kernels scaled to the fill distance.
result: They obtain algebraic convergence with sparse, uniformly well-conditioned systems, a sharp scale-invariant bound between log-Euclidean and affine-invariant distances on positive definite matrices, and sharp bounds on differences between log-Euclidean and Karcher means.
conclusion: The framework provides approximation guarantees for manifold-valued functions under appropriate sample locations and scales, but it is purely numerical/geometric and has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Reweighting For Transfer Classification: Exact Risk Conversion And Minimax Adaptation
authors: Yang Feng Aoran Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A source can make a training mixture easier to learn while making its accuracy less valuable for the target. We study how the training problem a source creates and the finite-sample error of learning it jointly determine target-risk guarantees under reweighting. For binary classification, for each pair of laws and each positive target weight, we derive the sharpest target excess hinge-risk bound implied by mixture excess alone, uniformly over clipped predictors. This exact conversion curve is determined by density-weighted local votes. A two-sample oracle inequality for weighted support vector machines supplies the mixture excess, and the composition becomes explicit for Gaussian kernels. On a tilted-boundary class, we establish the all-procedure minimax classification rate [MATH] in the transferable strength [MATH] and the tilt [MATH], separating source sampling uncertainty ([MATH]) from relation uncertainty ([MATH]). A target-checked Gaussian-SVM selector adapts to unknown [MATH] and [MATH] up to a logarithmic factor for fixed dimension, and retains the target-only rate up to the same factor against arbitrary independent sources under the stated target model. On a separate smooth opposition class, the minimax risk within the family of exact Gaussian SVMs fitted to the original labels with nonnegative weights is exponentially larger than the unrestricted minimax risk whenever the target sample is at most half the source sample, despite arbitrary data-dependent weighting and tuning. The value of a source thus depends on the training problem it creates, on what accuracy there means for the target, and on whether the permitted use of the source can implement the needed correction.
tldr: The paper derives exact conversions between mixture excess hinge risk and target excess risk under covariate-shift reweighting, plus minimax-optimal adaptation rates for weighted Gaussian-kernel SVMs in binary transfer classification.
motivation: A source dataset can make training easier while being less informative about the target, so one needs a principled way to quantify how much target risk reduction a given source and reweighting scheme can actually deliver.
method: For each pair of source/target laws the authors compute the sharpest target excess hinge-risk bound implied by mixture excess risk uniformly over clipped predictors, combine it with a two-sample oracle inequality for weighted SVMs, and analyze minimax rates over a tilted-boundary class and a smooth opposition class.
result: The exact conversion curve is governed by density-weighted local votes; on the tilted-boundary class the minimax rate separates source sampling uncertainty from relation uncertainty and a target-checked Gaussian-SVM selector adapts up to log factors, while on the opposition class exact Gaussian SVMs with nonnegative weights are exponentially worse than unrestricted minimax risk when the target sample is at most half the source sample.
conclusion: The usefulness of a source is jointly determined by the training problem it induces, the target-relevant meaning of its accuracy, and whether the allowed use of the source can implement the required correction.

title: Finite-rank Toeplitz Commutators On The Harmonic Bergman Space
authors: Puyu Cui, Zengyong Huang, Yufeng Lu, Chao Zu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We completely characterize finite-rank commutators of Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on the harmonic Bergman space of the unit disk. Apart from affine dependence, finite rank occurs precisely when both symbols are analytic with rational primitives, or both are coanalytic and their complex conjugates have rational primitives. Our approach combines a block-matrix decomposition with Luecking's theorem, which rules out nonzero finite-rank Toeplitz operators with bounded symbols on the Bergman space. In particular, every such finite-rank commutator has square zero.
tldr: The paper fully characterizes finite-rank commutators of Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on the harmonic Bergman space of the unit disk.
motivation: Finite-rank commutators are a central structural question in operator theory and are connected to analyticity and rationality properties of symbols.
method: The authors combine a block-matrix decomposition with Luecking's theorem, which excludes nonzero finite-rank Toeplitz operators with bounded symbols on the Bergman space.
result: Apart from affine dependence, finite rank occurs exactly when both symbols are analytic with rational primitives, or both are coanalytic and their complex conjugates have rational primitives; every such commutator has square zero.
conclusion: The paper provides a complete classification of finite-rank Toeplitz commutators on the harmonic Bergman space and shows they are nilpotent of order two.

title: Constrained Nested-Logit Pricing: An Exact Reformulation And Global Optimization Method
authors: Tien Mai Hoang Giang Pham
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09023v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sellers must price substitutable products while meeting operational requirements such as price limits and sales targets. Nested logit captures stronger substitution among similar products, but these requirements can undermine the structure used to solve unconstrained pricing problems. We develop an exact reformulation and a global optimization method for a fixed assortment with price bounds and weighted price caps. The key novelty is to concentrate the difficult interactions at the nest level while retaining convex optimization over individual products, without discretizing prices or approximating demand. This structure makes the number of nests, rather than products, govern the exponent in a conditional worst-case complexity bound. The method returns feasible prices together with a bound on how much profit could still be gained, allowing decision makers to assess solution quality even when computation stops early. Extensions cover purchase-probability bounds and price-order rules, with explicit accounts of their computational cost. In synthetic experiments, the method certifies solutions for assortments of up to 500 products with few nests. Projecting unconstrained prices onto the feasible set loses up to 32.60% of profit relative to direct constrained optimization, highlighting the value of jointly optimizing substitution and feasibility.
tldr: The paper develops an exact reformulation and global optimization algorithm for constrained nested-logit pricing over a fixed assortment with price bounds and weighted price caps.
motivation: Sellers of substitutable products must satisfy operational constraints (price limits, sales targets) that break the structure exploited by unconstrained nested-logit pricing solvers, and naive projection of unconstrained prices onto the feasible set can lose substantial profit.
method: The authors concentrate hard interactions at the nest level while preserving convex optimization over individual products, avoiding price discretization or demand approximation, and derive a worst-case complexity bound governed by the number of nests; extensions handle purchase-probability bounds and price-order rules.
result: The method returns feasible prices with a certified optimality-gap bound and solves synthetic instances with up to 500 products and few nests; projecting unconstrained prices onto the feasible set loses up to 32.60% of profit relative to direct constrained optimization.
conclusion: Jointly optimizing substitution structure and feasibility constraints is valuable, and the nest-level decomposition yields a tractable, certifiably near-optimal pricing method for constrained assortments.

title: A Smooth Equality Reformulation Of Nonlinear Exponential Cone Optimization
authors: Ellen H. Fukuda Huimin Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exponential cone optimization has received considerable attention in the modern literature, but studies involving nonlinear objective and constraint functions are still limited. This work can be seen as one of the first steps toward understanding nonlinear exponential cone optimization (NECO) problems. Here, we ask the question "Can smooth equality constraints replace nonlinear exponential cone constraints?". From a practical point of view, even squared slack reformulations in nonlinear programming introduce difficulties. However, such reformulations can be useful for studying optimality conditions. Motivated by this observation, in this work, we use a smooth surjective parameterization of the exponential cone to reformulate NECO as an equality-constrained nonlinear program (RNLP). We then analyze Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) and second-order optimality conditions for NECO through RNLP. Although feasibility is represented exactly, the KKT conditions for RNLP do not in general guarantee those for NECO. We characterize this correspondence through multiplier restrictions that are equivalent to a second-order condition involving only slack variables. We also establish an exact curvature identity showing that RNLP reproduces the sigma term of NECO without additional assumptions. Finally, we prove the relationships between second-order necessary and sufficient conditions for the two problems. We identify when RNLP can be used to rule out local minimizers of NECO or establish strict local optimality for NECO without explicitly evaluating the sigma term.
tldr: The paper reformulates nonlinear exponential cone optimization problems as equality-constrained nonlinear programs via a smooth surjective parameterization of the exponential cone, and analyzes KKT and second-order optimality conditions.
motivation: Studies of exponential cone optimization with nonlinear objective and constraint functions are scarce, and squared-slack reformulations in nonlinear programming are difficult in practice but potentially useful for studying optimality conditions.
method: The authors use a smooth surjective parameterization of the exponential cone to convert NECO into an equality-constrained nonlinear program (RNLP), then derive KKT multipliers and second-order conditions, including an exact curvature identity reproducing the sigma term.
result: KKT conditions for RNLP do not in general imply those of NECO; the correspondence is characterized by multiplier restrictions equivalent to a second-order condition on slack variables, and second-order necessary/sufficient conditions for the two problems are related.
conclusion: RNLP can rule out local minimizers or certify strict local optimality for NECO without explicitly evaluating the sigma term, offering a systematic route to optimality analysis in nonlinear exponential cone optimization.

title: Construction Of Dae Solver Rodas4PW And Numerical Test Examples With Rosenbrock And W-methods In OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock.jl
authors: Gerd Steinebach
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper compares various Rosenbrock and Rosenbrock W-methods. To achieve this, some methods implemented in the Julia package OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock.jl are selected and benchmarked using test examples. The test examples include stiff ODE problems as well as differential-algebraic equations. In addition to the already known methods, the new W-method Rodas4PW is introduced and included in the tests.
tldr: The paper benchmarks Rosenbrock and Rosenbrock W-methods in the Julia package OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock.jl and introduces a new W-method, Rodas4PW, for stiff ODEs and differential-algebraic equations.
motivation: Practitioners need reliable, well-tested stiff ODE and DAE integrators, and existing Rosenbrock-type methods vary in robustness and efficiency, motivating a comparative evaluation and a new solver.
method: Several methods already implemented in OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock.jl are selected and benchmarked on stiff ODE and DAE test problems, alongside the newly proposed Rodas4PW W-method.
result: Numerical test examples compare the accuracy and performance of the existing Rosenbrock and W-methods against the new Rodas4PW solver.
conclusion: The study provides practical guidance on choosing Rosenbrock-type solvers and offers Rodas4PW as an additional option, though it lies entirely outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems research.

title: ReplayAudit: Auditing Outsourced Llm Fine-Tuning Via Sealed Records And Selective Replay
authors: Yihan Xia, Wenxin Xu, Taotao Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Auditing outsourced LLM fine-tuning requires checking an untrusted provider's training while controlling verification cost. Uniform sampling ignores training-time signals, while checking a suspicious record can require replaying several preceding steps. We present ReplayAudit, a telemetry-guided auditing system that seals training records before challenges and independently replays sampled intervals from sealed checkpoints. Loss changes and parameter-update norms guide stratified random sampling; replay determines whether the selected computation agrees with its records. We relate sampling probabilities to replay work and evaluate the system on real LoRA training. A 7B BF16 prototype rejects a false update-norm report during a random audit; targeted checks also reject false loss reports and skipped updates. We calibrate sampling budgets offline to at least a 90% probability of directly selecting an injected step. For two learning-rate deviation settings, executing these budgets on the same honest 1.5B trajectory reduces median complete-audit wall time by 49% and 67% relative to uniform sampling. When skipped updates evade the high-anomaly stratum, the corresponding audit instead costs 38% more. These results show how deviation capture and actual replay work jointly determine the cost of telemetry-guided auditing.
tldr: ReplayAudit is a telemetry-guided auditing system that seals LLM fine-tuning training records and selectively replays sampled intervals from sealed checkpoints to verify an untrusted provider's work at reduced cost.
motivation: Outsourced LLM fine-tuning requires verification of the provider's training process, but uniform sampling ignores training-time signals and checking suspicious records can require replaying many preceding steps, making audits expensive.
method: The system seals training records before challenges and independently replays sampled intervals from sealed checkpoints, using loss changes and parameter-update norms to guide stratified random sampling, with sampling probabilities explicitly related to replay work.
result: A 7B BF16 prototype rejects false update-norm reports, false loss reports, and skipped updates; calibrated budgets achieve ≥90% probability of selecting an injected step and reduce median complete-audit wall time by 49% and 67% versus uniform sampling, though evasion of the high-anomaly stratum costs 38% more.
conclusion: The cost of telemetry-guided auditing is jointly determined by deviation capture and actual replay work, offering a practical cost-controlled approach to verifying outsourced LLM fine-tuning.

title: Contextual Search And Bilateral Trade With A Trace-Square-Root Potential
authors: Romain Cosson, Federico Fusco, Anupam Gupta, Stefano Leonardi, Renato Paes Leme, Matteo Russo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a unified potential method for contextual search and bilateral trade with one-bit feedback and obtain order-tight algorithms for both problems. Our framework starts from a Bayesian perspective in which the unknown target (for contextual search) and the unknown pair of valuations (for bilateral trade) are sampled from a known prior distribution. In that model, the decision maker bases its prediction on the posterior distribution, obtained by conditioning on feedback received in previous rounds. For Bayesian contextual search, we present an algorithm with a total loss bounded by [MATH], where [MATH] is the covariance matrix of the target's prior; and for contextual bilateral trade, our algorithm's regret is bounded by [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] are the covariance matrices of the seller's and buyer's valuations. We then use ideas from this Bayesian setting and adapt a ``dual'' of this trace-square-root potential to the classical worst-case setting, where the target and valuations are chosen adversarially from the unit Euclidean ball. For both contextual search and bilateral trade, we obtain tight [MATH]-regret algorithms. These results match the existing lower bounds up to a constant factor and improve on the previous guarantees of [MATH] for contextual search and of [MATH] for bilateral trade.
tldr: A unified trace-square-root potential method yields order-tight algorithms for Bayesian and worst-case contextual search and bilateral trade under one-bit feedback.
motivation: Contextual search and bilateral trade are fundamental online decision problems where matching known lower bounds with simple, unified techniques remained open.
method: The authors derive a Bayesian potential based on the covariance of the prior and adapt a dual trace-square-root potential to the adversarial setting with targets in the unit Euclidean ball.
result: They obtain loss and regret bounds scaling with the trace square root of the covariance matrices, matching existing lower bounds up to constants and improving prior guarantees.
conclusion: The framework unifies and tightens guarantees for both problems, providing tight sqrt-trace regret algorithms in both Bayesian and worst-case models.

title: MemoryDojo: Benchmarking Poisoning Through Llm Agent Memory
authors: David H. Yang, Blake Bullwinkel, Amanda Minnich, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Giorgio Severi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents benefit from using memory systems to improve performance on long-horizon, multi-session tasks. However, memory introduces a critical attack surface. Malicious instructions encountered in one session may be stored and propagated through memory before being retrieved and acted upon in later sessions. Because memory systems differ in how they process and retrieve information, the downstream effects of poisoning can vary significantly across systems. To quantify the effects of poisoning across different memory architectures, we introduce MemoryDojo, a benchmark for tracing the lifecycle of poisoned information through agent memory and measuring its influence on subsequent agent behavior. MemoryDojo is easily extensible, consists of 155 multi-session long-horizon trajectories covering four domains, and supports five different memory systems. Through our evaluation, we find that all memory systems are susceptible to memory poisoning, with substantial variation in downstream effects. We further propose a memory-aware poison optimization process that increases the poisoning efficacy, highlighting differences between memory architectures. We hope that MemoryDojo will support research on understanding and mitigating agentic memory risks.
tldr: MemoryDojo is a benchmark for tracing and quantifying poisoning attacks propagated through LLM agent memory systems across multi-session tasks.
motivation: LLM agents increasingly rely on memory for long-horizon tasks, creating an attack surface where malicious instructions stored in one session can affect later sessions, but the downstream impact across memory architectures is not well characterized.
method: The authors introduce a benchmark of 155 multi-session long-horizon trajectories across four domains, supporting five memory systems, and propose a memory-aware poison optimization process to compare poisoning efficacy across architectures.
result: All evaluated memory systems are found to be susceptible to memory poisoning, with substantial variation in downstream effects; the optimized poisoning process increases attack efficacy and highlights architectural differences.
conclusion: The work aims to support research on understanding and mitigating risks in agentic memory systems, but it does not address quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Branch-Extended Automatic Differentiation
authors: Jan H\"uckelheim, Jeffrey Larson, Matt Menickelly
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present branch-extended automatic differentiation (BEAD), a software package that provides information about inactive branches of piecewise-differentiable functions, intended for use in nonsmooth optimization algorithms. BEAD is implemented in Python, building on the popular JAX framework. For supported nonsmooth operations such as abs and max, BEAD identifies alternative branches within tolerance from the given input, and computes gradients of the resulting branches extended to the given input. Such information has been previously used for robust optimization methods, but has required error-prone and tedious manual differentiation, unlike BEAD, which is fully automated for functions written in NumPy-like JAX code. Our experiments show that our approach is as accurate as manually written derivative code, and offers more flexibility in modifying the function and choosing between branch-discovery rules. While we were originally motivated by the manifold sampling algorithm for nonsmooth composite objectives, we also integrate BEAD branch-extension gradients into a nonsmooth BFGS-SQP solver. On two small nonsmooth test problems, the resulting path-aware search resolves failures or substantially reduces the number of evaluations required by the BFGS-SQP solver.
tldr: BEAD is a JAX-based Python package that automatically computes branch-extension gradients for piecewise-differentiable functions, exposing information about inactive branches useful for nonsmooth optimization.
motivation: Robust nonsmooth optimization methods such as manifold sampling require gradients of inactive branches of functions involving abs, max, etc., but obtaining these has previously required tedious, error-prone manual differentiation.
method: The authors build on JAX to implement branch-extended automatic differentiation, which detects alternative branches within a tolerance of the input and automatically computes their extended gradients for NumPy-like JAX code, with configurable branch-discovery rules.
result: BEAD matches the accuracy of hand-written derivative code while offering greater flexibility; integrated into a nonsmooth BFGS-SQP solver, the path-aware search resolves failures or substantially reduces evaluation counts on two small test problems.
conclusion: BEAD automates a previously manual and fragile component of nonsmooth optimization workflows, providing a practical, flexible tool for robust derivative-based solvers.

title: Cantor's Onion: A Uniformly Quasiregular Map Whose Julia Set Is A Cantor Set Of Spheres
authors: Gaven J. Martin Alastair N. Fletcher
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For integers [MATH] with [MATH], we construct a uniformly quasiregular map of [MATH] of degree [MATH] whose Julia set is a Cantor set of concentric round spheres. To our knowledge, this is the first example of a uniformly quasiregular map in dimension three with infinitely many Fatou components. The map is a three-dimensional analogue of McMullen's maps [MATH], built from two Zorich-type power maps glued across a single shell by a slit construction. Its Julia set has Hausdorff dimension [MATH], where [MATH], and the restriction of the map to its Julia set is a skew product over the shift on two symbols and has topological entropy [MATH]. We also prove that uniformly quasiregular maps that expand uniformly near their Julia set, possibly with branching there, have no wandering domains and only finitely many periodic Fatou components, all of them attracting basins. The map constructed here belongs to this class.
tldr: The authors construct the first example of a uniformly quasiregular map in three dimensions whose Julia set is a Cantor set of concentric round spheres and whose Fatou set has infinitely many components.
motivation: Prior to this work no uniformly quasiregular map in dimension three with infinitely many Fatou components was known, and the class of such maps lacks concrete examples analogous to McMullen's planar maps.
method: The construction glues two Zorich-type power maps across a single shell using a slit construction, and the authors additionally prove a no-wandering-domains theorem for uniformly quasiregular maps that expand uniformly near their Julia set.
result: The resulting map has degree specified by the parameters, a Julia set of Cantor-sphere type with computable Hausdorff dimension, and acts on its Julia set as a skew product over the two-symbol shift with nontrivial topological entropy.
conclusion: The paper establishes existence of a new three-dimensional quasiregular dynamical example and identifies a broad class of such maps with only finitely many periodic Fatou components, all attracting basins.

title: Hausdorff Dimension Of Planar Box-like Self-affine Sets With Rotations
authors: Antti K\"aenm\"aki, R. D\'aniel Prokaj, K\'aroly Simon, Sascha Troscheit
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Hausdorff dimension of proximal planar self-affine sets whose defining maps have diagonal or anti-diagonal linear parts, with both types present. Such systems are irreducible but not strongly irreducible. Under a projective exponential separation condition, we show that the Hausdorff dimension equals the minimum of [MATH] and the affinity dimension, thereby extending the dimension formula of Hochman--Rapaport to all proximal irreducible planar systems. When the affinity dimension is at most an explicit threshold determined by the Lyapunov exponents, the formula holds assuming only that there are no exact overlaps. Above the threshold, it holds under the strong open set condition. These dimension formulae are proved by approximation with finite diagonal subsystems. Assuming projective exponential separation, we also determine the pointwise dimensions of the coordinate projections of the equilibrium state. Below the threshold, the projections are not exact-dimensional: the pointwise dimension of each exists almost everywhere and takes exactly two values, each on a set of positive measure. At or above the threshold, both projections are exact-dimensional with dimension one.
tldr: The paper studies Hausdorff dimension formulae for planar self-affine sets with diagonal and anti-diagonal linear parts under projective exponential separation.
motivation: The work aims to extend Hochman–Rapaport-type dimension formulae from strongly irreducible systems to all proximal irreducible planar box-like self-affine systems.
method: The authors use approximation by finite diagonal subsystems and analyze pointwise dimensions of coordinate projections of the equilibrium state under a projective exponential separation condition.
result: They show the Hausdorff dimension equals the minimum of an explicit quantity and the affinity dimension, with simplified assumptions below an explicit Lyapunov threshold; above it, the strong open set condition is required.
conclusion: The results provide a complete dimension formula for this class of planar self-affine sets and characterize when coordinate projections are exact-dimensional.

title: A Structure-preserving Discontinuous Galerkin Method For Variable-density Incompressible Flow With A Partitioned Time Integrator
authors: Zonghao Bai, Yinhua Xia, Yan Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Preserving density bounds and mass conservation, together with a conservative momentum discretization and exact incompressibility, is a central challenge in high-order simulations of variable-density incompressible flow. We develop a structure-preserving discontinuous Galerkin method that couples conservative density transport with an \(H()\)-conforming mixed discretization of the momentum equation. The method uses a partitioned time integrator: density is advanced explicitly by strong-stability-preserving Runge--Kutta stages with a bound-preserving limiter, while momentum is updated by a linearly implicit backward differentiation formula. The transport velocities are extrapolated from previously computed mixed velocities. Because the discrete solenoidal space is linear, this extrapolation preserves elementwise zero divergence and single-valued normal traces, providing compatible transport velocities without an auxiliary reconstruction or projection. For source-free transport on triangular meshes with impermeable or periodic boundaries, we prove bounds for density cell averages and limiter control-point values under the stated spatial, quadrature, and stagewise Courant--Friedrichs--Lewy conditions. The conservative fluxes and mean-preserving limiter yield global mass conservation. Numerical experiments on triangular and structured rectangular meshes demonstrate the expected convergence rates, machine-level divergence errors, and bound preservation, including in a low-density regime with high density ratio.
tldr: The paper develops a structure-preserving discontinuous Galerkin method for variable-density incompressible flow using a partitioned time integrator.
motivation: High-order simulation of variable-density incompressible flow requires simultaneous preservation of density bounds, mass conservation, conservative momentum discretization, and exact incompressibility.
method: The authors couple conservative density transport with an H(div)-conforming mixed discretization of momentum, advancing density explicitly via SSP Runge-Kutta with a bound-preserving limiter and momentum via a linearly implicit BDF scheme.
result: They prove density bounds and limiter control under suitable CFL and quadrature conditions, and numerical experiments show expected convergence rates, machine-level divergence errors, and bound preservation even at high density ratios.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a robust high-order structure-preserving approach for variable-density incompressible flow, though it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Conflux: Preventing Privilege Escalation With Principal Contexts And System-Level Evaluation
authors: Christian Schroeder de Witt Raya Buckley
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents combine information from multiple principals while acting externally. We formalise privilege escalation (PE) as the system-level security objective: an action may proceed only if every principal that influenced it would allow it. Model-level defences remain probabilistic, so enforcement must sit outside model judgement. We present Conflux, a principal-context defence. Its kernel, ITES, derives authority from provenance and the organisation's existing access-control system and intersects the permissions of every influencing principal. We prove a conditional authority-confinement theorem: under complete mediation, no-laundering provenance, a known non-empty decision context, fresh permission checks, and action binding, the kernel admits no action that escalates privilege with respect to any recorded influencing principal. The theorem covers the represented value-influence fragment; control influence from tool, branch, recipient, or plan-step selection remains a refinement obligation. Conflux extends the kernel with independent policy ports, argument-aware authorisation, disclosure, consent, delegation, restriction, and exposure planning. We describe two system- level evaluators. SLED is a black-box evaluator: it exhaustively explores a declared finite model of a defence up to a bound. SLED-V is a white-box evaluator: it checks a serialisable intermediate representation against security and provenance properties. The evidence is bounded and partial. The appendix reports retained AgentDojo, SLED, and SLED-V results, including the limits of those runs. No result in this paper is an unbounded deployment guarantee.
tldr: Conflux is a principal-context defence kernel (ITES) that prevents privilege escalation in LLM agents by intersecting the permissions of every principal that influenced an action, backed by a conditional authority-confinement theorem and two system-level evaluators (SLED, SLED-V).
motivation: LLM agents fuse information from multiple principals while acting externally, so model-level defences are only probabilistic and privilege escalation must be enforced outside model judgement at the system level.
method: The ITES kernel derives authority from provenance and existing access-control systems, intersecting permissions across all influencing principals; the authors prove a conditional authority-confinement theorem and add policy ports, argument-aware authorisation, disclosure, consent, delegation, and exposure planning, evaluated via black-box (SLED) and white-box (SLED-V) system-level evaluators.
result: Under assumptions of complete mediation, no-laundering provenance, known non-empty decision context, fresh permission checks, and action binding, the kernel admits no privilege-escalating action within the represented value-influence fragment, with bounded empirical results from AgentDojo, SLED, and SLED-V runs.
conclusion: The work provides formal, system-level guarantees against privilege escalation for LLM agents, though control influence and deployment-scale guarantees remain open refinement obligations and evidence is explicitly bounded and partial.
